## 2026-06-07 — M11 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment-workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) Plan phase, grounded in the current code at HEAD `8b5baa7` ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 11, Increment 3). This is the **headline** increment — `jigc describe` must **reflect the resolved cascade**, proven by a project override *visibly changing* the projection (not by "describe prints the list"). Four single-concern tasks, risk-first/serial: the project shadow-dir **substrate** first (the layer feed), then the **compose** read path routed through `file_owner`, then the **describe** read path routed through `file_owner`, then the **flow-14** e2e through the binary. No new fork surfaced; the design ([overrides.md](design/overrides.md) → Authored metadata on a definition resolves by whole-file shadow; [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 14; the M11-planning settle — whole-file shadow, **no field-merge**, `project > pack-default` only, team layer unfed) fully covers this cut. The deferred field-granular override stays parked with its trigger ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → Field-granular per-definition-metadata override).

Grounded facts (verified against the code, exercised against the M11-inc-3 *new shape*): (a) the describe read path is **pack-only today** — `describe::run` (`describe.rs:35`) requires the project layer only as the setup gate, then `load_workflow_defs`/`load_schemas` (`describe.rs:58,72`) read `pack.read(Workflows/Schemas)` directly with **no `file_owner` consult** and build **no `Resolved`**; the engine assembler `Description::assemble` (`introspect.rs:95`) is already **cascade-agnostic** (it consumes `(id, &WorkflowDef)` pairs + `&Schema` values), so the assembler does **not** change — the cascade work is entirely the CLI feed. (b) the live **compose** definition reads are likewise pack-only — `read_workflow` (`start.rs:1854`) and `all_schemas` (`start.rs:1182`) call `pack.read`/`pack.list` directly, bypassing `file_owner`; only *step* reads are layer-aware (`CascadeStepSource`, `start.rs:1326`, the faithful template this increment extends). (c) the cascade `files` surface is fed from `steps/` **only** — `load_project_layer` (`start.rs:1478`) calls `project_step_ids` (`start.rs:1593`, basenames of `<project_config>/steps/*.yaml`) and `shadow_file`s each; there is **no `workflows/`/`schemas/` enumeration**, so `file_owner("single-task")` is `None` today even though the pack ships that workflow (the pack-default layer is built with `files = Vec::new()` at every live resolve site — `start.rs:775,805`). (d) `cascade::resolve` builds **one** `file_owners: BTreeMap<String, LayerKind>` keyed by **bare id** (`cascade.rs:824`) shared across step/workflow/schema ids — a real **namespace hazard**: pack workflow ids and pack step ids are **disjoint today** (verified: no overlap; schema ids `adr`/`commit`/`prd`/`spec` also disjoint), but once `workflows/`/`schemas/` feed the map, a project workflow shadow and a project step shadow of the same id would collide on one key — so T1 must **prove** disjointness holds for the *real* shadow set and guard a same-id project workflow-vs-step collision rather than trust it. (e) the e2e harness pattern is proven — `config_fork_compose.rs` builds a throwaway git repo + `.jigc/config/` + writes a `steps/<id>.yaml` shadow and drives the binary; flow-14 mirrors it with a `workflows/single-task.yaml` shadow. The shipped `single-task.yaml` carries a real `usage:` (bare clause, post-`aedd991`), so the override edits a field that genuinely projects.

- **T1 — Substrate: feed the project `workflows/`/`schemas/` shadow dirs into the cascade `files` surface.** Extend `load_project_layer` (`start.rs`) to enumerate `<project_config>/workflows/<id>.yaml` and `<project_config>/schemas/<id>.yaml` basenames (two helpers mirroring `project_step_ids` — sorted, missing-dir → empty, never an error) and `shadow_file` each, so `cascade::Resolved::file_owner(<workflow-or-doctype-id>)` returns `Project` for an id the project ships. **Prove the namespace-disjointness assumption (fact (d)), do not trust it:** the red step asserts a project that shadows a **workflow** `single-task` resolves `file_owner("single-task") == Project` *and* that a project shadowing a **step** and a **workflow** of the same id is rejected with a routed `config.*-id-collision` finding (the `check_not_already_forked`/`check_basename_collision` precedent in `config.rs` — extend the collision guard across the shared keyspace, or prove the read path queries the right id so no real collision occurs; whichever the executor verifies, the test exercises a *same-id* project step+workflow shape, never disjoint inputs). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli` green with — a `workflows/single-task.yaml` project shadow yields `file_owner("single-task") == Project`; a `schemas/adr.yaml` shadow yields `file_owner("adr") == Project`; an unshadowed id stays pack-default/`None`; a same-id project step+workflow collision is a routed blocking finding (or proven impossible — the executor records which). *Why:* the layer feed is the substrate both read paths (T2/T3) consume; isolated and proven before any read routes through it (avoids the inert-substrate / dead-feature trap, hardening #2). *Design refs:* [overrides.md](design/overrides.md) → Authored metadata on a definition resolves by whole-file shadow (the project shadows a whole `workflows/<id>.yaml` / `schemas/<id>.yaml`); Native-file id = filename basename. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/start.rs`, `crates/cli/src/config.rs` (collision guard if extended).
- **T2 — Compose: route `read_workflow`/`all_schemas` through `file_owner` (whole-file shadow, no field-merge).** Make the live compose definition reads layer-aware — a faithful extension of `CascadeStepSource` (`start.rs:1326`): when `file_owner(<id>) == Project`, read `<project_config>/workflows/<id>.yaml` (resp. `schemas/<id>.yaml`); else read the pack body. **Whole-file replace, never a field-merge** — the project file wins entire (honoring [overrides.md](design/overrides.md)'s no-field-level-merge invariant). A project-owned-but-missing/malformed file is a clear path-bearing located fault, never a silent fall-through to the pack body (the `CascadeStepSource` located-error precedent). The reads need a `Resolved` + `project_config`; thread them in from the call sites that already hold the cascade (`compose_core`/the resume path — `start.rs:433,581,1058`). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli` green with a compose test exercising **both a context that shadows the workflow and one that omits it** (hardening #5 — composing a project `workflows/single-task.yaml` shadow changes the composed output vs the pack baseline; composing an *unshadowed* workflow stays byte-identical to pack-default), and a same-shape `schemas/` shadow exercised on a finalize/validate read of `all_schemas`. *Why:* the scope bullet names `read_workflow`/`all_schemas` explicitly — cascade reflection must hold on the *compose* read path, not only describe, or describe would reflect a cascade compose ignores (the two would drift); routed before describe because it is the more load-bearing consumer and shares the `file_owner` plumbing T3 reuses. *Design refs:* [overrides.md](design/overrides.md) → Authored metadata … resolves by whole-file shadow; Resolution algorithm phase 2 (by-id shadowing). *Files:* `crates/cli/src/start.rs`.
- **T3 — Describe: route the describe enumerator through `file_owner` so the projection reflects the cascade.** Make `describe::run` build the resolved cascade (`resolve_severity_cascade` / `load_project_layer`, already `pub(crate)`) and route `load_workflow_defs`/`load_schemas` through `file_owner` (reusing the T2 layer-aware read), so a project `workflows/<id>.yaml` / `schemas/<id>.yaml` shadow's prose wins for that one definition while every unshadowed definition still shows pack prose. The engine assembler is unchanged (it already consumes resolved `(id, def)` pairs). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli` green with a describe test asserting — with a project `workflows/single-task.yaml` shadow carrying edited `usage:`, the describe projection **contains the project prose and not the pack prose** for `single-task`, while another definition (e.g. `quick-fix`/`adr`) still shows its **pack** prose unchanged (the override *changed the output* — a "describe mentions single-task" assertion is rejected as masking); a both-fields-absent project shadow leaves that definition **not narrated** (skip-on-absent still holds through the cascade). *Why:* this is the headline read path — describe reflecting the resolved cascade; it rides the T1 substrate + the T2 layer-aware read, so it lands after both. *Design refs:* [overrides.md](design/overrides.md) → `describe` reading the resolved (shadowed) definitions is exactly what makes its output cascade-reflecting; [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 14 bar #1. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/describe.rs`.
- **T4 — e2e acceptance: flow 14 (the override walk) through the binary.** A throwaway-repo e2e (the `config_fork_compose.rs` harness pattern) authoring a project **`workflows/single-task.yaml`** whole-file shadow with an edited `usage:` over the **real shipped definitions** (not a renderer-shaped fixture pack — fixture-topology honesty, hardening #6), `project > pack-default` only (team layer unfed). Drives the built `jigc describe` binary and asserts: **(i) the override walk** — output **contains the project `usage` prose and not the pack `usage` prose** for `single-task`, and an **unshadowed** definition's pack prose is **unchanged** (assert the diff against the pre-override baseline output — the override *changed the output*; over a **workflow** here, never a command-ref — `hint` is pack-only and **not** asserted as cascade-reflecting); **(ii) the non-contractual format predicate** holds on the **real overridden** output (reuse the inc-2 predicate — not-JSON / not-top-level-YAML-mapping-or-sequence / no key-shaped line / no bullet row / no per-definition extractable key / prose-density); **(iii)** the authored project string appears verbatim (assembled, not generated — no LLM call). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli` green for the new `crates/cli/tests/flow14_acceptance.rs`; a manual `jigc describe` against a shadowed repo shows the project prose. *Why:* the milestone's headline acceptance — proves cascade-reflection end-to-end through the binary, the one path that converts "describe reflects the cascade" from supported to proven. *Design refs:* [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 14 (all bars; the override-proof shadows a workflow/doctype, never a command-ref; team unfed); [introspection.md](design/introspection.md). *Files:* `crates/cli/tests/flow14_acceptance.rs` (new).

*Scope-bullet coverage:* Grouped-scope bullet 1 (CLI/engine — new project `workflows/`/`schemas/` shadow dirs + route `read_workflow`/`all_schemas`/the describe enumerator through `file_owner`, whole-file replace no field-merge) → **T1** (the shadow-dir `files` feed) + **T2** (`read_workflow`/`all_schemas` routing) + **T3** (the describe enumerator routing) — the three named reads each map to a task; bullet 2 (e2e flow 14 — the override walk over real definitions, the non-contractual predicate on the real output, `project > pack-default` only) → **T4**. No bullet deferred; the namespace-collision hazard (fact (d)) is delivered as a T1 red-step *assumption to prove*, not trusted; field-granular override stays parked with its trigger. Nothing creeps beyond the increment — the engine assembler is untouched (already cascade-agnostic); command-ref `hint` stays pack-only (not asserted cascade-reflecting, per the M11 settle); the team layer stays unfed.

- **T1 landed.** `load_project_layer` now feeds all three project definition dirs into the cascade `files` surface: `project_step_ids` refactored onto a shared `project_native_ids(subdir)` lister, plus net-new `project_workflow_ids` / `project_schema_ids` (sorted, missing-dir → empty, never error); a new `shadowed_definition_ids` merges the three sets and `shadow_file`s each, so `file_owner("single-task"|"adr") == Project` for a project `workflows/`/`schemas/` shadow. **Namespace hazard — guarded, NOT proven-impossible (the executor's recorded choice):** the shared `file_owners` keyspace (cascade.rs:824) *can* collide via a human-authored same-bare-id shadow in two dirs (e.g. `steps/foo.yaml` + `workflows/foo.yaml`), so `shadowed_definition_ids` rejects it up front with a routed blocking `config.shadow-id-collision` `Finding` (one id, one file) — pack ids stay disjoint today but the project dirs are out of pack control, so the guard is real, not theatre. ## 2026-06-07 — M11 (describe / introspection) shipped

Built end-to-end via the [milestone-build](implementation/milestone-build) harness across the three planned risk-first increments + the [milestone-completion audit](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md). **`jigc describe` is a cascade-reflecting, non-contractual prose self-description surface** — the document model applied to jigc describing itself ([introspection.md](design/introspection.md); [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 11 status).

**Against the M11 win condition (the planning lens):** ✅ the milestone's **two load-bearing proofs both hold, through the real binary** — (1) *non-contractual enforced by format, both directions*: agent output is not JSON / parses only as a bare YAML scalar / no key-lines/bullets/per-definition-extractable-field / prose-density floor, **and** `--format json` of the same data IS a structured catalog (so the property is real, not vacuous — the #1 watch-item, the M10 "contract satisfied, not waived" analogue, nailed); (2) *cascade-reflection by a visible change*: a project whole-file shadow of a workflow **and** a doctype makes project prose win and the pack prose for that definition vanish, unshadowed defs keep pack prose, **no field-merge** (dropped field doesn't fall back) + **skip-on-absent**, byte-identical across runs and across divergent shadow-creation orders — not a "describe mentions X" masking assertion. ✅ **0 design halts** (the four open-thread forks settled at plan-time held; build-health trend M9=0 · M10=0 · M11=0). ✅ Scope honesty: command-ref `hint` stays honestly **pack-only** (disclosed, the M4 unwired-resolver shape named openly), the cut stretch (data-value roots, field-granular override, left-behind pointers) stayed cut, the two fields are load-bearing (woven), prose authored on all 9 workflows + 4 doctypes. The only in-build remediation was increment 2's 1 fix round — the build's own validation caught + de-masked a "doubled-lead" weave defect (pack `usage:` colliding with the weave template).

**Audit → 2 findings, both LOW, human-triaged fix-now, both remediated + re-verified** (`8220fd6`):
- **LOW** — the weave assumed the authored `description:` ends in a period; a period-less string would run on into "Reach for it when". De-fragilized (strip one trailing period, rejoin with ". ") — **byte-identical** for the current period-ending pack prose, fixed for period-less input. Authoring-fragility, not a shipped defect.
- **LOW** — stale `jigc describe --help` ("pack-only in M11 (cascade reflection is a later increment)") after increment 3 shipped cascade reflection → corrected to describe cascade reflection. The **agent-facing-honesty class** (cf. the M9 `ingest --help` fix; an agent reads `--help` to decide behaviour).

**Harness fold-backs (post-run reflection, all domain-agnostic):**
- **Settle — "question the docs you lean on"** (already folded during planning above): a pre-existing locked doc you build *around* is a claim too; friction is signal to elaborate / revise-a-design-doc / revise-VISION(special-case), not to bend.
- **Scope — the roadmap's *forward*-difficulty framing is a claim** ([milestone-planning-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md) → Scope): a "design-locked / planning-light / trivial-addition" entry should *raise* baseline-audit intensity, not relax it (M10's "add the impl" and M11's "planning light" were both overturned by the spike). Second instance → widens the existing "don't trust roadmap optimism" caution from *shipped* (backward) to *difficulty* (forward).
- **Completion — fix-now by default, narrow human gate** ([milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) → Plan/triage): context is freshest at completion, so a confirmed audit finding is fixed immediately via the dev-workflow gate (mirrors the build phase auto-executing); the human gate fires only for *too-big* (→ its own task/increment) and *contested* (→ would revise a settled decision / change intended behavior — the same discipline as the Settle fold). Validated by this very session — the 2 LOW findings were obvious fix-nows that the old gate ceremony-taxed.
- **`milestone-build.js` — report the milestone it actually built**: the result reported `"the next milestone"` / `base:null` because `args` arrived empty and the auto-resolved id was never captured; the `milestone-reader` now returns the canonical id (`INCREMENTS_SCHEMA.milestone`) and the result/messages echo it (harness reporting-honesty).

The post-spine arc continues: **M12 self-hosting** next (the harness these folds live in is M12's distill target — incl. the new "treat the roadmap's difficulty framing as a claim," which sorts onto the judgment-stays-the-agent's side of the determinism cut).

## 2026-06-07 — M12 planning (self-hosting): de-parked, four forks settled, bounded to a reduced-linear dev-workflow encode

Planned via `/milestone-plan M12` (scope → 4 `capability-auditor`s → 4 `gap-detector`s → settle → review → decompose). **The exercised baseline turned M12's "exploratory / dialect-surface-discovered-by-encoding" framing from a hedge into a measured fact** — and, surprisingly, *in M12's favour for the bounded slice*: the **dev-workflow proper is flat, single-pass linear** (the bounded fix-loop / hard halts / conditionals the roadmap feared live in the *increment-workflow wrapper*, not the dev-workflow), so a **reduced-linear encode runs end-to-end today with zero dialect extension** — spiked against the real binary on a fresh **non-Rust** repo (composes deterministically + `setup → start → finalize → one git commit`, git-only). Design de-parked from `ideas/self-hosting.md` → [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) (the M11 `describe`→`introspection.md` precedent; idea file removed, live pointers repointed, wired into the reading order as the terminus).

**The four planning forks, settled (all human-gated):**
- **Encode scope → reduced-linear only.** Encode the flat prose spine; **name** the degradations (test-first ordering + the mechanized gate ride as un-enforced prose) as the dialect-extension milestone's triggers, don't build them. **Zero engine/dialect code in M12** — pure pack authoring + design + dogfood.
- **Subsume vs thin → subsume.** Baseline killed "thin": any `creates-task: true` pack must vendor a `commit` schema (finalize hardcodes `COMMIT_TYPE`) + reproduce the full intrinsic-knob severity surface floored at blocking — a truly-thin pack needs engine changes M12 won't make. The methodology pack **vendors** the dev surfaces and composes **alone** (the M14 circularity broken: M12 must not need M14's multi-pack composition to run).
- **Success bar → composition-fidelity + qualitative judgment check.** The headline ("matches/beats the build-health trend") has **no runnable home** — the halt/fix-round tally lives in the external `milestone-build.js` harness, not the binary or pack — so the quantitative comparison is **deferred** (building measurement scaffolding would balloon the bounded slice). The bar is: the pack composes the dev-workflow deterministically + runs a real task end-to-end through the binary, the judgment slots stay agent-authored (not hollowed), and the prose-washed mechanizables are named (not silently dropped).
- **Dogfood target → `gherrink-galey`** (a TypeScript pnpm monorepo — genuinely unlike jigc, so jigc-shaped gates can't flatter it; has planned-but-unbuilt work = a real dev task); `gherrink-lacon` (Rust) the fallback. **Constraint: never touch the original — run on a `/tmp` copy.** Because the slice is reduced-linear (gate-as-prose, `doc-code` probe gated off since the pack ships no `code-anchor`), the unlike-jigc choice costs nothing and buys the honest portability test.

**The honesty knife-edge (the acceptance bar, recorded so the build can't blunt it):** M12 fails at **either** edge — *hollowing a judgment slot* (gap-detection/design-review/settle → a checklist probe) **or** *prose-washing a mechanizable structure* (handing the dev-workflow's test-first **ordering** — which is structure, not judgment — back to the agent as prose and calling it faithful). The reduced encode rides the second risk deliberately and **defuses it by naming**, not by pretending. **Graduated:** the M12-keyed `(D)` workflow-progress/resumption primitive — defers cleanly under reduced-linear (restart-from-scratch holds), named as dialect-extension trigger #4 (out of [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)). **The expected outcome stands:** M12 surfaces a dedicated workflow-dialect-extension milestone (the five named triggers: test-first ordering gate · structural human-gate · portable gate-command knob · bounded fix-loop + resumption · owner-artifact gate) — an honest result, not a failure.

## 2026-06-07 — M12 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment-workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) Plan phase, grounded in the current code ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 12, Increment 1; [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → the dev-workflow sort + Verified friction; [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 15). **Pure pack authoring + tests — zero `crates/*/src` changes** (the Deliverable's hard constraint; the executor's final gate must confirm the diff touches no `crates/*/src`). Four single-concern tasks, risk-first/serial: the cascade-config substrate first (the verified-friction enum-rewrite trap — a verbatim `knobs.yaml` copy fails `no workflow 'router'`), then the workflow + four prose steps (the lone-line-placeholder + four-command-ref-finalize traps), then the determinism + orientation tests through the real binary, then the honesty artifact. **The verified-friction facts in [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) are spike-verified but illustrative in notation — every one is re-proven as a red step against the binary here, not trusted as a pin** (the M3 "mirrors `adr`" / "zero engine change" lesson): each pack-authoring task's done-criterion is an *observable binary check* (a compose that resolves, a finalize that lands one commit), so a prose-washed friction fact that is subtly wrong fails loudly. Grounded facts verified on disk at HEAD `8929f7d`: (a) the embedded `knobs.yaml` hardcodes `default-workflow: { of: [router, single-task, quick-fix, plan, implement-from-spec], default: router }` and the enum **constrains** the cascade value, so the methodology copy must rewrite `of:`/`default:` to `[dev-task]`/`dev-task`; (b) `pack_field_types` treats an absent `config/field-types.yaml` as the empty set (no error) — the methodology pack ships **no** `field-types.yaml` and **no** `probes/` (no `code-anchor`, the `doc-code` probe gated off, [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) Open threads); (c) `pack-id` lives in `defaults.yaml` (not a knob), and a `pack-id` declared in `knobs.yaml` is rejected; (d) the commit schema requires `type` (enum) + `scope` (string, rejected empty) **non-empty** and `summary`/`body` are slots, so finalize *renders* an already-filled doc — the agent must `set-field type/scope --value` + `set-slot summary/body --from-file -` first; (e) `doc set-field <addr> --value <v>` and `doc set-slot <addr> --from-file -` are the two distinct verbs (`cli.rs`), addressable via the `{from: "task.commit#<field>"}` command-ref arg form (mirroring the embedded `set-commit-summary`); (f) a `{{…}}` placeholder resolves **only as the entire trimmed line** (inline emits literally — the M4 flow-3a class), so every authored placeholder is its own line; (g) `compose_in_repo` builds the selectable `catalog` from `creates-task: true` workflows and a selectable workflow missing a `when` hint is a hard error — `dev-task` must carry `when`. No new fork surfaced; the four settled forks (reduced-linear · subsume · composition-fidelity bar · `gherrink-galey` dogfood) + the locked design fully cover this cut. The dogfood-on-a-real-project half is **increment 2** (named in T3's notes — the throwaway-repo tests here are the controlled-repo proof *before* the foreign-project run, never a substitute).

- **T1 — Pack substrate: the methodology pack's cascade config + vendored commit schema (the enum-rewrite trap).** Author `packs/methodology/config/defaults.yaml` (`pack-id: methodology`, `default-workflow: dev-task`), `config/knobs.yaml` **copied from the embedded `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml` and edited** — the `default-workflow` enum rewritten to `of: [dev-task]` / `default: dev-task`, the full intrinsic-check severity surface (every `floor: blocking` row) kept verbatim — `config/commands.yaml` with the command-refs the steps use (`finalize-task` + the four commit-fill refs T2 wires), and `schemas/commit.yaml` **vendored** byte-faithfully from the embedded `commit` schema (finalize hardcodes `COMMIT_TYPE="commit"`). **No `field-types.yaml`, no `probes/`** (fact (b)). The pack lives at a build-chosen path the tests point `JIGC_PACK_DIR` at (the `pack_source_determinism.rs` `copy_tree` precedent — doc-elaboration pin: the executor picks the on-disk home, e.g. `crates/cli/tests/packs/methodology/` or a tmp build, recording which). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli` green with a throwaway-repo test (the `pack_source_determinism.rs` harness) that `JIGC_PACK_DIR=<methodology-pack> jigc setup` then `jigc start` (no intent) exits 0 and renders the `Pack: methodology/...` provenance label — proving the pack **loads as the sole pack** (the enum rewrite is correct: a verbatim `router`-defaulted copy would fail `no workflow 'router'` here, so this is the trap's red step) — *and* a same-shape run with the enum left as `router` is asserted to **fail** (the trap proven, not assumed). At T1 the workflow/steps don't exist yet, so `start "<intent>"` is **not** yet asserted to compose — that lands in T2. *Why:* the cascade-config substrate every later task rides; its enum-rewrite + knob-floor trap is the verified-friction headline, isolated and proven before any workflow composes over it (the inert-substrate trap, hardening #2). *Design refs:* [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → Settled forks (subsume; the knob-enum build note), Verified friction; [overrides.md](design/overrides.md) → Scalar knobs. *Files:* `packs/methodology/config/{defaults,knobs,commands}.yaml`, `packs/methodology/schemas/commit.yaml` (new), `crates/cli/tests/` (the load test).

`implement` = write-the-failing-test-FIRST → confirm-it-fails-for-the-right-reason → minimal green → refactor, **all agent-self-policed prose** (no ordering gate — the named trigger, not built); `gate` = "run your project's configured test + lint + build gate; all pass or the task isn't done" as **portable prose, no hardcoded `cargo`**; `finalize` wires a command-ref **each** for `set-field type` + `set-field scope` (`--value`, `{agent: ...}` arg) + `set-slot summary` + `set-slot body` (`--from-file -`) **then** `{{ cli.finalize-task }}` — four fill refs, not one (fact (d)/(e)). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli` green with a throwaway-repo test that `JIGC_PACK_DIR=<pack> jigc setup` then `jigc start "<a real intent>"` exits 0, **composes the `dev-task` flat spine** (the four step bodies present in order), and **resolves `{{task.intent}}`** to the literal intent on its own line (assert the resolved intent string appears, not the literal `{{task.intent}}`); and a finalize-reachability check — the four emitted commit-fill `Run:` lines + the `finalize-task` line render verbatim with the addresses resolved (the emitted-bytes contract, hardening #4 — assert on the emitted lines, do not reconstruct). *Why:* the workflow + steps are the encode itself; the lone-line + four-ref-finalize friction facts are the two traps the spike flagged, each proven by a compose that resolves rather than a trusted pin. *Design refs:* [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → The dev-workflow sort (the per-step table), Verified friction (lone-line, four command-refs); [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 15 setup block. *Files:* `packs/methodology/workflows/dev-task.yaml`, `packs/methodology/steps/{scope,implement,gate,finalize}.yaml` (new), `crates/cli/tests/` (the compose test).
- **T3 — Tests: byte-identical recompose determinism + orientation surfaces the methodology workflow.** A throwaway-repo e2e (the `pack_source_determinism.rs` harness pattern) over the methodology pack: capture the stdout of the **original successful** `jigc start "<intent>"` (the mint), then `jigc start --task <id>` and assert the recompose is **byte-identical** to that capture (fact: re-minting the same intent fails "already active" — diff against the *mint's* successful stdout, never a re-mint's error output, [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) Verified friction); and an orientation assertion — bare `jigc start` (no intent) lists the methodology pack's **`dev-task`** workflow with its `when` hint (the pack's `default-workflow: dev-task` means bare-start orients, not mints). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli` green: the `--task` recompose stdout equals the mint stdout byte-for-byte; bare `jigc start` orientation output contains `dev-task` + its `when` hint and the `Pack: methodology/...` label. *Why:* the Deliverable's **deterministic, byte-identical-on-recompose** clause + the orient-shows-the-pack clause — the determinism bar proven by re-execution (hardening #7: same logical input → byte-identical), not by inspecting one run. **The real-project (`gherrink-galey`) dogfood walk is increment 2** — these throwaway-repo tests are the controlled-repo proof that must hold before that foreign-project run. *Design refs:* [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M12 Inc 1 Tests bullet; [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → Determinism via `--task` recompose; [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 15 bar #1. *Files:* `crates/cli/tests/` (the determinism + orientation test).
- **T4 — Honesty artifact: the three-way sort table + named-trigger list match the *authored* steps (the falsifiable check).** A check (test or a `DECISIONS`-recorded executor verification, the executor records which form) confirming the [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) dev-workflow sort table + named-trigger list describe **what T2 actually authored** — every judgment step (scope-restatement, test-first discipline, gate) is **agent-authored prose** (no `gap-count`/checklist lint, no hardcoded `cargo` in `gate` — bar #2 FAIL exemplar (a) absent), and every prose-washed mechanizable (the test-first ordering in `implement`, the gate command in `gate`) **appears in the named-trigger list** (bar #2 FAIL exemplar (b) absent — prose-washed-without-naming). If the authored steps diverge from the table (e.g. a step mechanizes a judgment, or a prose-wash is un-named), this is a **blocking** finding to reconcile — either the encode or the table is corrected, never left divergent. *Done:* the falsifiable check passes: a grep/assertion (or recorded manual confirmation) that `gate.yaml` contains no `cargo`/`pnpm`-hardcoded gate command and `implement.yaml` carries no ordering-enforcement structure (pure prose), cross-checked against the trigger list naming test-first-ordering + gate-command; the executor records the form + result. *Why:* the Deliverable's "the encode's honesty is part of the deliverable" clause + the milestone's both-ways acceptance bar (hollowing OR un-named prose-wash both fail) — the one task that proves the encode is honest, not just that it composes. *Design refs:* [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → The honest caveat (the acceptance bar), The three-way determinism cut, The named dialect-extension trigger; [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M12 Inc 1 Honesty-artifact bullet. *Files:* `crates/cli/tests/` or a `DECISIONS.md` verification note (executor's recorded choice); the authored `packs/methodology/steps/*.yaml`.

Falsifiability verified by transient injection: hardcoding `cargo` in `gate`, stripping the enforcement-tell from `implement`, and un-naming either trigger in the doc each turn the test red.

## 2026-06-07 — M12 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment-workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) Plan phase, grounded in the current code + the real foreign repo ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 12, Increment 2; [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → The dogfood acceptance flow + What "done/good" looks like; [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 15). **Still pure pack data + tests — zero `crates/*/src` changes** (the milestone-wide hard constraint; the validator's mandatory check, hardening rule that a quiet `crates/*/src` touch fails the milestone). Increment 1 shipped + is verified (commits `03e6569`/`67c8e42`/`8f4707d`/`f69e037`; the methodology pack lives at `packs/methodology/`); this increment is the **integration proof** — the same encode driven on a real, unlike-jigc project (`gherrink-galey`, a TypeScript pnpm monorepo) rather than the controlled throwaway repo. **The cut's load-bearing structural fact (grounded against the real binary + the real repo at planning, HEAD `8929f7d`):** flow 15's deliverable is *"the agent does the TS work"* — writes a failing vitest test, implements, runs `pnpm test`/`biome` **by hand** (the prose gate), then fills the commit doc — so the dogfood is **two honestly-different halves**, and conflating them is the trap to avoid. **Half A (automatable, a `cargo test` regression gate): the deterministic CLI walk** — setup → compose → byte-identical recompose → the four fill verbs → finalize-lands-exactly-one-code-only-commit, over a `/tmp` copy, driven through the binary with *fixed inputs* (a stand-in code edit, not genuine agent judgment). This half a headless executor/validator subagent **can** run and re-run. **Half B (NOT a `cargo test` — the M8 "owner-assigned recorded artifact" / bucket-3 shape recursing onto M12, [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → three-way cut #3): the genuine live-agent dogfood** — a real agent exercising the *judgment* slots (scope-restatement, test-first discipline, running the project's own gate) on the live foreign project, where real TS prose + real `pnpm test`/`biome` runs are the proof "the judgment slots are genuinely exercised on a **live** run (not just by inspection)" (success-bar #2's *live* clause). By the determinism boundary a headless subagent can no more author genuine TS judgment than it can spawn the Task tool, so Half B is a **recorded, orchestrator/human-driven milestone-completion artifact**, not an increment-loop `cargo test` — the direct analogue of flow 10's Half-B genuine-spawn artifact ([milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) → step 1's orchestrator-driven artifact; the **hollow-dogfood trap**: passing off Half A's fixed-input CLI walk *as* the genuine-agent proof, the sibling of the hollow-spawn trap). The build-health record (bullet 2) is observational + rides on the live Half-B run. **Grounded facts verified at planning (against `target/debug/jigc` + a `/tmp` copy of the real `gherrink-galey`):** (a) `gherrink-galey` is a real TypeScript **pnpm monorepo** (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `packages/{core,react,vue,vanilla,pm,…}`, `vitest` + `@biomejs/biome` in `package.json`, a git repo, a `.planning/` roadmap carrying planned-but-unbuilt work) — genuinely unlike jigc, the portability target; (b) `JIGC_PACK_DIR=<methodology> jigc setup` succeeds **on the real repo** (installs the adapter artifacts), `jigc start "<intent>"` composes the flat `scope → implement → gate → finalize` spine with `{{task.intent}}` resolved on its own line + the four commit-fill `Run:` lines + the `finalize-task` line all rendered verbatim with the minted slug resolved, and `start --task <id>` recompose is **byte-identical** to the mint capture — all reproduced live at planning; (c) **a real friction the toy-repo spike did not surface** (exactly the "portability gap" bullet 2 asks to capture, recorded here so the executor expects it): the `/tmp` copy is **not clean** — the working tree carries pre-existing uncommitted edits, and `node_modules` is ~1.5 GB, so a faithful "exactly **one** code-only commit" requires the executor to **establish a clean baseline first** (commit/stash the pre-existing dirt **before** `jigc setup`, and sequence the `setup` commit ahead of the work commit, per flow 15) and to choose a copy strategy that still lets `pnpm test`/`biome` run (a naive `cp -r` is heavy but `pnpm test` needs `node_modules`) — a doc-elaboration pin the executor records (how the clean baseline + copy are established), not a fork; (d) the original `gherrink-galey` is **never modified** — the run is on the `/tmp` copy (verified: the planning probe touched only the copy; the original's working-tree dirt is pre-existing, not planning-induced) — the validator asserts the original's HEAD + tree are unchanged by the run. No new fork surfaced: the four settled forks (reduced-linear · subsume · composition-fidelity bar · `gherrink-galey` dogfood) + flow 15 + the locked design fully cover this cut; the Half-A/Half-B split is *applying* the milestone's own settled three-way cut (bucket 3) + the existing completion-artifact mechanism, not a new decision.

- **T1 — Half A: the deterministic dogfood CLI walk as a `cargo test` e2e on a `/tmp` copy of `gherrink-galey` (the automatable regression gate).** A throwaway-copy e2e (the `pack_source_determinism.rs` / `flow10_acceptance.rs` harness pattern) that, against the real binary over a **clean-baseline `/tmp` copy** of `gherrink-galey` with `JIGC_PACK_DIR=<methodology>`: runs `jigc setup`, commits the setup artifacts, `jigc start "<intent>"` mints + composes the flat spine, captures the mint stdout and asserts `start --task <id>` recompose is **byte-identical**, makes a *fixed stand-in* code edit (TS file — standing in for the agent's work, the determinism half not the judgment half), runs the four fill verbs (`doc set-field type/scope --value`, `doc set-slot summary/body --from-file -`), then `jigc task finalize <id>` and asserts **exactly one new git commit** lands, **code-only** (the commit diff carries the stand-in code edit, *not* `.jigc/tasks/`), **git-only** (no `cargo`/`rustc` invoked — the finalize path is stack-free on a non-Rust project), and the **original `gherrink-galey` HEAD + tree are unchanged**. ## 2026-06-07 — M12 Increment 2 / T2 shipped: the genuine live-agent dogfood — the recorded milestone-completion artifact (flow 15 integration proof)

**T2 — Half B: the genuine live-agent dogfood ran end-to-end on a `/tmp` copy of the real `gherrink-galey`; the six-part bar witnessed live; build-health recorded.** This is the **recorded milestone-completion artifact** (the bucket-3 owner-assigned-artifact half of the flow-15 split, [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → three-way cut #3; the direct analogue of flow 10's Half-B genuine-spawn proof) — produced by a real agent doing genuine TypeScript judgment, **not** an increment-loop `cargo test` (a headless subagent can no more author genuine TS judgment than spawn the Task tool). The transcript *is* the artifact; this entry records its outcome and the landed commit. **The milestone is shippable on this** (its absence was a blocking completion finding per [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) → step 1; T1's fixed-input walk was never a substitute — the hollow-dogfood trap).

The walk, on a `/tmp/jigc-m12-dogfood/galey` copy of `gherrink-galey` (rsync excluding `.git`; **`node_modules` copied this time** — Half B's hand-run `pnpm test`/`biome` gate genuinely needs it, unlike Half A's finalize-only walk; pnpm's relative `.pnpm`-store symlinks survive a `cp -a`, so the copied tree's toolchain resolves), with the methodology pack as the sole `JIGC_PACK_DIR` and an isolated `$HOME`:
- **Real planned-but-unbuilt task** (from galey's own i18n module, a genuine latent bug): `mergeMessages` did an **exact** `cat[locale]` lookup while `resolveLocale("en-US")` keeps the region subtag — so an `'en'`-keyed catalog never merges under locale `'en-US'` and every message silently degrades to its messageId. The fix: `mergeMessages` falls back to the locale **primary subtag** (`en-US` → `en`) when the exact bundle is absent; exact still wins.
- **Setup → commit setup → start**: `jigc setup` installed the adapter (appended to galey's pre-existing `CLAUDE.md`, wrote `.jigc/` + `.claude/`), committed ahead of the work commit (`chore: jigc setup`). `jigc start "<intent>"` composed the flat `scope → implement → gate → finalize` dev-task spine with `{{task.intent}}` resolved and all four commit-fill `Run:` lines + the `finalize` line addressed to the minted slug `mergemessages-falls-back-to-a-locale-primary`; `start --task <id>` recompose was **byte-identical** to the mint capture (and stable across repeats).
- **Genuine TS work, judgment slots live**: wrote a failing **vitest** test first and **observed it fail for the right reason** (`AssertionError: expected {} to deeply equal { 'a.b': 'ext-en', 'c.d': 'app-en' }` — the genuine assertion, not a compile error); added a guard test that an exact region bundle wins over the fallback (green before impl, proving the precedence isn't broken); implemented the minimal `bundleForLocale` helper; re-ran → 14/14 green.
- **Hand-run gate (the prose step, genuinely exercised)**: ran galey's own gate by hand — `biome check` **caught real format drift** (line-length on the new test lines), fixed via `biome check --write`; `tsc --noEmit` clean; the **full** core vitest suite **235/235** green.
- **Fill + finalize**: the four fill verbs (`set-field type=feat / scope=i18n`, `set-slot summary/body --from-file -`), then `jigc task finalize` landed **exactly one** new commit (2→3) whose message *is* the rendered commit doc (`feat(i18n): fall back to the locale primary subtag in mergeMessages` + body), carrying only the two genuine TS files + jigc's `.jigc/.gitignore` bookkeeping — **no `.jigc/tasks/` scratch** (the task working area was removed at finalize), **git-only** (no `cargo`/`rustc` in finalize output, a non-Rust project).

**The six-part bar, witnessed on the live run:** (1) composition fidelity — a real task ran through to one commit on a non-Rust project, byte-identical recompose; (2) **judgment slots genuinely exercised, not by inspection** — the vitest test was *observed* failing then passing, the hand-run gate caught + fixed real drift (the part T1's fixed-input walk structurally cannot prove); (3) pack composed **alone** + pure pack data — the **M12 diff (`8929f7d..HEAD`) touches no `crates/*/src`** (only `packs/methodology`, tests, docs); (4) M13 seam holds — galey's `.planning/` working docs stayed plain markdown, no managed methodology doctype, the only managed write was the `commit` doctype → git message; (5) `doc-code` probe gated off — no `code-anchor` in the pack, never fired on the TS project; (6) the real unlike-jigc project **never modified** — the original `gherrink-galey` HEAD (`4147a36…`) + porcelain-status hash were byte-identical before and after (the whole run was on the `/tmp` copy).

**Observational build-health record (bullet 2; qualitative — the quantitative tally stays deferred, no runnable home on a foreign dogfood):** the live run had **zero halts** and **zero fix-rounds** — one clean pass through scope → red → green → gate → finalize. One genuine in-loop gate catch (biome format drift, fixed in seconds by `--write`), which is the gate doing its job, not a fix-round. **Portability gaps the toy-repo spike did not surface:** (a) the **node_modules copy strategy** — Half A could skip the ~1.4 GB `node_modules` because finalize never shells out, but Half B's *agent gate* needs it; a `cp -a` works only because pnpm's store symlinks are relative (a naive content-addressed-store assumption could have broken cross-tree); (b) **`jigc setup` appends to a pre-existing `CLAUDE.md`** rather than creating one (galey ships its own) — benign here (committed in the setup commit, ahead of the work commit) but a real foreign-repo interaction the clean toy repo never exercised; (c) the toy-spike-noted **pre-existing working-tree dirt + heavy `node_modules`** (the clean-baseline requirement) held exactly as anticipated. No portability gap blocked the run; jigc ran the reduced-linear slice of its own dev-workflow on a fresh foreign TypeScript codebase to one clean code-only commit.
