## 2026-06-07 — M13 planning: arch-doc earns its driver (half #1); methodology-doc graduation (half #2) deferred

M13 (doctype & surface completion) planned via [/milestone-plan](.claude/commands/milestone-plan.md) (scope → baseline audit → detect gaps → settle → review → decompose). Four `capability-auditor` subagents established the baseline by exercising the real binary; four `gap-detector` subagents + a design spike reshaped the design. The done-picture is recorded in [architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md) (new design doc, slotted into the reading order after `finalize`).

**The central judgment — half #2 defers, M13 = half #1 only.** M12's dogfood earned **zero** methodology doctypes (the dev-workflow only *reads* docs at fixed paths; the promote-a-doctype escape hatch did not fire). The workflows that would *author* the methodology's working docs (roadmap / deferral-ledger / decisions-log) are the **planning and completion workflows** — not encoded, and encoding them *is* the surfaced dialect-extension milestone. Schematizing those doctypes now would invert the earn-from-the-driver discipline ([doctype-map.md](implementation/doctype-map.md)) the M13 entry itself invokes. So **half #2 defers behind the dialect-extension milestone** ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)), and M13 is a focused, honest **arch-doc** milestone + the relations triage.

**Settled forks (human-gated):**
- **arch-doc shape → repeatable component entries** (the richer, genuinely-faithful shape, chosen over the minimal fixed-prose option). A persisted doctype (`location: architecture/`): a doc-level `overview` slot, a doc-level n→n `cites → adr` **header** ref (walks the edge index today — exercised), and a **repeatable `components` section** (each component a `description` slot + an `implemented-by` `code-anchor`). Single-word section ids route around the latent multi-word-heading defect (still deferred).
- **"Living" → create-only + the git-editable channel.** The workflow creates a fresh arch-doc; hand-edits are absorbed by OOB-reconcile and re-checked by `arch-doc↔code`. The create-or-update-via-bind path is unexercised (`unverified-reuse`) and deferred.
- **arch-doc↔code → per-component `symbol-exists`.** This forces M13's one engine concept: a **per-field-type predicate selector** (`check:` on the pack field-type decl), since position no longer discriminates the `doc-code` predicate (`spec.criteria` wants `criterion-maps-to-test`; arch-doc's `components` want `symbol-exists`). A pure positional flip would break `spec.criteria`; keying on doctype would violate engine-empty — the `check:` selector keeps the predicate pack-declared, on the axis the adjudicator already rides. Acceptance points anchors at jigc's own Rust codebase (the `doc-code` probe is Rust-grammar-only).
- **Doc home → a new `design/architecture-documentation.md`** (the architecture-documentation workflow is first-class, with no natural host doc), inserted into the reading order.
- **Relations triage → only `cites→adr` IN.** `spec —decided-by→ adr` and `prd —decomposes-into→ spec` are both **OUT** (no driver in M13; `decomposes-into` additionally structurally blocked on the deferred `prd` repeatable-requirements shape) — the no-edge-without-a-driver gate.

**The repeatable shape pulls a bounded engine surface into M13** (sized by a planning spike against the real binary, decomposed risk-first below): the `check:` predicate selector (cross-cutting, first); item-scoped engine setters `set_item_slot`/`set_item_field` (reusing the span-generic `splice` + the per-item spans `ParsedItem` already records); the CLI `add-item` verb + `#section/item/leaf` addressing; then the pack + design + acceptance (flow 16). This is real engine work earned by the chosen shape — not the "pure pack data" the minimal shape would have been. Graduated from [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md): `add-item` (+ item-leaf setters) and the arch-doc doctype shape; `remove-item`/`reorder` and the multi-word-heading fix stay deferred (arch-doc does not trip them).

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M13 Increment 1 ("the per-field-type `check:` predicate selector — the cross-cutting engine change, retired first") into three ordered, single-concern tasks, each with an observable red step. The increment makes the `doc-code` predicate (`symbol-exists` vs `criterion-maps-to-test`) **pack-declared and position-independent** — chosen from the resolved field-type's `check:` (overridable per schema field), not by section position ([architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md) → The per-field-type predicate selector; [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The `doc-code` probe; [document-type-schema.md](design/document-type-schema.md) → Pack-declared field types). No `arch-doc` doctype, no item setters, no CLI verb this increment (those are inc 2–4); no probe code changes (the `(doc-code, symbol-exists)`/`(doc-code, criterion-maps-to-test)` check ids are unchanged — only the *selection mechanism* moves). *Grounding (read + exercised against the real code at base `daa2efa`, the M13-inc-1 shape):*

- **(a) The predicate is chosen by *position* today, via two hardcoded constants.** `crates/engine/src/target_surface.rs` declares `const SYMBOL_EXISTS` (l.60) + `const CRITERION_MAPS_TO_TEST` (l.64); `collect_simple` (l.193) hardcodes `check_id: SYMBOL_EXISTS` for every header/simple-section `code-anchor`, and `collect_repeatable` (l.221) hardcodes `check_id: CRITERION_MAPS_TO_TEST` for every repeatable-item `code-anchor` leaf. The module doc-comment (l.38–42) states "The position *is* the discriminator" — exactly the coincidence arch-doc breaks (its repeatable `components/implemented-by` wants `symbol-exists`). The two constants must be **deleted** and the check id read from the resolved field type / field override.
- **(b) The carriers to widen.** `FieldType::Pack(PackFieldType { name, adjudicator })` (`schema.rs:309`) gains an optional `check`; the on-disk `PackTypeDecl { name, adjudicator }` (`schema.rs:329`, `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`) gains a **required** `check` (the design pins "no implicit engine default" — [architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md) l.52); the schema `Field` (`schema.rs:171`, `deny_unknown_fields`) gains an optional `check: Option<String>` (`skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none`). `resolve_field_type` (`schema.rs:416`) threads `decl.check` → `pack.check` alongside the existing `decl.adjudicator` → `pack.adjudicator`. Because `PackTypeDecl`'s `check` is required and `deny_unknown_fields` is set on both ends, the shipped `crates/cli/pack/config/field-types.yaml` decl (`{ name: code-anchor, adjudicator: doc-code }`, l.11) and the test helper `dev_pack_field_types()` (`schema.rs:439`) **must** gain `check: symbol-exists` in the **same task** as the struct widening, or the shipped-bytes load breaks (`pack_field_types` in `crates/cli/src/pack.rs:31` deserializes the file directly into `Vec<PackTypeDecl>`; ~6 engine call-sites thread `dev_pack_field_types()`) — so T1 carries the engine widening *and* the decl-side edits together to keep the tree green.
- **(c) `is_code_anchor` already matches on `PackFieldType.name`** (`target_surface.rs:258`), so the resolved `FieldType::Pack(p)` is already in hand at both enumeration sites — `collect_simple`/`collect_repeatable` need only compute `check_id = field.check.clone().or_else(|| p.check.clone())` and `.expect`/error on the (post-T1, structurally-impossible-for-a-resolved-pack-type) `None`. This is the `field.check ?? field_type.check` resolution order the scope names.
- **(d) The intended golden diff (recorded, hardening #4).** `FieldType::Pack` serializes as a **bare string** (only `name` — `schema.rs:280`), so the **type-level** `check` never appears in a serialized schema; only the **field-level** override on `spec.criteria/maps-to-test` will. The `schema_spec` inline-snapshot golden (`crates/engine/src/schema.rs` tests, `engine__schema__tests__schema_spec.snap`) **must be re-pinned** to admit the added `check: criterion-maps-to-test` row on `maps-to-test` — a justified, intended output-*adding* diff. `schema_adr`/`schema_commit` are unchanged (`adr.cites-code` stays bare `code-anchor`, inheriting the type-level `symbol-exists`). The `enumerate_target_surface` acceptance test (`target_surface.rs:428`) already asserts the bound spec's `maps-to-test` → `criterion-maps-to-test` and the created adr's `cites-code` → `symbol-exists`; it must stay green (now via the `check:` resolution, not position).

*No genuine new fork surfaced* — the design ([architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md) → The per-field-type predicate selector) settles the semantics, resolution order (`field.check` else type `check`), the "no implicit engine default" pin, and the spec-override requirement; the rejected alternatives (positional flip / doctype-keying) are recorded. The only executor latitude is the concrete representation of the optional `check` on the two structs (an elaboration pin within the locked model), not a fork. Risk-first, linear: widen the carriers + thread resolution + keep the shipped decl loadable (T1), then move the two enumeration sites onto the resolved check + delete the positional constants + the new repeatable-`symbol-exists` proof (T2), then the `spec.yaml` override edit + the flow-13 green-bar regression + the golden re-pin (T3). *Why this cut:* the smallest set delivering all three *Grouped scope* bullets — the `PackFieldType`/`Field`/decl widening + the shipped `field-types.yaml` `check` (bullet 1 → T1), the `target_surface.rs` `check_id = field.check ?? field_type.check` read at both sites + the two-constant deletion (bullet 2 → T2), the `spec.yaml` explicit `check: criterion-maps-to-test` + the flow-13 green-bar re-run + the new repeatable-`symbol-exists` test (bullet 3 → T2 for the engine-side new test, T3 for the spec edit + flow-13 re-run). No creep into inc 2 (item setters), inc 3 (`add-item` verb), inc 4 (the `arch-doc` doctype + workflow), or inc 5 (the flow-16 acceptance).

- **T1 (engine — widen `PackFieldType` / `Field` / `PackTypeDecl` by `check` + thread it through resolution, shipped decl kept loadable):** the field-type vocabulary carries a `check` predicate id; a pack's on-disk decl declares it explicitly (no engine default); `resolve_field_type` binds it like the adjudicator. *Done:* `crates/engine/src/schema.rs` — `PackFieldType` gains `check: Option<String>` (None until resolved), the schema `Field` gains `check: Option<String>` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, the per-field override), `PackTypeDecl` gains a **required** `check: String`; `resolve_field_type` sets `pack.check = Some(decl.check.clone())` alongside the existing adjudicator binding; the shipped `crates/cli/pack/config/field-types.yaml` decl and the `dev_pack_field_types()` test helper both carry `check: symbol-exists`; an engine unit test asserts a schema loaded with the pack set resolves a bare `code-anchor` field to a `FieldType::Pack` carrying `check: Some("symbol-exists")` **and** a field declaring an explicit `check: criterion-maps-to-test` carries that field-level value (the override present in the model), and a `PackTypeDecl` YAML **missing** `check` fails to load (the no-default pin); the existing schema/target_surface/probe engine tests + the shipped-bytes loads stay green — gate green.
- **T2 (engine — `target_surface.rs` reads `check_id` from `field.check ?? field_type.check` at both sites; delete the two positional constants; new repeatable-`symbol-exists` proof):** the predicate is read from the resolution, not the section's shape. *Done:* `crates/engine/src/target_surface.rs` — `collect_simple` and `collect_repeatable` compute `check_id = field.check.clone().or_else(|| <resolved FieldType::Pack>.check.clone())` (the field override else the type check), `const SYMBOL_EXISTS` and `const CRITERION_MAPS_TO_TEST` are **deleted**; a **new** engine test enumerates a fixture doctype whose **repeatable** section carries a `code-anchor` leaf resolving (via the type-level `symbol-exists`, no field override) to `check_id: "symbol-exists"` (the position-independence proof the scope names — a repeatable anchor that is *not* the test predicate); the existing `enumerates_created_and_bound_anchors_skips_unrelated_committed` acceptance (`target_surface.rs:428`) stays green, now asserting `spec.criteria/maps-to-test → criterion-maps-to-test` and `adr.cites-code → symbol-exists` resolved by `check:`, not position — gate green.
- **T3 (pack + acceptance — `spec.yaml` explicit override + flow-13 green-bar + golden re-pin):** `spec`'s shipped predicate is preserved by an explicit field-level `check:`, proven by re-running the M10 acceptance. *Done:* `crates/cli/pack/schemas/spec.yaml`'s `criteria` block `maps-to-test` leaf gains `check: criterion-maps-to-test`; the `schema_spec` inline-snapshot golden (`crates/engine/src/schema.rs` tests) is re-pinned to admit the added `check` row (grounding (d) — the justified output-adding diff); the M10 **flow-13 acceptance** (`crates/cli/tests/flow13_acceptance.rs`, all four scenarios) is **re-run green** — `spec.criteria/maps-to-test` still selects `criterion-maps-to-test` and still **blocks a deleted test** (`flow13_blocking_walk_dangling_maps_to_test_blocks_finalize`), the regression the review flagged; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + the full `cargo test` suite pass — gate green.

- *Elaboration pin (T1 — the `check` carrier representation):* the design settles the *semantics* (a pack-declared `check` predicate id, field-level override else type-level, no implicit engine default) but leaves the concrete struct fields illustrative. The executor pins `Option<String>` on `PackFieldType`/`Field` and required `String` on `PackTypeDecl` (mirroring how `adjudicator` already rides as `Option<String>`/`String` respectively) — a doc-elaboration pin within the locked model, not a fork. *Shipped (T1):* widening `Field` by `check` tipped `schema::Leaf` over the `large_enum_variant` floor, so `Leaf::Field(Field)` became `Leaf::Field(Box<Field>)` (the clippy-blessed fix); the five `Leaf::Field(..)`-match sites are unaffected (auto-deref), the one `collect()` site dereferences via `f.as_ref()`.
- *Grounding pin (T2 — the resolved-type check is already reachable):* `is_code_anchor` (`target_surface.rs:258`) already destructures `FieldType::Pack(p)`, so both enumeration sites already hold the resolved type when they decide the check id — moving the predicate source is a local change at each site, not new plumbing. The post-T1 invariant (a resolved pack field type always carries `check: Some(_)`) makes the fallback total; the executor handles the structurally-impossible `None` as a typed error/`expect`, never a silent default that could re-introduce the absent-default trap the review flagged.

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 1 / T2 shipped: the selector reads `field.check ?? field_type.check` at both enumeration sites; positional constants deleted; T3 folded in (atomic)

`target_surface.rs` now computes `check_id` via `resolve_check_id(field)` (the field-level `check:` override else the resolved `FieldType::Pack`'s `check`) at **both** `collect_simple` and `collect_repeatable`; the two positional constants `SYMBOL_EXISTS` / `CRITERION_MAPS_TO_TEST` are **deleted** — the predicate is pack-declared and **position-independent**. The structurally-impossible `None` (a resolved pack type always carries `check: Some(_)`, the post-T1 invariant) is an `expect`/`unreachable!`, never a silent default (the absent-default trap). New engine test `repeatable_anchor_inherits_type_level_symbol_exists` proves a **repeatable** bare `code-anchor` resolves to `symbol-exists` (red-for-the-right-reason verified: the deleted positional constant forced it to `criterion-maps-to-test`); the existing `enumerates_…` acceptance stays green now asserting both anchors resolved by `check:`, its bound `spec` schema switched to an inline fixture carrying the explicit override so the proof is self-contained.

**T3 folded into this task (the grouped scope handed to this run did so):** deleting the positional constant **necessarily** breaks the M10 flow-13 acceptance over the *shipped* `spec.yaml` (whose `maps-to-test` had no `check:` yet), so a green T2 gate is impossible without the override — they are atomic, not separable. So this commit also lands `spec.yaml`'s `maps-to-test: { …, check: criterion-maps-to-test }` and re-pins the `schema_spec` golden to admit the added `check` row; **flow 13 re-runs green** (`spec.criteria/maps-to-test` still selects `criterion-maps-to-test` and still blocks a deleted test). The earlier T2/T3 decomposition rows above stand as the plan; the build merged them because the gate forced it.

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M13 Increment 2 ("Item-scoped engine setters `set_item_slot` / `set_item_field`") into two ordered, single-concern tasks, each with an observable red step. **Engine-only, fixtures-only — no CLI** (the CLI `add-item` verb + item-leaf address routing is Increment 3). *Grounding (read the code — every pinned reuse verified against `crates/engine/src/write.rs` + `parse.rs`):* (a) the wrong-item bug is **real and located** — `set_field`/`set_field_validated` locate the value via `locate_field_value` (`write.rs:879`), which scans **globally** over `scan_blocks` and returns the *first* matching `key:` line (so component B's `implemented-by` resolves to component #1's bytes), and `set_slot` locates via `locate_slot_span` (`write.rs:2774`), which only reads a *section-level* `slot`, never a per-item one; (b) the byte-region locator the design names already exists — `locate_item_block(source, id)` (`write.rs:954`) returns the item's whole `### …{#id}` … next-boundary span; (c) the region-bounded field scanner already exists — `field_value_in_lines(source, region, key, bullet)` (`write.rs:906`) takes a `Range` region bound, so threading the item region in is *threading, not new parsing* (the design's exact pin); (d) **the parser already records per-item slot+field structure** — `ParsedItem` (`parse.rs:119`) carries `slot: Option<Span>` and `fields: Vec<Field>`, populated by `parse_sections`, so `set_item_slot` can read the addressed item's recorded slot span *directly* (the dual of `set_slot`'s `locate_slot_span`, item-scoped) and `set_item_field` can assert the field's presence from the parsed item before locating its value bytes; (e) `splice` (`write.rs:762`) is span-generic and reused unchanged. So this increment is **two new separate functions + their multi-item goldens**, riding the already-built `locate_item_block` / `field_value_in_lines` / parsed-`ParsedItem`-span / `splice` substrate — the shipped `set_field`/`set_slot`/`set_field_validated` are **not** reused (their global/section-only scan *is* the bug). Order: field first (the literal global-scan-bug locus, the region-threading the design pins), slot second (reads the parsed item's recorded span — simpler, builds on T1's region-locator pattern). *Why this cut:* the smallest set that retires the wrong-item write bug in isolation on fixtures, before the CLI verbs (Increment 3) and arch-doc's `components` (Increments 4–5) ride on it.

- **T1 (engine):** `set_item_field(schema, source, section_id, item_id, field_key, value) -> Result<String, SpliceError>` — set a repeatable item's field by `(section_id, item_id, field_key)`, scoped to that item's byte region. *Done:* a new `set_item_field` (separate from `set_field` — **not** a wrapper) re-parses for conformance, finds the addressed `ParsedItem` in `section_id` (else `SpliceError::NotPresent`), asserts `field_key` is present in *that item's* parsed `fields` (else `NotPresent`), locates the value span via `field_value_in_lines(source, locate_item_block(source, item_id)?, field_key, /*bullet=*/true)` — the scan restricted to the item's region — and `splice`s only the value bytes. The red step is a **multi-item disambiguation golden**: a fixture repeatable section with ≥2 items A and B carrying an **identical field key** (e.g. both `- implemented-by: …`) with distinct values; `set_item_field(.., "B", "implemented-by", NEW)` asserts (a) B's value is exactly `NEW`, (b) **A's identically-keyed field is byte-for-byte untouched** (the surgical-byte-equality assert pattern at `write.rs:~1766`), (c) `render(parse(out)) == out` (still conformant); and the inverse `set_item_field(.., "A", ..)` proves A is targetable too (so the test is not order-trivial). Gate green.
- **T2 (engine):** `set_item_slot(schema, source, section_id, item_id, prose) -> Result<String, SpliceError>` — set a repeatable item's per-item slot prose by `(section_id, item_id)`, scoped to that item. *Done:* a new `set_item_slot` (separate from `set_slot` — its `locate_slot_span` reads only a section-level slot) re-parses, finds the addressed `ParsedItem` in `section_id` (else `NotPresent`), reads that item's recorded `slot: Option<Span>` (else `NotPresent` "slot in item"), and `splice`s the recorded span with `prose`. The red step is a **multi-item disambiguation golden**: a fixture repeatable section whose item template declares a per-item slot, ≥2 items A and B each with slot prose; `set_item_slot(.., "B", NEW)` asserts (a) B's slot prose is now `NEW`, (b) **A's slot prose is byte-for-byte untouched**, (c) `render(parse(out)) == out`; plus the inverse targeting A. Gate green.

- *Elaboration pin (T1 — item fields are sentinelled bullets, so `bullet=true`):* `append_field_group` (`write.rs:194`) emits per-item fields as a sentinelled `<!-- fields -->` + `- key: value` bullet group, so `field_value_in_lines` over the item region must pass `bullet=true` (strip the `- ` marker before reading the key) — matching how `locate_field_value`'s `Block::List` arm reads body bullets. The header front-matter path (`bullet=false`) does not apply to repeatable-item leaves.
- *Elaboration pin (T2 — read the parsed span, do not re-derive it):* the design says "thread `item_id`→region into the locator," and the most faithful reuse is to read the parsed `ParsedItem.slot` span directly from `parse_sections` (the dual of `set_slot`/`locate_slot_span`, restricted to the item) rather than re-scanning the item region for slot bytes — the parser already owns the per-item slot-span derivation (`write.rs:587` re-slices it today in `reparse_to_instance`), so re-deriving it in the setter would duplicate parser logic. `locate_item_block` is still the region anchor for T1's field scan; T2's slot span comes from the parsed item. This is a doc-elaboration pin within the settled "scope the scan to the item" contract, not a new fork.
- *Elaboration pin (both — `SpliceError`, not a new error type):* the new setters return the existing `SpliceError` (`NotPresent` / `NotConformant`), mirroring `set_field`/`set_slot`, so Increment 3's CLI routing maps them through the existing `splice_error_finding` path unchanged — no new engine error surface.
- *Scope note:* both grouped-scope bullets are covered — bullet 1 (the two setters over `locate_item_block` + region-restricted scan + `splice` reuse) splits cleanly into T1 (field) + T2 (slot); bullet 2 (the shipped setters are **not** reused — they carry the wrong-item bug) is a build *constraint* satisfied by making both new functions standalone, asserted by the multi-item goldens proving the addressed item (not the first match) is targeted. No CLI, no `add-item` verb, no addressing — those are Increment 3.

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M13 Increment 3 ("CLI `add-item` verb + item-leaf addressing") into three ordered, single-concern tasks, each with an observable red step over the **real `jigc` binary**. The increment makes **repeatable items authorable through the binary** — `jigc doc add-item <addr>#<section> --title "…"` mints an item; `set-slot`/`set-field` resolve a `#section/item/leaf` fragment and route to the Increment-2 item-scoped setters ([write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md); [architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md) → build surface 3). CLI wiring only — every engine primitive it calls (`add_item`, `set_item_slot`, `set_item_field`) already ships. *Grounding (read + exercised against the real code at HEAD `baac821`, the M13-inc-3 shape):*

- **(a) `add_item` ships, `pub`, with no production caller yet.** `engine::write::add_item(schema, source, section_id, title, slot: Option<&str>, fields: &[Field]) -> Result<String, GenerateError>` (`write.rs:1348`) mints the `{#id}` from `title` via `slug::slugify`, self-materializes the `## <Section>` home when absent, appends the item, and rejects a colliding minted id (`AlreadyPresent`). Its only callers today are engine tests — **this increment is its first production caller** (the create→first-`add-item` home-materialization the design flags as a low-risk caveat is exercised by T3's acceptance, not assumed).
- **(b) The Increment-2 item setters ship, `pub`, returning `SpliceError`.** `set_item_field(schema, source, section_id, item_id, field_key, value) -> Result<String, SpliceError>` (`write.rs:883`, commit `6dcfb8c`) and `set_item_slot(schema, source, section_id, item_id, prose) -> Result<String, SpliceError>` (`write.rs:933`, commit `baac821`) scope the write to the addressed item's byte region — the wrong-item bug already retired on fixtures. **They are *not* the `*_validated` wrappers** (`set_field_validated`/`set_slot_validated`, `write.rs:2874`/`2967`, which carry the value type-check + slot-heading-ceiling + `validate_after` adjudication) — *the item setters carry no equivalent adjudication*, so the CLI routing must decide what gate, if any, wraps an item-leaf write (see the *adjudication-parity* pin below — an elaboration, not a fork).
- **(c) The error→`Finding` mappers the scope names are *private*.** `generate_error_finding` (`write.rs:3068`) and `splice_error_finding` (`write.rs:3101`) are module-private `fn`s — so the scope's "map `GenerateError`→`Finding`" and Increment 2's pin ("CLI routing maps them through the existing `splice_error_finding` path unchanged") cannot be honored as written without **exposing them `pub`** from `engine::write`. Expose-vs-replicate is an elaboration pin (below); the executor must verify the chosen path compiles + produces a routed block (no private-path assumption left untested).
- **(d) The fragment the parser actually produces ≠ the scope's literal wording.** `Fragment::parse` (`address.rs:131`) splits by hop count: **1 hop → `Fragment::Unit`**, **2 hops → `Fragment::UnitLeaf`**, **3 hops → `Fragment::UnitItemLeaf`** — it **never emits `Fragment::UnitItem`** (the 2-hop bytes are ambiguous with `UnitLeaf`; `UnitItem` is reachable only with schema knowledge, `address.rs:257`). The authoring forms the verbs need are therefore: `add-item arch-doc:<slug>#components` → **`Fragment::Unit`** (the section hop), and `set-slot/set-field …#components/<id>/<leaf>` → **`Fragment::UnitItemLeaf`** (the item-leaf). So the routing T2 adds is `field_target`/`slot_target` learning **`UnitItemLeaf`** (not `UnitItem`, which no parsed address carries); `add-item`'s `#<section>` reads as a bare `Unit` hop. The scope's "`UnitItem`/`UnitItemLeaf`" wording is loose — the parsed-address reality is `Unit` (add-item) + `UnitItemLeaf` (setters); recorded so the executor does not chase a `UnitItem` arm the parser cannot reach.
- **(e) `field_target`/`slot_target` return `None` for item fragments today.** Both (`doc.rs:493`/`518`) match only `Fragment::Unit`/`UnitLeaf` and fall through to `_ => None` for the three-hop item-leaf — so an item-leaf `set-field`/`set-slot` currently fails with "no field/slot addressed". T2 adds the `UnitItemLeaf` arm to each, threading `(section, item, leaf)` to the Increment-2 setters via a new branch in `run_set_field`/`run_set_slot`.
- **(f) The end-to-end fixture is a *shipped* doctype — `spec`, no fixture pack needed.** `spec` (`crates/cli/pack/schemas/spec.yaml`) ships a repeatable `criteria` section with a per-item `statement` **slot** + a `maps-to-test` **field**, and `plan` (`workflows/plan.yaml:6`) `allows-create: [{type: spec, as: spec}]`. So T3's acceptance drives the whole surface on shipped pack content — `jigc start --workflow plan` → `jigc doc create spec` → `add-item spec:<slug>#criteria --title …` → `set-slot …#criteria/<id>/statement` → `set-field …#criteria/<id>/maps-to-test` — **directly retiring the `spec.criteria` deferral** the roadmap names ("the capability `spec.criteria` deferred"), with no test-only fixture pack. The existing `doc_write.rs` e2e (drives `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` against a `git init` temp repo started on a workflow) is the established pattern T3 follows.

*No genuine new fork surfaced* — the design ([architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md) → build surface 3 + the `add-item` ergonomics caveat) settles the verb shape, the mint-empty-then-fill ergonomic (the deliverable: `--title` mints; `set-slot`/`set-field` fill), and the item-leaf addressing; the engine primitives all ship. The executor latitude is three elaboration pins within the locked model (below), not a fork. Risk-first, linear: the mint verb first (the one net-new clap surface + first `add_item` production caller), then the item-leaf set routing (the `UnitItemLeaf` arm over the shipped setters), then the combined end-to-end byte-stable acceptance proving both verbs compose. *Why this cut:* the smallest set delivering both *Grouped scope* bullets — bullet 1 (`DocCommand::AddItem` + `run_add_item`, the `run_create` clone calling `add_item`, error→`Finding`) → T1; bullet 2 (`field_target`/`slot_target` learn the item-leaf fragment, route to the Increment-2 setters) → T2 — plus the deliverable's mandated end-to-end "mint an item, fill its slot + field, byte-stable" proof → T3. No creep into inc 4 (the `arch-doc` doctype + `architecture-documentation` workflow) or inc 5 (the flow-16 acceptance + `arch-doc↔code` activation).

- **T1 (CLI — `DocCommand::AddItem` + `run_add_item`, the mint verb):** `jigc doc add-item <addr>#<section> --title "…"` mints a repeatable item through the binary and surfaces the minted item address. *Done:* `crates/cli/src/doc.rs` — a new `DocCommand::AddItem { addr, title, task }` variant (clap auto-wires it onto the `doc` subcommand tree, as `Create`/`SetField`/`SetSlot` already are) dispatches to a new `run_add_item` cloning the `run_create`/`run_set_slot` shape: resolve the active task (`ActiveTask::resolve`), `parse_addr`, load the addr's schema, resolve the **section id** from the `Fragment::Unit` hop (reject a non-`Unit` / non-repeatable-section addr with an actionable error), `read_or_copy_in` the staged doc, call `engine::write::add_item(&schema, &source, &section_id, &title, None, &[])` (mint-empty-then-fill — `--title` only), map a `GenerateError` to a routed blocking `Finding` (`DocFailure::Block`), `persist` the returned buffer, and **print the minted item address** `<type>:<slug>#<section>/<engine::slug::slugify(&title)>` on stdout (mirroring `run_create` printing `created.address`, so the agent can address the leaf next). *Red step:* a `doc_write.rs`-style e2e starts a `plan` task, `jigc doc create spec --title "Auth flow"`, then `jigc doc add-item spec:auth-flow#criteria --title "Rate limit holds"` — asserts exit 0, stdout is exactly `spec:auth-flow#criteria/rate-limit-holds`, the staged `spec` now parses with one `### Rate limit holds  {#rate-limit-holds}` item, and `render(parse(staged)) == staged` (byte-stable); plus an `add-item` into a **non-repeatable** section (e.g. `spec:auth-flow#goal`) blocks with a routed finding, never panics. Gate green.
- **T2 (CLI — item-leaf addressing: `field_target`/`slot_target` learn `UnitItemLeaf`, route to the Increment-2 setters):** `set-slot`/`set-field` on a `#section/item/leaf` fragment write the addressed item's leaf. *Done:* `crates/cli/src/doc.rs` — `field_target` gains a `Fragment::UnitItemLeaf(section, item, leaf)` arm resolving to the item-leaf target, and `run_set_field` routes that case to `engine::write::set_item_field(&schema, &source, &section_id, &item_id, &field_key, &value_text)` (the shipped Increment-2 setter), mapping its `SpliceError` to a routed `Finding`; symmetrically `slot_target` + `run_set_slot` route a `UnitItemLeaf` to `set_item_slot(&schema, &source, &section_id, &item_id, &prose)`. The error→`Finding` path the scope names is wired per the *expose-vs-replicate* pin below. The existing `Unit`/`UnitLeaf` (section-level) paths are **unchanged** (they still call `set_field_validated`/`set_slot_validated`). *Red step:* a `doc_write.rs`-style e2e (over a `plan`-started `spec` with **two** `criteria` items A and B added via T1's verb, both carrying a `statement` slot + a `maps-to-test` field) — `set-slot spec:<slug>#criteria/<B>/statement` and `set-field spec:<slug>#criteria/<B>/maps-to-test --value '`crates/x.rs#f`'` assert (a) B's leaf bytes are exactly the new values, (b) **A's identically-keyed leaf bytes are byte-for-byte untouched** (the multi-item disambiguation proof, hardening #4, driven through the binary), (c) the staged doc round-trips (`render(parse) == staged`); and the inverse targeting A proves A is addressable too (not order-trivial). Gate green.
- **T3 (acceptance — end-to-end byte-stable item authoring on the shipped `spec` doctype):** the deliverable's mandated proof — mint an item, fill its slot + field, byte-stable — across both verbs on shipped pack content. *Done:* `crates/cli/tests/` — a new e2e drives the real `jigc` binary on a `plan`-started task: `jigc doc create spec --title …`, `jigc doc add-item spec:<slug>#criteria --title …` (×2, two distinct criteria), then per item `set-slot …/statement` + `set-field …/maps-to-test`, asserting each emitted `add-item` item-address line **runs verbatim** as the next `set-*`'s addr (hardening #4 — the agent-facing emitted bytes are the contract, executed as emitted, not reconstructed in test code), each item's leaves resolve to **its own** authored bytes (per-item disambiguation through the binary), and the final staged `spec` is canonical (`render(parse) == staged`, the byte-stability the deliverable names). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + the full `cargo test` suite pass — gate green.

- *Elaboration pin (T1/T2 — expose-vs-replicate the error mappers):* the scope says "map `GenerateError`→`Finding`" and Increment 2's pin routes the item setters' `SpliceError` "through the existing `splice_error_finding` path"; both mappers are **module-private** in `engine::write` (grounding (c)). The faithful, minimal elaboration is to **expose them `pub`** (`pub fn generate_error_finding` / `pub fn splice_error_finding`) so the CLI reuses the one canonical block shape (matching how `doc.rs` already imports `set_field_validated`/`set_slot_validated` from `engine::write`), rather than replicating the match in the CLI (which would drift from the engine's codes). The CLI's `block(&finding, verb, addr)` helper (`doc.rs:537`) still supplies the retry route when the finding carries none. The executor verifies the chosen path compiles and emits a routed block (grounding (c)'s "no private-path assumption left untested"); whichever path is taken is a doc-elaboration pin within the locked design, not a fork.
- *Elaboration pin (T2 — adjudication-parity for item leaves is *deferred-by-absence*, not silently dropped):* the section-level `set-field`/`set-slot` route through `set_field_validated`/`set_slot_validated` (value type-check + slot-heading-ceiling + `validate_after`); the Increment-2 item setters carry **no** equivalent gate (grounding (b)). M13's scope wires the CLI to the **raw** item setters as the Increment-2 plan pinned — so item-leaf writes get the engine's structural splice + the setters' own re-parse-conformance/NotPresent guards, but **not** the value-type/heading-ceiling adjudication the section path has. This is **within** the settled Increment-2 contract (which built the raw setters deliberately), not a new reduction: the arch-doc acceptance (inc 5) drives well-formed leaf values, and a validated item-setter wrapper is a follow-on the design does not require for M13. The executor records this parity gap in a `run_set_field`/`run_set_slot` code comment at the item-leaf branch (so it is *tracked*, not hidden) and does **not** silently present the item path as carrying the section path's adjudication. (If the executor finds an arch-doc/`spec` acceptance genuinely *needs* item-leaf value adjudication to pass, that is a halt — a new gate is out of this increment's cut.)
- *Elaboration pin (T1 — the minted-id surface reuses the engine's slugger):* `add_item` returns only the edited buffer, not the minted id; `run_add_item` computes the surfaced item address via `engine::slug::slugify(&title)` (`slug.rs:52`, `pub`) — **calling the engine's mint, never reimplementing slug logic in the CLI** (the CLI owns presentation/IO, the engine owns the id derivation; the determinism boundary is unaffected). Keeping `add_item`'s signature unchanged (no new return tuple) is the smaller surface; the slugify call is the shared-truth read.
- *Scope note:* both grouped-scope bullets land in this increment — bullet 1 (`DocCommand::AddItem` + `run_add_item`) → T1; bullet 2 (`field_target`/`slot_target` handle the item-leaf fragment, route to the Increment-2 setters) → T2 — with T3 the deliverable's mandated end-to-end byte-stable proof. The loose "`UnitItem`/`UnitItemLeaf`" wording in bullet 2 resolves to the parser-real `Unit` (add-item section hop) + `UnitItemLeaf` (item-leaf set) per grounding (d); no `UnitItem` arm is added (no parsed address carries it). Nothing punted to a later increment; no creep into inc 4/5.

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 3 / T1 shipped: the `add-item` mint verb + an `insert_block` EOF-append byte-stability fix the first production caller surfaced

Shipped `DocCommand::AddItem` + `run_add_item` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs`) cloning the `run_create`/`run_set_slot` shape — resolve active task, `parse_addr`, resolve the section from the `Fragment::Unit` hop (`section_hop`, which also passes a `UnitLeaf`/`UnitItem`/`UnitItemLeaf` leading hop through to let the engine adjudicate shape), `read_or_copy_in`, call `engine::write::add_item(&schema, &source, &section_id, title, None, &[])` (mint-empty: `--title` only), map `GenerateError`→routed block via the now-`pub` `engine::write::generate_error_finding` (the expose-vs-replicate pin, taken as exposed), persist, and print `<type>:<slug>#<section>/<slug(title)>` via `engine::slug::slugify` (the slugger-reuse pin). First production caller of `add_item`.

**Genuine new finding (in-scope bug fix, not a fork):** T1's mandated `render(parse(staged)) == staged` byte-stability surfaced a latent round-trip defect in `engine::write::insert_block`'s **EOF-append** branch (`write.rs:1658`). The branch emitted `{head}\n\n{block}\n`, but a generated item block already carries its own trailing newline(s) — an **empty** repeatable item renders `### …{#id}\n\n\n` — so appending an item into a trailing repeatable section left `\n\n\n\n` trailing debris, non-canonical. The populated golden masked it (insta trims trailing whitespace; the create→first-`add-item` path the planning flagged as a "low-risk caveat" is the exact shape that hits it). Fix: back-trim the block's trailing `\n` before the append so the canonical EOF rule (exactly one trailing `\n`) holds across the insert. Guarded by a raw-byte engine round-trip test (`add_item_into_empty_trailing_section_is_byte_stable`) + the e2e byte-stable acceptance; all 368 engine + CLI tests stay green (no snapshot regression — the other `insert_block` callers' goldens already ended canonically).

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 3: absent-item-field generation (the mint-empty-then-fill gap)

**The gap (a build halt, settled resolution — not a fork).** `add-item` mints items **empty** (heading + empty slot span, no field bullets — the mint-empty ergonomic), but the only item-field setter, increment-2's `engine::write::set_item_field`, splices a bullet **only if already present** (`SpliceError::NotPresent` on an absent one). So filling a freshly-minted item's *declared field* through the binary was **unreachable** — the workflow's `add-item → set-field` path could never write the first item-field value. The header path had no such gap: `set_field_validated` falls back to `insert_front_matter_field` to *generate* an absent header field. **Resolution: give items the same generation capability (mirror the header path); keep `add_item` mint-empty.**

- **New `engine::write::insert_item_field`** — the item-scoped twin of `insert_front_matter_field`/`insert_field`: when a present item's declared bullet is **absent**, it generates the `- key: value` bullet, emitting the `<!-- fields -->` sentinel **once** if the item has no field group yet. All scanning is confined to `locate_item_block(source, item_id)`, so a sibling item's identical key is out of range (the wrong-item write bug, on the insert path). For a **mint-empty** item (empty slot span) it re-renders the item via `render_item` and splices over its located block — byte-stable by construction (`render(parse(out)) == out`), where a slot-prose-end bullet insert would mis-space the empty slot's canonical blank lines.
- **One CLI entry point: `engine::write::set_item_field_or_insert`** — splice-present (the inc-2 `set_item_field`) **else** insert-absent (`insert_item_field`), mirroring `set_field` ↔ `insert_front_matter_field`. The resuming CLI `UnitItemLeaf` `set-field` arm calls this single function.
- **Adjudication-parity stays deferred.** This fix generates the absent bullet only — **no** value-type / slot-heading-ceiling gate (no `set_item_field_validated` mirroring the header `set_field_validated`). The item-leaf adjudication-parity gap is the planner's already-pinned deferral (`no value-type/heading-ceiling gate`); not reopened here.
- Engine-only; CLI routing + the e2e is the resuming T2. Red→green: `set_item_field_generates_absent_bullet_on_minted_item` (mint two empty items, generate the first's bullet at its field-group position, second's identical key stays absent, byte-stable) + `set_item_field_or_insert_splices_a_present_bullet` (present-bullet regression). 370 tests green.

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 3: mint-empty repeatable-item byte-stability

**A byte-stability defect *pair* at the new repeatable-item authoring seam** (`add-item` mints empty, then item-leaf setters fill) — the project's retired #1 risk (`render(parse(x)) == x`) leaked. Both were missed because increment-2's setter tests only exercised **canonically-rendered** items (a filled item always re-renders identically), never a **mint-empty** one. Engine-only fix; CLI item-leaf addressing (T2) untouched.

- **Defect 1 — `set_item_slot` not byte-stable on a mint-empty item.** The parser records a mint-empty item's slot span *without* the canonical surrounding blank lines, so splicing prose into that bare span yielded `### H  {#h}\nprose\n### Next` while `render_item` emits `### H  {#h}\n\nprose\n\n### Next`. Mint-empty is the **only** state an item-leaf set-slot runs in.
- **Defect 2 — `add_item` mis-spaced an empty item that *precedes* another.** Two adjacent mint-empty items rendered as `### A\n\n### B` (add_item's fixed one-blank join) but re-rendered as `### A\n\n\n\n### B` (`render_item`'s empty-item form `### A\n\n\n`). Existing tests only ever left the **trailing** item empty, so a **non-trailing** empty item was never round-trip-checked.

**Fix — one canonical item-bytes path (`render_item`), the trick `insert_item_field` already uses.** `set_item_slot` now re-renders the affected item via `render_item` (slot replaced, fields preserved) and splices the whole item block. `add_item`'s present-section append re-renders the **preceding** last item canonically next to the new one (full `render_item`s joined by a single `\n`, exactly `render_section`'s join), via a new `locate_last_item_block` helper. Both re-attach the **canonical** inter-block separator (`body\n\n` before a following `###`/`##` heading, `body\n` at EOF) — **not** the recorded one, because a now-filled item's gap shrinks from the empty-item form's `\n\n\n\n` to one blank line.

- **Defect-2's fix exposed the same recorded-separator bug in `insert_item_field`** (the inc-3 absent-field generator): with two empty items now `\n\n\n\n`-spaced on disk, re-attaching the recorded separator over-spaced the now-filled item. Fixed identically (canonical separator), keeping the three callers consistent. No golden re-pinned (filled items re-render byte-identically; the disambiguation snapshots are unchanged).
- Red→green regressions (the gaps current tests missed): `set_item_slot_on_mint_empty_item_is_byte_stable` (mint two empty, fill the **first**/non-trailing, `render(parse(out)) == out`) + `two_empty_add_items_are_byte_stable` (two empty `add_item`s, no fill, byte-stable). 372 engine tests + full CLI suite green.

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 3 / T2 shipped: item-leaf addressing

**The CLI write-path now reaches per-item leaves.** `field_target`/`slot_target` gained the `Fragment::UnitItemLeaf(section, item, leaf)` arm, returning a target that carries the **item id** so two items with identically-keyed leaves disambiguate. `run_set_field` routes the item case to `engine::write::set_item_field_or_insert`, `run_set_slot` to `set_item_slot`; section-level `Unit`/`UnitLeaf` stay on `set_field_validated`/`set_slot_validated`. (`splice_error_finding` exposed `pub`, mirroring `generate_error_finding`.)

- **Parity gap honored (pinned, not reopened).** Item-leaf field writes carry **no** value-type / heading-ceiling adjudication — a one-line code comment marks the branch; the section-level path keeps its `set_field_validated` gate.
- Red→green e2e (`crates/cli/tests/doc_write.rs`): `set_slot_and_field_target_the_addressed_item_leaf` — `plan` task → `create spec` → two `add-item`s (A, B) → set the targeted item's `statement` slot + `maps-to-test` field through the binary, asserting (a) the target's leaves are the new values, (b) the sibling's identically-keyed leaves stay untouched (disambiguation through the binary), (c) `render(parse(staged)) == staged` (the mint-empty seam, now byte-stable per the prior fix); run in **both directions** (target B, then A). Full suite green.

## 2026-06-07 — M13 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M13 Increment 4 ("The `arch-doc` doctype + the architecture-documentation workflow — the pack + the `cites` edge") into four ordered, single-concern tasks, each with an observable red step over the **real `jigc` binary**. The increment ships the `arch-doc` doctype + its driving workflow as **pure pack content** (the engine surface it needs — the item-authoring verbs and the `check:` predicate selector — all shipped in increments 1–3) and verifies the **n→n `cites → adr`** edge walks at finalize (pass + block) with promotion to the fourth `location:` (`architecture/`), all riding proven paths ([architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md) — the design of record; [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md)). *Grounding (read + exercised against the real code at HEAD `ff39955`):*

- **(a) The `cites → adr` edge walks today — header Simple section only.** `doc_edges` (`crates/engine/src/index.rs:442`) emits a forward edge for every present **`ref` field in a Simple section** and **one edge per element** of a `Value::List` (`index.rs:471-479`), so a header `cites` (`card: "0..*"`) n→n walk is the proven `supersedes`/`implements` path; `ref_resolves` (`index.rs:357`) blocks a dangling target, passes a present one. A `ref` in a **repeatable** section emits **no** edge (`index.rs:446-447`, "repeatable-section refs are not an MVP target") — so `cites` **must** live in the header `meta` section (where the design places it), not in `components`. Verified, not assumed.
- **(b) The agent authors a single cite via a scalar `set-field`.** `run_set_field` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs:176-181`) writes a header field as `Value::Scalar`, so `jigc doc set-field arch-doc:<slug>#cites --value adr:<slug>` records one `cites` edge (the acceptance cites a single adr — exactly flow-16's bar). Multi-element list authoring through `set-field` is **not built and not needed** for M13 (a single-cite scalar write + the per-element `doc_edges` walk cover the deliverable); recorded so the executor does not build a list-authoring surface this increment.
- **(c) Promotion to `architecture/` is zero new finalize code.** `plan_promotions` (`crates/engine/src/finalize.rs:326`) reads `schema.location.as_deref()` for **any** persisted doctype and promotes the staged `<type>:<slug>.md` to `{location}/{slug}.md` (`finalize.rs:364-375`), already serving `decisions/`/`specs/`/`prds/`. So `arch-doc` with `location: architecture/` promotes to `architecture/<slug>.md` with no finalize change — the design's pin, verified.
- **(d) The router lists the new workflow with zero code.** `selectable_workflows` (`crates/cli/src/start.rs:887`) enumerates every pack workflow with `creates-task: true` + `selectable: true` carrying a required `when` hint; a selectable workflow missing `when` is a surfaced definition bug. So shipping `architecture-documentation.yaml` (`creates-task: true`, a `when`) makes the router list it automatically — the deliverable's "router lists the new workflow," verified.
- **(e) `as: arch-doc` binds the created doc to `task.arch-doc`.** Mirrors `single-task`'s `allows-create: [{type: adr, as: decision}]` → `task.decision` and `project-setup`'s `[{type: prd, as: brief}]` → `task.brief`; the `author-arch-doc` step addresses `task.arch-doc#overview` / `task.arch-doc#cites` / `task.arch-doc#components/<id>/…`.
- **(f) The `implemented-by` `check:` resolves to `symbol-exists` by inheritance.** `arch-doc.components/implemented-by` is a **bare** `code-anchor` (no field-level `check:`), so it inherits the type-level `check: symbol-exists` from `field-types.yaml` (increment 1 — `target_surface.rs`'s `field.check ?? field_type.check`). No schema field override needed; the explicit override is `spec.criteria/maps-to-test` only.

**The one scope-boundary pin the executor must honor (the inc-4 ↔ inc-5 seam).** The arch-doc carries `implemented-by` `code-anchor` fields that **also** run through the `doc-code` probe at finalize. The **`symbol-exists` block proof on a repeatable-item anchor** — deleting component A's symbol and asserting `finalize` blocks naming A's item address — is **Increment 5's** mandated headline ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M13 Increment 5; the first real finalize snapshot-spawn over a repeatable-item `doc-code` anchor). So Increment 4's `cites` pass+block acceptance (T4) **points every `implemented-by` at a present, real symbol** in jigc's own Rust tree, so `doc-code` *passes* and the **`cites` edge is the sole variable under test** (pass when the cited adr exists, block when it dangles). This is not a punt: the symbol-block proof is **named to and owned by Increment 5** (tracked landing, not "a later task" in the abstract), and T4 deliberately holds `implemented-by` valid so the `cites` pass/block is isolated. No new fork — both increments' boundaries are set in the design.

*No genuine new fork surfaced* — the design ([architecture-documentation.md](design/architecture-documentation.md)) settles the schema shape (header `cites` n→n + repeatable `components`), the workflow front-matter (`creates-task: true`, `allows-create: [{type: arch-doc, as: arch-doc}]`, a `when`), the create-only "living" model, the `check:`-inheritance for `implemented-by`, and the relations triage (only `cites→adr` IN). Executor latitude is the concrete prose of the `author-arch-doc` step + the authored `description:`/`usage:` wording (a doc-elaboration pin within the locked model), not a fork. Risk-first, linear: the schema (pure data, round-trips + the `cites` edge proven on a fixture) first, then the workflow/step/command + the router-lists check, then the describe-surface projection (the M11 clause), then the mandated end-to-end `cites` pass+block + promotion acceptance. *Why this cut:* the smallest set delivering both *Grouped scope* bullets — bullet 1 (the four pack files + authored describe prose) splits into T1 (schema), T2 (workflow + step + command-ref + router-lists), T3 (the `description:`/`usage:` describe-surface clause, a distinct M11-surface concern); bullet 2 (promotion to the fourth `location:` + the `cites` edge verified pass+block) → T4. No creep into inc 5 (the `symbol-exists`-block flow-16 acceptance + the doc fold-back).

- **T1 (pack — `schemas/arch-doc.yaml` + round-trip + the `cites` edge on a fixture):** the `arch-doc` schema ships and round-trips; a header `cites` ref emits one edge per element and resolves. *Done:* `crates/cli/pack/schemas/arch-doc.yaml` per the design — `type: arch-doc`, `location: architecture/`, `id-from: title`, authored `description:`/`usage:`; header `meta` section (`header: true`) with `cites: { type: ref, to: adr, card: "0..*", inverse: cited-by }`; an `overview` slot section; a repeatable `components` section (`id-from: title`, block = `title` string + `description` slot + `implemented-by: { type: code-anchor, check: symbol-exists }` — bare, inheriting `symbol-exists`, **no** field override).
