## 2026-06-08 — M14 milestone-completion: built, audited, 1 coupled finding fixed + re-verified

M14 (multi-pack composition) is **shipped + audited** — and **closes the post-spine arc (M10–M14)**. Built via the [milestone-build](implementation/milestone-build) harness across three risk-first increments (all validated independently CLEAN, **0 design halts / 0 in-increment fix rounds** — back to the M9–M12 baseline after M13's 2); full delivery record in [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → "Milestone 14 … decomposition" → Status.

**Proves:** the architectural invariant *engine-neutral, packs supply content* **generalizes to scale** — the embedded dev pack + the M12 methodology pack co-compose in one project via a `.jigc/config/packs.yaml`-selected composite `PackSource` (base lowest), the engine knowing neither. **Top-level** collisions (`default-workflow` knob, `commit` doctype) resolve by precedence-override (whole-definition, no new merge primitive); **body-references** (a workflow's `{{include: step:X}}` + `{{cli.X}}`, a schema's field-types) resolve **pack-locally** via a new defaulted `PackSource::origin_pack` seam — two independent axes. The single-pack **byte-identity floor** holds (composite-of-`[base]` ≡ the single-pack path; all M12 compose-alone regressions untouched); provenance names every composed pack by path + blake3.

**Plan-time discipline held:** the two-axis collision model + the subsume reckoning (KEEP-SUBSUME, forced by the cost-of-thinning) were settled at Settle, and the design survived **two** independent reviews — the same-model `design-reviewer` (caught the command-catalog body-reference axis) and a human-approved cross-model `/review-codex` (added the field-type axis + the in-binary cold-start floor + path/hash provenance) — all baked before the cut. The result: 0 halts, even on an engine-heavy cascade reshape.

**Audit → 1 coupled finding (a CRITICAL + the HIGH test masking it), human-triaged fix-now + remediated + re-verified** (`f651b14`; final gate green: fmt · clippy `-D warnings` · full `cargo test -p cli` 0 failed): the pack-local rule was applied to the fresh-compose front doors but **not the resume/re-entry spine** `compose_task_workflow` (shared by `jigc start --task` + `workflow W --task`), so resuming a *loser*-pack workflow silently swapped in the precedence-winner's step bodies + catalog — mint ≠ resume, the exact M3-class corruption the milestone exists to prevent — and flow-17 assertion 6a **masked** it (resume-vs-resume, never resume-vs-fresh; comment misnaming the resumed workflow). Fix mirrors the proven fresh-compose origin-scoping onto the resume spine and **de-masks 6a** to compare resume-vs-fresh (the M9/M13 masking-fixture lesson recurring — the audit doing its job). The e2e's set-field item-leaf value-laxity is the already-tracked item-leaf adjudication-parity gap (pre-existing, reproduced in a plain dev-only repo), not an M14 defect.

**Deferred (tracked, [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)):** reconciliation over a composed base (subsumes the fired `override-default` content-target check); cross-pack probe/field-type *collision*; closed-enum union + finer precedence; the `--explain` collision-winner highest-owns-it assumption (correct at the two-pack bound, latent for N>2). **The post-spine arc is complete; the next owed work is the workflow-dialect-extension milestone.**

## 2026-06-08 — VISION: single-domain non-goal dropped; the adoption arc (M15–M17) created

After the post-spine arc closed, the human directed two moves: revise the now-obsolete single-domain framing, and schedule the remaining self-hosting-completion + dogfood work.

**VISION revision (a flagged invariant change, human-initiated).** The *"not a second domain (yet) / not a public extension API"* non-goal is rewritten to **"Not (yet) a public pack platform — but no longer single-domain."** Rationale: M12 minted a second (methodology) pack and M14 composed it with the dev pack under deterministic collision resolution — the engine/pack boundary is now **proven architecture, not just internal discipline**, and the mechanism generalizes to N domains. The honest residual: M14 deliberately kept the mechanism **internal** (it never built a third-party-facing surface), so a *stabilized, documented public pack-authoring API* (third-party contract + versioning) is recast from a permanent non-goal to **future work, earned when a real *external* domain needs it**. Mirrored in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) → Non-goals. ([VISION.md](VISION.md) → "What it is *not*"; [multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md).)

**The adoption arc (M15–M17), milestone-level only** ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → The adoption arc; [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)). The post-spine arc completed the *product*; this arc **completes self-hosting then proves adoption**:
- **M15 · workflow-dialect extension** — the five M12-named triggers; encodes the harder harness workflows (increment/planning/completion). **Built ahead of the dogfood (prereq #1); likely slices at planning.**
- **M16 · methodology working-docs → managed doctypes** (was M13 half-#2) — unblocked by M15's drivers (earn-from-driver); **may fold into M15.** Prereq #2.
- **M17 · dogfood + measurement** — run jigc on three real projects (unlike-jigc · existing-with-ingest · greenfield) with a **composite-facts heuristic**: jigc/the harness emit mechanizable facts (**adapter-adherence** — writes through jigc vs. direct edits the reconcile absorbed, the enforced-not-sandboxed core bet; **drift-caught** — validation blocks that stopped a bad commit; **build-health** — halts/fix-rounds/findings), while the **verdict stays a human/LLM-judge slot** (the engine emits no opinion — the three-way determinism cut). Homes the **M12-deferred quantitative build-health comparison**.

**Gap policy:** dogfood-first / fill-what-hurt — M15 + M16 are the *only* deferrals built ahead of need (the human-set prerequisites); every other tracked deferral fills when a dogfood surfaces it as actually blocking, never speculatively.

## 2026-06-09 — M15 planning: workflow-dialect extension (the checkpoint step kind)

Planned via `/milestone-plan M15` (scope → baseline audit → 4 gap-detectors → settle → review → decompose). The slice (human-confirmed): **encode the increment-workflow only** — planning + completion deferred. The baseline audit + four gap-detectors converged: **M15's entire engine delta is one new primitive — the `checkpoint` step kind**; the rest is pack authoring + prose + orchestration that already exists.

**The central reckoning (the no-runtime/no-conditional invariant, [VISION.md](VISION.md) → Non-goals).** The five M12-named triggers sit against "no DAGs, conditionals, or a runtime." Settled per-trigger:
- **#2 (human-gate) + structural-#4 (halt signal) → one `checkpoint` step kind**, the third kind after `fan-out`/`join` ([workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md#the-checkpoint-step-kind-m15)). It **always composes** (structure stays task-independent) and emits a reserved sixth emit class `Checkpoint: <reason>` the agent/orchestrator **honors by halting** — adding *halting* (finalize's blocking gate lifted to an arbitrary step; the invariant never barred it) without *branching* (a step appearing/disappearing on runtime state; still barred). **Convention-honored, not binary-enforced** (the spike found compose is a pure whole-text function with no streaming/pausing; a binary-enforced mid-workflow halt would require a stateful stepper = a runtime = a VISION revision, rejected). One kind with a `reason` slug, because Settle / the increment's three halts / the fix-loop's halt-pending-fix are all the same shape. **VISION gets a one-sentence clarifying carve-out, not a revision.**
- **#4's loop bound (≤N) + re-run → stay orchestration-level** (the build harness), riding the existing **stateless restart-from-scratch** resumption (`start --task` re-derives from disk; no progress cursor). The dialect contributes only the halt signal — "repeat until clean" is not a dialect construct. The paired never-started-fan-out backstop + Resume hook ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)) are **not triggered** — M15 encodes no fan-out methodology workflow.
- **#1 (test-first ordering) → stays agent-policed prose; the A==A-oracle lint DEFERRED** — no deterministic substrate for "a test observed failing before impl" (a test-running gate breaches the determinism contract), and the static lint has **no `code-anchor` target** to fire against (the methodology pack ships only `commit`). Building it is dead capability until a methodology doctype carries a test-source anchor.
- **#3 (gate-command knob) → DEFERRED** — the gate stays portable prose (more correct on a foreign project the pack can't know the gate command for); surfacing a knob into composed step output needs a new `cascade`/`knob` compose data-value root that doesn't exist, disproportionate to its bounded leverage.
- **#5 (owner-artifact gate) → DEFERRED with the completion-workflow** (out of the increment-only slice).

**The honest encode bound (recorded — the falsifiable edge).** jigc composes a single-agent linear workflow; the increment-workflow is a multi-agent orchestration loop. M15 encodes the **single-agent composable spine** with the checkpoint halts made structural; the multi-agent orchestration (per-phase-agent independence, the independent read-only validate, the bound + re-run) stays orchestration-level — the M12 reduced-linear / M8 genuine-spawn analogue. Written down so a faithful-looking encode can't over-claim jigc owns the loop.

**M16 fold → SEQUENCE, don't fold.** Encoding the increment-workflow earns **zero** managed doctype: Plan's "record the decomposition in DECISIONS.md" is a plain `git` markdown edit (verified against historical decomposition commits), Validate is read-only, Fix delegates to the already-vendored `commit`. M16's drivers (planning/completion workflows) are out of slice; schematizing a doctype before its driver is the M12 trap.

**Honesty tripwire stays green.** M15 adds a **new** `increment` workflow + task-ref-free steps; it does **not** modify the existing prose-degraded `dev-task` steps the `methodology_honesty_artifact` test pins.

**Forward-harness review (mandated, novel off-substrate milestone).** Named failure class M15's green gates could pass: **halt-masking / resumption-state-leak** — (a) a checkpoint that parses but composes inert (the M8 face-#5; probe: composed output must differ with vs. without the marker, against the live fill-aware path), and (b) any mid-workflow progress state that breaks stateless restart (probe: resume-vs-**fresh** byte-identical + same halt verdict, never resume-vs-resume — the M14 A==A mask). Both baked into the checkpoint task's Red/validator obligations.

**Acceptance:** [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 18 (increment-workflow encode). Spiked at planning against the real binary: `jigc start --workflow <X>` composes a `creates-task:false` workflow; a `task.*` ref inside it blocks; a `checkpoint:` marker today composes as inert prose (the "before" state). The `Checkpoint:`-directive emission is the build's red obligation.

Design elaborated: [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) (the carve-out + the sixth emit class + the checkpoint step-kind section), [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) (per-trigger M15 resolution + the honest bound), [VISION.md](VISION.md) (the carve-out sentence). No new design doc / reading-order change (the primitive folds into workflow-dialect.md). Decomposition below.

## 2026-06-09 — M15 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1 — the `checkpoint` step kind (the novel engine surface)](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-1--the-checkpoint-step-kind-the-novel-engine-surface) into four ordered, single-concern tasks. *Why this order:* the primitive is parse → emit → conformance-gate, mirroring how M8 built `fan-out`/`join` in the same file; each layer needs the one before it (emit reads the parsed `kind`; the shadow check reads pre-emit bodies the emit arm consumes), so the engine layers land first (T1–T3) and the real-binary acceptance that discharges the forward-review obligations rides on top (T4). Grounded facts the cut rests on (verified against the base commit `52a59380`, not assumed):

- `StepKind` (`compose.rs:945`) is today a closed 3-variant enum (`Plain`/`FanOut`/`Join`); `StepFrontMatter` (`compose.rs:967`) carries exactly `fan-out` + `join`; `parse_step_kind` (`compose.rs:1027`) is a 2-marker `match (fan_out, join)` already emitting `workflow-refs.step-kind-malformed` (located at line 2) for malformed YAML / both-markers / fan-out-missing-`over`-or-`run`. So the three-marker rewrite + the `Checkpoint { reason }` variant + the new `checkpoint:` field are a **net-new extension of a live, tested seam**, not new machinery. `Checkpoint` has **no pairing rule** (unlike `fan-out`↔`join`) and the boundary-leaf kind inheritance (`compose.rs:1689`) is generic over `step.kind`, so it rides for free.
- The emit seam is `compose_with_store` (`compose.rs:1805`): the `FanOut` arm there **appends** its `Spawn:` directives *after* the body (`compose.rs:1819`). The `Checkpoint:` directive **prepends** *before* the body — the opposite splice point — per [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md#emitted-format) rule 5. `compose_with_store` is the path the CLI's live fill-aware compose drives (after `FillStepSource` resolves fills, `start.rs:1416`), so emitting there is what makes the marker honored on the live path.
- **Verified inventory reality (a scope-pin correction).** The roadmap bullet names "the three check-inventory lists (`CHECK_INVENTORY` ↔ `knobs.yaml` ↔ `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS`)." Against the code this is **false for a compose-level shadow check**: the M8 sibling `spawn-marker-not-shadowed` lives in `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` (`knobs.rs:51`, 16 keys) **and** the `knobs.yaml` per-check enum surface (`pack.rs:827`, floored blocking) — but **not** in `CHECK_INVENTORY` (`result.rs:173`), which carries only `run-marker-not-shadowed` and gates the *task-validate/finalize* severity post-pass, not compose-time checks (`fan-out-join-paired` is likewise absent). So `checkpoint-marker-not-shadowed` follows its M8 sibling's **two-list** footprint (`INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` + `knobs.yaml`), not three. T3's done-criterion makes this an **assumption to prove, not trust**: it asserts the new key's registration footprint is byte-for-byte the same set of lists `spawn-marker-not-shadowed` appears in (and the `per_check_severity_surface_reconciles_to_the_25_16_9_inventory` test at `knobs.rs:571` updates 25→26 / 16→17, incl. the `assert_eq!(INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS.len(), 16)` at `knobs.rs:596`).

- **T1** — Parse the third kind. Add `StepKind::Checkpoint { reason }` (`compose.rs`), give `StepFrontMatter` a `checkpoint:` field (a marker carrying one `reason` slug), and rewrite `parse_step_kind` from the 2-marker `match` to a **three-marker mutual-exclusivity** check: a step is exactly one kind; **any** two of `fan-out`/`join`/`checkpoint` present → the existing blocking `workflow-refs.step-kind-malformed` (line 2); a `checkpoint:` missing/empty `reason` → `step-kind-malformed`; neither marker → `Plain`. *Done:* unit tests on `load_step_def`/`parse_step_kind` assert a `checkpoint: {reason: <slug>}` step loads as `StepKind::Checkpoint { reason }`, that `checkpoint` + any other marker is rejected `step-kind-malformed` at line 2, that an empty/missing `reason` is rejected, and the pre-existing `fan-out`/`join`/`Plain` cases still hold (the serde-tagged golden discriminant updated). *Files:* `crates/engine/src/compose.rs`. *Refs:* [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md#the-checkpoint-step-kind-m15) (Engine reality), [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → Front-matter.
- **T2** — Emit the directive (engine). Add the `Checkpoint` arm to `compose_with_store` (`compose.rs:1805`): a checkpoint step **prepends** `Checkpoint: <reason>` (bare slug, no backticks) as the first line of the step's emitted text, *before* the body prose — the inverse of the `FanOut` arm's append. *Done:* an engine unit test composes a `MapSource` workflow with a checkpoint step and asserts the emitted text opens with `Checkpoint: <slug>\n` followed by the body, **and** asserts the same workflow with the checkpoint marker stripped (a plain step, same body) composes **without** that line — the with-vs-without delta proven at the engine seam (the M8 face-#5 parsed-but-ignored guard, unit layer). *Files:* `crates/engine/src/compose.rs`. *Refs:* [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md#emitted-format) (rule 5, the sixth emit class). *Note:* the binary-level with-vs-without proof on the live fill path is T4.
- **T3** — `checkpoint-marker-not-shadowed` conformance + inventory sync. The novel engine surface — the third step kind, built halt-only within the no-runtime invariant (always composes, emits a `Checkpoint: <reason>` directive the agent honors; halting, not branching; convention-honored; riding stateless restart-from-scratch) — was retired in isolation first, then the methodology `increment` workflow rode it into the plan→execute→validate→fix spine with three machine-recognizable halt directives, composing through the real binary.

No e2e findings; no scope dishonesty; the **honest single-agent-spine bound held** (the multi-agent orchestration stays the build harness's, not over-claimed — the spawn-class check confirmed `increment` ships no fan-out).

## 2026-06-09 — M16 re-scoped: fuse the planning/completion encode with the working-doc doctype graduation

After M15 shipped (the increment-workflow encode + the `checkpoint` step kind), the human asked whether to handle the deferred planning/completion encode next or do M16. They're **not alternatives**: M16 graduates the methodology's working docs to managed doctypes, and by earn-from-driver each doctype earns its schema from the workflow that *authors* it — those authoring workflows are the **planning and completion workflows**, which M15 deferred. So the planning/completion encode is strictly **upstream of M16** (the increment-workflow M15 *did* encode authors nothing managed — verified). 

**Decision (human-chosen): fuse.** M16 is re-scoped from "working-docs → doctypes" to **"close the self-hosting loop — encode planning/completion + graduate the working-docs they drive,"** building each driver and its doctype in one earn-from-driver motion (the M13 `arch-doc` pattern), rather than encoding the workflows then retrofitting doctypes in a separate milestone. Two halves, likely sliced at planning: **(1) planning** — Settle = the human-gate = the **`checkpoint` kind M15 already built**, so *no new dialect primitive* — + the **roadmap** / **deferral-ledger** doctypes; **(2) completion** — forces the deferred **#5 owner-assigned-artifact gate** (a new dialect primitive) — + the **decisions-log** / completion-record doctype. The honest single-agent-spine bound holds (the multi-agent orchestration stays the build harness's). This settles the M15/M16 fuse-vs-sequence boundary the adoption arc left open. Mirrored in [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16 + [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md). M16 stays adoption-arc prereq #2, ahead of M17 (dogfood + measurement).

## 2026-06-09 — M16 planning: close the self-hosting loop (planning/completion encode + 4 doctypes)

Planned via `/milestone-plan M16` (scope → baseline audit ×4 → 4 gap-detectors → settle → review → decompose). The baseline + gap pass **overturned the roadmap's "earn-from-driver, mirroring M13" framing as too light** — the M13 `arch-doc` analogy breaks three ways (M13's workflow was `creates-task: true`; it was create-only; it had one repeatable level with its only ref in the header). M16's docs break all three. Design-of-record: new [design/methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md). Forks settled (human-chosen):

- **The authoring spine → option D: `creates-task: true, selectable: false`** (the shipped `sub-task` precedent). The crux the gap pass found: a managed doctype is authored only through the **task-scoped** create-gate, and a `creates-task: false` workflow mints no task area (the increment-workflow M15 shipped authors nothing managed — verified). Rather than build a new no-task authoring path (the gap-detectors' A/B/C), planning/completion take `sub-task`'s exact front-matter: mint a task, author via the **proven** create-gate + finalize-promote spine, stay off the router. **Spiked against the real binary (2026-06-09):** `jigc start --workflow sub-task "..."` composes **and** mints a task dir; the existing off-router test pins selectable:false. Near-zero new authoring engine work.
- **Scope → Full-4 doctypes, methodology pack, fresh instances.** `roadmap` + `deferral-ledger` + `decisions-log` + `completion-record`, all schemas in the methodology pack (composes alone — co-composition is M14). Proven on **fresh instances**; jigc's *own* `roadmap.md`/`DECISIONS.md` stay plain markdown until a **v1 migration** (human's direction — evaluate jigc first, migrate when stable). Three are running (cross-milestone, append-maintained); `completion-record` is per-milestone create-fresh.
- **`decisions-log` vs `completion-record` → two distinct doctypes** (running append-only log vs per-milestone audit instance), not one.
- **Roadmap one-level bound** — two-level (milestone→increment) is **not expressible** (`schema.rs` `Leaf` has no `Repeatable` variant, not merely deferred). The roadmap doctype is one level: a milestone entry carries its increment cut as **prose in a `decomposition` slot**. Structured per-increment items wait for multi-level repetition (deferred).
- **B4 → build repeatable-section conformance + ref-edges.** `validate.rs` and `index.rs` both skip repeatable sections; every M16 doctype's payload is repeatable, and per-entry refs are in scope (a `completion-record` finding → `adr`/`spec`). Lift both (validate-layer-only, data present) so a half-authored entry blocks and a dangling per-entry ref is caught — else the "validate against reality" differentiator is vacuous on exactly these docs.
- **B5 → idempotent create** (copy-in on an existing committed slug instead of clobbering). Kills the silent-data-loss clobber **and** gives **create-or-update for free** — the running-doc workflows always "create" then `add-item`, no conditional (barred), no agent branch-judgment.
- **#5 owner-artifact gate → finalize-time presence check.** `exists(recorded-path)` for the named owner-artifact (the Half-B genuine-audit recording, the M8 genuine-spawn sibling), **pure presence, zero content inspection** (reading the bytes = judgment = the FAIL exemplar). Intrinsic (floored blocking) → +1 row across `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` (17→18), both `knobs.yaml` (26→27), `CHECK_INVENTORY`, and the [validation.md](design/validation.md) inventory. Chosen as a *check*, not a step kind (a step kind only emits a directive — it cannot verify at finalize).

**The honest single-agent-spine bound (sharper than M15, recorded).** The planning/completion workflows are *more* multi-agent than the increment-workflow (planning fans out recon + review; completion runs parallel audits + a verdict). jigc composes the single-agent spine — the phase walk, the checkpoints, the #5 presence-gate, the doctype authoring; the fanned recon, the independent review, and the **completion audit verdict** stay orchestration-level (the build harness) and irreducible judgment. Bigger cut than M15's — recorded so the completion audit can't charge it.

**Forward-harness review (mandated, novel off-substrate milestone).** Named failure class M16's green gates could pass: **the vacuously-green managed-doc gate** — a conformance/presence/idempotent-create gate that composes and validates clean while never *firing* (a conformance loop that only sees well-formed `add-item` output; a #5 gate whose recorded-path passes vacuously; an idempotent-create only spiked cold). The build's red obligation: **every new gate fires-and-blocks on deliberately-malformed input before its green test** (hand-malformed repeatable entry; missing owner-artifact; re-author over a drifted committed doc — the M13 cold/warm spike). Baked into every engine increment's Red obligation.

**Stays deferred (logged):** multi-level repetition; in-place migration of jigc's own docs (→ v1); the A==A-oracle lint (re-checked, **does not fire** — no M16 doctype carries a test-source `code-anchor`); `remove-item`/`reorder` (append-only suffices); the required-read-role finalize gate (maintained-doc edit is direct-address `add-item`, no bound read-role).

**Review (design-reviewer + cross-model `/review-codex`).** Independent adversarial pass found 6 valid findings (3 blocking), all accepted + baked into [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md): **B-1** `location: ./` is unbuildable (the reconcile sweep would vacuum every root `.md`) → each running doc gets a dedicated subdir (`roadmap/`/`ledger/`/`decisions-log/`/`completions/`); **B-2** a "running singleton" has no stable slug under `id-from: title` → a net-new `singleton: true` schema flag fixes the slug to the doctype id (idempotent-create's premise); **B-3** the #5 gate's recorded-path home was undesigned → it reads an `owner-artifact` path field on the `completion-record` meta header + an explicit honesty bound (presence-at-named-path, **not** genuineness — the M8 orchestrator-responsibility analogue); **I-1** copy-in doesn't reconcile (drift caught at finalize-preflight, not copy-in — tighten the warm-spike to record-baseline-then-drift); **I-2** idempotent-create modifies the *shared* `create` primitive → gate the committed-copy-in to singleton doctypes so the `single-task` ADR/superseding flow is unchanged; **I-3** per-item ref-edge `from` identity must carry the item fragment (else `absorb_doc` wipes a doc's item-edges) — slightly wider than "validate-layer-only." Net effect: keeps Full-4, makes the running-doc engine weight honest. **Cross-model `/review-codex` then caught 5 more the same-model pass missed (1 blocking), all baked:** the **#5 gate was vacuous** (`exists(arbitrary path)` passes with `README.md`) → `owner-artifact` is now a repo-relative path under an owned home (`completions/artifacts/<milestone>/`), promoted in the same finalize transaction, unsafe paths rejected — durable presence, not any-path; **`decisions-log` driver was wrong** (decisions come from planning Settle too, not just completion) → authored by **both** halves, Flow 19 writes it; **pack-alone conflicts with `completion-record → adr/spec` refs** (dev-pack targets, methodology composes alone) → per-finding reference **downgraded to a `string` evidence field**, so **no M16 doctype carries a managed per-entry ref** and **B4 shrinks to conformance-only** (the `index.rs` ref-edge lift + per-item edge-identity defer to a co-composition milestone); **"fully closed" overclaimed** → softened to "manages fresh instances," + a **two-run warm-append** acceptance demonstrates the running-singleton maintained over time; **"no conditional" reworded** ("deterministic state-dependent write command"). The cross-model pass paid for itself — the #5 vacuity + the pack-alone/ref conflict were load-bearing.

**Acceptance:** [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 19 (planning encode) + flow 20 (completion encode). New design doc [design/methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md), wired into the [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) reading order before `multi-pack` (the terminus). Decomposition below.

## 2026-06-09 — M16 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1 — repeatable-section conformance (the shared validation substrate)](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-1--repeatable-section-conformance-the-shared-validation-substrate) into two ordered, single-concern tasks. This increment is **engine work #1 only** ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work, item 1): lift the `validate.rs` skip past repeatable sections so `schema_conformance` adjudicates each item's leaves. **Ref-edges are OUT** (Codex finding 3 — no M16 doctype carries a per-entry managed ref, so the `index.rs` repeatable-edge lift + per-item edge-identity stay deferred); this is **conformance-only**. *Why two tasks, this order:* the engine lift + its fixture-proven fire-and-pass test is the whole deliverable (T1); the design fold-back the scope's *Updates* line names (validation.md + document-type-schema.md) is a separate doc-only commit (T2, the M13/M15 fold-back pattern). Serial over the shared tree, each one conventional commit. Grounding facts the cut rests on (verified against base `c3e9205`, not assumed):

- **The skip to lift is exact and singular.** `schema_conformance` (`validate.rs:323`) iterates `schema.sections`; for a matched section it `continue`s past any non-`Simple` body (`validate.rs:332–339`, the `let SectionBody::Simple { … } = &section.body else { continue }`). That `else`-arm is the *only* place repeatable sections are dropped from conformance — lifting it is the whole engine change. The four per-leaf helpers it would call are already written and reusable as-is: `check_slot_present`/`check_field`/`check_field_value`/`is_author_required` (`validate.rs:356–450`) + `crate::write::check_value` (the same write-time adjudicator).
- **The parser already records everything the per-item checks need — validate-layer-only, no parser change.** `ParsedItem { id, title, slot: Option<Span>, fields: Vec<Field> }` (`parse.rs:119–130`) carries each item's slot span + per-item fields; the M13 `#section/item/leaf` address vocabulary already exists (`target_surface.rs:249` emits `{ty}:{slug}#{section.id}/{item.id}/{declared.id}` for repeatable-item leaves) — so findings address at `#section/item/leaf` with the proven fragment, no new addressing.
- **The `id-from` exemption is an assumption to PROVE, not trust — and it has a real trap.** The scope says "exempt the `id-from` source field (mirror the `parse.rs` heading-field exclusion)." Verified: `ItemTemplate::from` (`parse.rs:802–824`) already excludes `repeatable.id_from` from `field_keys` (`parse.rs:811`), so the parser renders the id-source field as the `###` heading and **never** puts it into `item.fields`. **The trap:** if the lifted check iterates the schema's `repeatable.block` leaves and runs `required-field-present` on the `id-from` leaf, it looks in `item.fields`, doesn't find it (it's the heading), and **falsely reports a required field missing on every conformant item**. So the check code must skip the `id-from` leaf when iterating the block (mirroring `ItemTemplate::from`). T1's green test proves this: a conformant item with its id-from heading present yields **zero** findings, not a spurious "required field missing."
- **The red obligation needs a purpose-built fixture schema — no shipped doctype carries a required field inside a repeatable item.** `spec.criteria`'s block is `title`(id-from, exempt) + `statement`(slot) + `maps-to-test`(optional `code-anchor`, exempt via `is_author_required`); `arch-doc.components` is the same shape. Neither has a **required typed field** inside the block. So T1 builds a minimal fixture repeatable doctype with a required slot **and** a required enum field inside the block (the inc-4 `note`-schema pattern — a test fixture, not pack content; [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md): "Proven on a fixture repeatable doctype, not yet any methodology pack content"). This is the only way to exercise `required-field-present` + `field-value-conformant` over an item.

- **T1** — Lift the repeatable skip + the fire-and-pass test (the whole engine deliverable). In `schema_conformance` (`validate.rs`), replace the `SectionBody::Repeatable` `continue` with a per-item adjudication: for each `ParsedItem`, iterate the schema `repeatable.block` leaves and run `required-slot-present` (over the item's slot span), `required-field-present` + `field-value-conformant` (over the item's fields), **skipping the `id-from` leaf** (mirror `parse.rs:811`), each finding addressed at `#section/item/leaf` (the M13 fragment). Reuse the existing leaf helpers; extend/parallel them to take `&ParsedItem` (same `slot`/`fields` shape as `&ParsedSection`). *Done:* a unit test over a **fixture repeatable doctype** (built in-test, required slot + required enum field in the block) asserts: **(a)** a fully-conformant repeatable instance yields **zero** findings (proving the `id-from`-heading-present item is not spuriously flagged "required field missing" — the exemption trap); **(b)** the **red obligation fires** — a hand-malformed entry with an empty required slot produces a blocking `schema-conformance.required-slot-present`, and a separate entry with a malformed required field value produces a blocking `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` (the loop *fires*, not merely passes good input — the vacuously-green guard); **(c)** the existing simple-section conformance tests + `validate_task` sweep still pass (no regression on the `Simple` path). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + full `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/validate.rs`. *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work (item 1); [validation.md](design/validation.md) → schema-conformance scope; [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → the vacuously-green guard. *Notes:* validate-layer-only (parser data already present); ref-edges OUT (conformance-only) — do **not** touch `index.rs`; the `id-from` skip is the load-bearing assumption proven by (a), not asserted.
- **T2** — Design fold-back (doc-only). Update [validation.md](design/validation.md) → the `schema-conformance` scope / "What intrinsic means" so it states the four checks now adjudicate **repeatable** sections per item (the MVP repeatable-skip is lifted), and [document-type-schema.md](design/document-type-schema.md) → near the repeatable-section item-template (≈line 170) so the MVP limit being lifted is recorded as lifted. Strike the now-stale in-code "out of MVP conformance scope" framing the design implied. *Done:* both docs read consistently with the shipped T1 behavior (repeatable conformance is in scope, conformance-only, `id-from` exempt, ref-edges deferred); no code touched; `cargo fmt --check` n/a (doc-only). *Files:* `design/validation.md`, `design/document-type-schema.md`. *Refs:* the increment's *Updates* line ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16 Increment 1 Proves). *Notes:* separate `design(...)` commit from T1's `feat(...)`, matching the M13/M15 fold-back discipline.

Every *Grouped scope* bullet maps: bullet 1 (lift the `validate.rs` skip, run the three checks per item over each block leaf, exempt the `id-from` field) → **T1**; bullet 2 (**ref-edges OUT** — `index.rs` untouched, conformance-only) → a constraint honored across **both** tasks (T1 touches no `index.rs`; T2 records the deferral), not a deliverable to build; bullet 3 (the red obligation — a hand-malformed entry produces a blocking finding) → **T1**'s done-criterion (b), in the same task as the lift because the scope names it as part of *this* deliverable, not a separable concern. The *Updates* line (validation.md + document-type-schema.md) → **T2**. No grouped-scope bullet is narrowed or punted. **No genuine new fork surfaced** — every shape maps to the settled M16 decisions (2026-06-09 → M16 planning: B4 shrinks to conformance-only, ref-edges deferred) and the locked [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) engine-work-1 spec; the one load-bearing pin (the `id-from`-leaf exemption inside the check, whose omission would spuriously flag every conformant item) is a **T1 assumption to prove**, not a trusted claim. Cross-references [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16 Increment 1.

## 2026-06-09 — M16 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 2 — `singleton` doctypes + idempotent create (the running-doc substrate)](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-2--singleton-doctypes--idempotent-create-the-running-doc-substrate) into three ordered, single-concern tasks. This increment is **engine work #2** ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work, item 2): a net-new `singleton: true` schema flag fixes a doctype's slug to the type id, and `create` on an **already-committed** singleton slug copies-in the committed doc instead of clobbering it — the create-or-update mechanism the running docs rest on. *Why this order:* the `singleton` flag + its fixed-slug minting is the data + identity premise both later tasks name (T1); the idempotent-`create` decision (committed-collision → copy-in, gated to singleton so non-singleton keeps mint-or-reject) is the engine behavior change that rides that flag (T2); the CLI wiring + the real-binary cold/warm/drift acceptance over a fixture singleton doctype proves the whole substrate end-to-end (T3). Serial over the shared tree, each one conventional commit. The forward-review red obligation (every gate fires-and-blocks before its green test — the *vacuously-green managed-doc gate* class) + the M13 cold-start discipline (spike the empty/cold state) are baked into T2 and T3. Grounding facts the cut rests on (verified against base `c3e9205` + the landed Increment-1 commits, tree clean at `2226d39`, not assumed):

- **The `singleton` flag is a clean additive `Schema` field.** `Schema` (`schema.rs:30`) is `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` with top-level `ty`/`location`/`id_from`/`description`/`usage`/`sections`; adding `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")] pub singleton: bool` mirrors the existing `header: bool` skip-on-false discipline (`schema.rs:82`) — so a schema omitting it leaves every existing golden untouched (no shipped schema declares `singleton`). The serde-roundtrip golden tests (`schema.rs:495+`) pin the projection; a `singleton`-bearing fixture schema is the new coverage.
- **The fixed-slug seam is in `create` (the slug derivation), not the router.** Today `create` (`state.rs:553`) derives the slug via `mint_id(id_source, type_name)` (`state.rs:423` — slugify the source, type-name fallback on empty). For a `singleton` schema the slug must be **the type id unconditionally** (`schema.ty`), *not* the `id-from`/title source — so a re-`create` deterministically targets the same `<location>/<ty>.md`. `singleton` is orthogonal to the `selectable`/`creates_task` router filter (that gates workflow visibility, not doc identity) — no router change.
- **`create`/`create_gated` only check the WORKING-AREA path — the committed-store collision the idempotent path needs is detected at the CLI, which holds `repo_root`.** Engine `create(task_dir, schemas, type_name, id_source)` (`state.rs:553`) takes **no `repo_root`** — its collision check is `path.exists()` over the working-area `instance_path` only (`state.rs:570`). The committed-store lookup (`engine::store::canonical_path(repo_root, schema, slug)` + `is_file()` + read, `store.rs:43`) lives at the CLI, exactly as the proven `read_or_copy_in` (`doc.rs:373`) already does for `set-slot`/`set-field`/`add-item` — its case-2 branch (`doc.rs:387–395`) reads the committed body and calls `state::copy_in`. So the idempotent-create seam is **CLI `run_create` (`doc.rs:275`) resolving the committed singleton + routing to copy-in**, paralleling `read_or_copy_in`, with the engine carrying the singleton-aware slug logic — but the **exact signature shape (engine gains a copy-in-or-mint helper that the CLI feeds the committed body, vs. CLI detects-then-copies-in around `create_gated`) is a T2 assumption to PROVE against the code, not a trusted pin** — whichever seam keeps `create_gated`'s gate/role-binding (`state.rs:595–622`) intact and reuses `state::copy_in` (`state.rs:240`, which records `edited-from-base` + applies `first_touch_canonicalize`).
- **Gating copy-in to `singleton` is the load-bearing regression guard (review finding I-2).** `create` is a *shared* primitive: the `single-task` ADR/superseding flow expects a committed-slug collision to **reject** (mint-or-reject), and `superseding_decision.rs` (`crates/cli/tests/`) pins it. The copy-in branch MUST key on the `singleton` flag — a non-singleton `create` on a committed slug keeps its current mint-or-reject `create.serial-collision` behavior (`state.rs:570`, `instance_collision_finding`) unchanged. T2's done-criterion proves both arms: singleton committed-collision → copy-in; non-singleton committed-collision → unchanged reject.
- **The warm-drift conflict-block rides EXISTING finalize-preflight machinery — copy-in does not itself reconcile (review finding I-1).** `copy_in` reads the committed body directly; OOB drift over a committed singleton is caught at finalize-preflight by `reconcile_committed_store` → DRIFTED+TOUCHED `reconciliation.conflict-block` (`file_state.rs:251`, `:196–197`, exemplar test `oob_conflict_blocks` `:749`). So T3's warm-drift spike adds no reconcile code — it **records the baseline first**, then OOB-edits the committed doc, then asserts finalize conflict-blocks (an unrecorded-baseline drift baseline-*adopts* vacuously — the spike must record-baseline-first or it proves nothing). Confirm `first_touch_canonicalize` (`write.rs`, applied by `copy_in` at `state.rs:247`) is a **no-op on an already-canonical** committed doc so the first warm edit doesn't perturb bytes.
- **The binary acceptance uses the proven fixture-pack mechanism — no methodology pack content yet.** `JIGC_PACK_DIR` selects a filesystem fixture pack UNIONED with the embedded dev base (`flow18_acceptance.rs:13,123,137,463`); the `add-item` CLI verb (`doc.rs:243`) already rides `read_or_copy_in`, so the warm-append (copy-in committed singleton → `add-item` appends → re-promote) is exercised through the shipped verb. T3 seeds a **fixture singleton doctype** (own `location:` subdir, a repeatable section so `add-item` has a target) + a `creates-task: true` fixture workflow that allows-creates it — a test fixture, not pack content ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md): "proven on a fixture singleton doctype").

- **T1** — The `singleton: true` schema flag + fixed-slug minting (the identity premise). Add `pub singleton: bool` to `Schema` (`schema.rs`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]`, mirroring `header`); in `create` (`state.rs`), when the resolved schema is `singleton`, derive the slug as `schema.ty` (the type id, unconditional) instead of `mint_id(id_source, …)` — so a singleton always mints/targets `<location>/<ty>.md`. Non-singleton `create` is unchanged. *Done:* **(a)** a serde-roundtrip unit test over a fixture `singleton: true` schema asserts the flag parses and re-serializes (and that an existing non-singleton schema golden is byte-unchanged — the additive-field guard); **(b)** an engine unit test asserts `create` on a fresh `singleton` schema mints at slug `=` the type id regardless of the `id_source` passed (a non-empty title does **not** change the slug), while `create` on a non-singleton schema still slugs the source. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + full `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/schema.rs`, `crates/engine/src/state.rs`. *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The four doctypes (the singleton/fixed-slug premise, review B-2); [document-type-schema.md](design/document-type-schema.md). *Notes:* identity-only — no copy-in behavior yet (that is T2); `singleton` is orthogonal to the router `selectable` filter — do not touch `selectable_workflows`.
- **T2** — Idempotent `create`: committed-singleton collision → copy-in, gated to `singleton` (the create-or-update engine behavior + the shared-primitive regression guard). Route a `create` on an **already-committed** `singleton` slug through the `copy_in` path (read the committed `<location>/<ty>.md`, copy it into the working area recording `edited-from-base`) instead of minting blank or rejecting; **gate this branch on the `singleton` flag** so a non-singleton committed-slug collision keeps its unchanged mint-or-reject `create.serial-collision` semantics. The exact seam (engine helper fed the committed body by the CLI vs. CLI-side detect-then-copy-in around `create_gated`, paralleling `read_or_copy_in`) is **proven against the code, not assumed** — it must keep `create_gated`'s gate-check + `as:`-role binding intact and reuse `state::copy_in`. *Done:* **(a)** the cold case — `create` of a `singleton` with **no** committed instance mints the empty instance (round-trips byte-stable through `write::render`); **(b)** the warm case — `create` of a `singleton` whose `<location>/<ty>.md` **is** committed copies the committed body in (records `edited-from-base`, the staged body equals `first_touch_canonicalize` of the committed source — no clobber, prior content preserved); **(c)** the **regression guard fires** — a non-singleton `create` on a committed slug still returns the unchanged blocking `create.serial-collision` (mint-or-reject unchanged), proving the gate is real not global; **(d)** `crates/cli/tests/superseding_decision.rs` (the `single-task` ADR/superseding flow) still passes unchanged. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + full `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/state.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs` (the seam landing site, per the proven assumption). *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work (item 2 — the B5 fix, copy-in gated to singleton, review I-2); [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → the vacuously-green guard + M13 cold-start. *Notes:* copy-in does **not** reconcile (review I-1 — drift is T3's finalize-preflight concern); no *workflow* conditional and no agent branch — `create` is a deterministic state-dependent write command (Codex finding 5).
- **T3** — The CLI wiring + the real-binary cold/warm/drift acceptance over a fixture singleton doctype (the substrate proven end-to-end). Seed (via `JIGC_PACK_DIR`, the flow18 mechanism) a fixture pack with a `singleton: true` fixture doctype (its **own** `location:` subdir, a repeatable section as the `add-item` target) + a `creates-task: true` fixture workflow allowing-create of it; drive the whole loop through the shipped binary. *Done:* an acceptance test in a throwaway repo asserts: **(a) cold-create round-trips** — `jigc start --workflow <fixture> "<intent>"` → `jigc doc create <singleton>` → author → `finalize` promotes `<location>/<ty>.md`, byte-stable; **(b) warm re-create copies-in + appends + re-promotes byte-stable** — a second task `jigc doc create <singleton>` (the slug now committed) copies-in the committed doc, `jigc doc add-item …` appends one entry, `finalize` re-promotes — the prior content is preserved and the bytes are stable (`first_touch_canonicalize` a no-op on the already-canonical committed doc); **(c) baseline-recorded-then-OOB-drifted warm edit conflict-blocks** — record the file-state baseline, OOB-edit the committed `<location>/<ty>.md`, touch it via the task, then `finalize`/preflight **blocks** with `reconciliation.conflict-block` (the spike records the baseline FIRST — an unrecorded drift adopts vacuously); **(d)** the `single-task` ADR/superseding flow regression-passes unchanged (re-assert at the binary, the I-2 guard). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + full `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/cli/tests/` (a new acceptance test, fixture-pack-seeded). *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → Acceptance flows (the running-singleton-maintained-over-time bar, Codex finding 4); [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → the state machine; [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → cold-start spike + the determinism-by-re-execution byte-stability discipline. *Notes:* drift rides existing `reconcile_committed_store` machinery (review I-1) — add no reconcile code; the fixture doctype is a test fixture, never methodology pack content (that is increments 4–5).

Every *Grouped scope* bullet maps: bullet 1 (the `singleton: true` flag → fixed-slug minting, slug = type id, review B-2) → **T1**; bullet 2 (idempotent `create` — committed-collision → `copy_in` path, **gated to singleton** so non-singleton keeps mint-or-reject, review I-2) → **T2**; bullet 3 (each running doctype its **own** `location:` subdir — review B-1 — and copy-in reads the committed doc directly, drift caught at finalize-preflight not copy-in, review I-1) → the own-`location:` subdir is exercised in **T3**'s fixture doctype (a per-doctype property the fixture sets, proven by the cold/warm round-trips landing under it), and the drift-at-preflight-not-copy-in is **T2**'s no-reconcile-in-copy-in design + **T3**'s done-criterion (c); bullet 4 (the red obligation + cold/warm/drift spike, M13 cold-start — cold round-trips, warm preserves + re-promotes byte-stable, warm-drift records baseline first, `single-task` regression holds) → split deliberately and tracked: the **engine-layer** cold/warm + regression spike is **T2** (b)/(c)/(d); the **binary-layer** cold/warm/drift + regression acceptance is **T3** (a)–(d) — the spike lands across T2 (engine) and T3 (binary) by design, named in both so the punt is tracked to its landing, never left to "a later task." No grouped-scope bullet is narrowed or punted to a later increment. **No genuine new fork surfaced** — every shape maps to the settled M16 decisions (2026-06-09 → M16 planning: B-2 singleton flag, I-2 gate-copy-in-to-singleton, I-1 drift-at-preflight, B-1 own-location) and the locked [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) engine-work-2 spec; the one genuinely open elaboration (the exact engine/CLI copy-in seam) is a **T2 assumption to prove against the code**, not a trusted pin (the M3 "mirrors `adr`" / "zero engine change" lesson). Cross-references [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16 Increment 2.

**T2 landed — the copy-in seam resolved (engine-fed, not CLI-side detect-then-copy).** The assumption-to-prove settled toward **threading `repo_root` into `engine::state::create`/`create_gated`** so the engine itself detects the committed-singleton collision and routes to `state::copy_in` — *not* a CLI-side detect-around-`create_gated` paralleling `read_or_copy_in`. Rationale found in the code: `create_gated`'s gate-check + `as:`-role binding already live in the engine, and the copy-in decision keys on `schema.singleton` (engine-owned) + the committed `store::canonical_path` (engine-owned), so the whole state-dependent decision belongs in `create` next to the working-area collision check it complements — the CLI just passes `task.repo_root` (already a field). The copy-in branch is **after** the working-area collision (step 3): a singleton already copied-in still serial-rejects on re-create, so a prior staged edit survives (the same steady-state guard `read_or_copy_in` relies on). Gated to `singleton` (review I-2): a non-singleton committed-slug `create` mints fresh then serial-rejects on re-create, **unchanged** — the `single-task` ADR/superseding flow regression-passes (`crates/cli/tests/superseding_decision.rs` green). Copy-in does **not** reconcile (review I-1) — it reads the committed body directly; `first_touch_canonicalize` is a no-op on an already-canonical committed doc (the warm-test asserts `staged == committed` byte-for-byte). Files: `crates/engine/src/state.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`.

## 2026-06-09 — M16 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 3 — the #5 owner-artifact presence gate (the completion-half engine primitive)](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-3--the-5-owner-artifact-presence-gate-the-completion-half-engine-primitive) into three ordered, single-concern tasks. This increment is **engine work #3** ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work, item 3): a finalize-time **intrinsic** check that reads the `owner-artifact` *owned-location path* field on a completion-record-shaped doc and asserts the named artifact is durably staged under the owned home (`completions/artifacts/<milestone>/…`), blocking on absent/unsafe/untracked and passing on a real durably-staged artifact — **presence, never the artifact's bytes** (the determinism boundary; the FAIL exemplar is a check that reads content). *Why this order:* the engine must first be able to **recognize** the owner-artifact field without pack content — a net-new **engine-native** `FieldType` is how the intrinsic gate keys on the field (the `code-anchor`→`doc-code` precedent, but engine-native since the gate is intrinsic, not a pack probe) (T1); the gate itself (path-safety + presence + tracked) then rides on that field-type recognition and is proven fire-and-block on a fixture doctype (T2); the four-list severity sync (`INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` 17→18, **both** packs' `knobs.yaml` 26→27, `CHECK_INVENTORY`, [validation.md](design/validation.md)) registers the new intrinsic key as floored-blocking (T3). Serial over the shared tree, each one conventional commit. The forward-review red obligation (the gate fires-and-blocks on deliberately-bad input before its green test — the *vacuously-green managed-doc gate* class; Codex blocking-1) is baked into T2. Grounding facts the cut rests on (verified against base `c3e9205` + the landed Increment 1–2 commits, tree clean at `b4720a1`, not assumed):

- **The gate is engine-native intrinsic, NOT a pack probe.** `code-anchor` is a *pack*-declared `FieldType::Pack` bound to the `doc-code` *subprocess* probe (tunable, in `CHECK_INVENTORY` but never floored, engine ships no adjudicator). The owner-artifact gate is the opposite: [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → engine work 3 makes it **floored-blocking intrinsic** (`INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` 17→18). So the field the gate keys on must be **engine-recognizable** without pack content — i.e. a **new native `FieldType`** (spelling `owned-location`), added to `FieldType::NATIVE` (`schema.rs:272`), not a `FieldType::Pack`. This is the "field-validation … is the net-new surface (real, not assumed-reusable)" the design names.
- **`validate_task` is the single fire site — finalize blocks automatically (one engine, two entry points).** `plan_finalize` (`finalize.rs:159`) phase-2 returns the blocking findings of the `ValidationReport` the CLI hands it (`finalize.rs:178`, built by `validate()` at `task.rs:398`); there is **no private finalize-only check path** (`finalize.md` → 2. Validate). So the gate must emit its `Finding` **inside `engine::validate::validate_task`** (`validate.rs:134`) — then `task validate` previews it and `finalize` blocks on it, with zero new finalize wiring. `validate_task` already carries `dir` (the task working area), `schemas`, and **`repo_root`** (`validate.rs:138`) — the owned-home root the presence check needs.
- **File existence is engine-side (`repo_root`); the "untracked → block" half needs a CLI-supplied git query (the `doc-code` invoker precedent).** The artifact lives in the **real repo working tree** under `completions/artifacts/<milestone>/…` (a repo-relative path the field names), NOT in the task `docs/` staging area — so `exists(repo_root.join(path))` is an engine filesystem read. But "untracked" is git knowledge the **engine is shell-free** about (the CLI owns `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` via `git_untracked`, `task.rs:778`; tracked-status is its complement). So `validate_task` gains a **CLI-supplied tracked-status query** threaded exactly like `invoke_doc_code: &ProbeInvoker` (`validate.rs:142`, the engine-stays-shell-free seam) — the engine decides the finding, the CLI answers "is this path tracked/staged?". The **exact closure shape** (a `Fn(&Path)->bool` tracked predicate vs. a pre-computed tracked-path set handed in) is a **T2 assumption to PROVE against the code**, not a trusted pin — whichever keeps the engine shell-free and reuses the existing `git_untracked`/`git ls-files` surface.
- **Path-safety + presence + tracked are ONE intrinsic finding key, not split across `field-value-conformant`.** The static path-shape rejections (absolute, `..`, out-of-repo) *could* ride the existing `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` check (`validate.rs:520`, via `write::check_value`), but the filesystem-dependent half (symlink-escape resolution, presence, tracked-status) cannot — and the design treats the gate as **one** check emitting **one** intrinsic key (the "blocks on absent/unsafe/untracked" is a single bar). So the new native `owned-location` type is **exempt from `field-value-conformant`** (its *adjudication* is the new gate, mirroring how `is_author_required` at `validate.rs:545` exempts `FieldType::Pack` and optional `ref` — "presence/adjudication is the finalize-time probe's job"), and ALL of path-safety + presence + tracked is the new `owner-artifact.present` check. This keeps the gate a single floored-blocking key with one severity, not a behavior smeared across two check ids.
- **Proven on a FIXTURE doctype — `completion-record` does not exist until Increment 5.** The roadmap deliverable says "proven on a fixture"; the `completion-record` schema + its `owner-artifact` field land in Increment 5. So T2 seeds a **fixture doctype** carrying an `owned-location` field (the inc-1/inc-2 fixture-pack precedent, `JIGC_PACK_DIR` unioned with the embedded base, `flow18_acceptance.rs:13`) and proves the gate against it — never methodology pack content (that is Increment 5, which wires the real completion-record onto this gate).
- **The four-list sync is load-bearing, not cosmetic — both packs' `knobs.yaml` MUST gain the key or pack-load aborts.** `load_knobs` asserts every `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` entry is **declared + floored-blocking** in the pack's `knobs.yaml` (`knobs.rs:211`, `UndeclaredIntrinsic`/`UnflooredIntrinsic`). Both packs exist on disk and each declares **26** per-check `validation.*.*.severity` rows today: the embedded dev pack (`crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml`) and the sibling methodology pack (`packs/methodology/config/knobs.yaml`, verified 26). Adding the 18th intrinsic key to `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` **without** declaring it in *both* knobs.yaml files makes pack-load fail — so T3's "both packs 26→27" is a hard requirement the engine enforces, and the `per_check_severity_surface_reconciles_to_the_26_17_9_inventory` test (`knobs.rs:577`) flips to 27/18/9.
- **`CHECK_INVENTORY` (the post-pass membership set) gets the row — UNLIKE the M15 checkpoint marker.** The M15 `checkpoint-marker-not-shadowed` key joined `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` + the knobs enum but was deliberately **kept out** of `CHECK_INVENTORY` (`result.rs:173`) because it is a **compose-time** marker check, not a task-validate/finalize check (`knobs.rs:616` pins this). The owner-artifact gate is the opposite — it fires at **task-validate/finalize**, so it **does** join `CHECK_INVENTORY` (so the severity post-pass `assign_severity` at `result.rs:217` can honor a `scalar-set` against it). This is the one place the new key's list membership diverges from its M15 sibling.

- **T1** — The engine-native `owned-location` `FieldType` (the field-recognition substrate). Add a native variant (spelling `owned-location`) to `FieldType::NATIVE` (`schema.rs:272`) + its `as_str` arm (`schema.rs:282`), and **exempt it from `is_author_required`** (`validate.rs:545`) and from `field-value-conformant` adjudication (its presence/path-validity is the new gate's job, not value-conformance — the `FieldType::Pack` exemption precedent) — so a fixture schema declaring an `owned-location` field loads, round-trips, and does **not** false-fail conformance on a present-or-absent value. *Done:* **(a)** a serde-roundtrip unit test over a fixture schema with an `owned-location` field asserts the type parses to the new native variant and re-serializes to the bare `owned-location` spelling (and every existing native-type golden is byte-unchanged — the additive guard); **(b)** an engine unit test asserts `schema_conformance` over an instance carrying an `owned-location` field emits **no** `field-value-conformant`/`required-field-present` finding for that field regardless of its value (the gate, not conformance, adjudicates it). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + full `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/schema.rs`, `crates/engine/src/validate.rs`. *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work (item 3 — the owned-location field is the net-new recognition surface); [document-type-schema.md](design/document-type-schema.md) → native field types. *Notes:* recognition only — no presence/path-safety logic yet (that is T2); engine-native (`NATIVE`), **not** `FieldType::Pack`, because the gate keying on it is intrinsic.
- **T2** — The owner-artifact presence gate (path-safety + presence + tracked, fire-and-block on a fixture). Add an `owner-artifact.present` check inside `engine::validate::validate_task` (`validate.rs:134`): for the staged instance whose schema carries an `owned-location` field, read the field string and emit a **blocking** `owner-artifact.present` `Finding` when the path is (i) absent/empty, (ii) unsafe — absolute, contains `..`, escapes the repo via symlink, or resolves out-of-repo, (iii) not under the owned home `completions/artifacts/<milestone>/`, or (iv) present-but-untracked; pass (no finding) when the artifact is durably staged/committed under the owned home. The engine reads existence under `repo_root`; the **tracked-status answer is supplied by the CLI** via a closure threaded like `invoke_doc_code` (the engine-shell-free seam — `task.rs:375` is the wire site, the CLI builds the predicate from `git_untracked`/`git ls-files`). The exact closure signature is **proven against the code, not assumed**. **Never read the artifact's bytes** (presence, not content — the determinism boundary). *Done:* an engine/CLI test over a **fixture** doctype with an `owned-location` field asserts the gate **fires (blocks)** on each of: absent path, absolute path, `..`-containing path, symlink-escape, out-of-repo target, and present-but-untracked target; and **passes** on a path durably staged under `completions/artifacts/<milestone>/` — proving fire-and-block, not a vacuous always-pass (Codex blocking-1). The finding is engine-emitted so a `finalize` over the fixture **blocks** on the absent case and **lands** on the staged case (one engine, two entry points — the `plan_finalize` phase-2 gate). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + full `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/validate.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs` (the tracked-status closure wiring), `crates/cli/tests/` (the fixture-pack acceptance). *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work (item 3 + the recording-surface/anti-vacuity statement, review B-3 + Codex blocking-1); [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) → the spawn-class third audit artifact (the genuineness stays orchestration-level); [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → the vacuously-green guard. *Notes:* the gate proves **presence-at-owned-path, NOT genuineness** — the orchestrator writes both the field and the file, so authenticity stays an orchestration-level recorded responsibility (the M8 orchestrator-responsibility analogue), recorded here so the completion audit can't charge it as a finding; proven on a fixture (the real `completion-record` rides this gate in Increment 5).
- **T3** — The four-list severity sync (register the new intrinsic key, floored-blocking). Add `validation.owner-artifact.present.severity` to `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` (`knobs.rs:51`, 17→18); declare it `default: blocking` + `floor: blocking` in **both** `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml` and `packs/methodology/config/knobs.yaml` (26→27 per-check rows each); add `("owner-artifact", "present")` to `CHECK_INVENTORY` (`result.rs:173` — a task-validate/finalize check, unlike the M15 compose-time marker); and update the [validation.md](design/validation.md) Severity inventory (the declared single source of truth) to **27 checks / 18 intrinsic / 9 tunable** with the new row. *Done:* **(a)** the `per_check_severity_surface_reconciles_to_the_26_17_9_inventory` reconciliation test (`knobs.rs:577`) is updated to 27/18/9 and passes over **both** packs' embedded/on-disk bytes; **(b)** both packs load without `UndeclaredIntrinsic`/`UnflooredIntrinsic` (the load-time assertion at `knobs.rs:211` holds for the new key); **(c)** a unit test asserts the new key's list membership matches its intrinsic-but-finalize-scoped profile — present in `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` + the knobs enum (floored blocking) **and** in `CHECK_INVENTORY` (the divergence from the M15 checkpoint sibling, which is absent from `CHECK_INVENTORY`); **(d)** [validation.md](design/validation.md) reads 27/18/9. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` + full `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/knobs.rs`, `crates/engine/src/result.rs`, `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml`, `packs/methodology/config/knobs.yaml`, `design/validation.md`. *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The engine work (item 3 — the severity-list sync); [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Severity inventory; the M15 three-list-sync discipline + the four-list reconciliation. *Notes:* the new key is a **task-validate/finalize** check → it joins `CHECK_INVENTORY` (unlike M15's compose-time `checkpoint-marker-not-shadowed`, deliberately excluded — `knobs.rs:616`); both knobs.yaml files MUST gain the key or pack-load aborts (the assertion is load-bearing, not cosmetic).

Every *Grouped scope* bullet maps: bullet 1 (the check — validate `owner-artifact` is a repo-relative path under the owned home, finalize promotes/stages it in the same transaction, then assert durable presence reading the field string + file presence, **never bytes**) → the field recognition is **T1**, the path-safety + same-transaction-staged presence assertion is **T2** (the staged-under-owned-home pass case proves the transactional-at-finalize landing, since the gate fires inside the `validate_task` the `plan_finalize` transaction gates on); bullet 2 (severity-list sync — the new intrinsic key across `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` 17→18, both packs' `knobs.yaml` 26→27, `CHECK_INVENTORY`, the [validation.md](design/validation.md) Severity inventory — the four-list reconciliation) → **T3**; bullet 3 (the red obligation — the gate **fires** on absent/unsafe/untracked and **passes** on durably-staged; the honest bound: presence-at-owned-path, **not** genuineness, the M8 orchestrator-responsibility analogue) → **T2**'s done-criterion (fire-and-block on all bad cases, pass on staged) + the honest-bound note recorded in T2. No grouped-scope bullet is narrowed or punted to a later increment. **No genuine new fork surfaced** — every shape maps to the settled M16 decisions (2026-06-09 → M16 planning: the #5 gate's owned-location promotion, the engine-native intrinsic check, the presence-not-genuineness honesty bound) and the locked [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) engine-work-3 spec; the two genuinely-open elaborations (the native-vs-pack field-type form; the exact CLI tracked-status closure seam) are resolved here toward the invariant-respecting form (engine-native because the gate is intrinsic; CLI-supplied query because the engine is shell-free) and the closure's precise shape is a **T2 assumption to prove against the code**, not a trusted pin (the M3 "mirrors `adr`" / "zero engine change" lesson). Cross-references [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16 Increment 3.

**T2 landed — the #5 owner-artifact presence gate, with the tracked-status seam resolved.** The assumption-to-prove settled toward a **`Fn(&str) -> bool` tracked predicate** (`engine::validate::TrackedPredicate`, repo-relative path in → tracked-bool out) threaded into `validate_task` exactly like `invoke_doc_code` — *not* a pre-computed path set, because the gate consults at most one path per `owned-location` leaf and the predicate keeps the engine shell-free while reusing the existing `git_untracked` surface (the CLI builds it as the complement of `git ls-files --others`). The gate lives in `engine::validate::owner_artifact_present` (one per-instance sweep in `validate_task`, alongside `file-state`/`schema-conformance`), emitting **one blocking `owner-artifact.present`** finding (not in `CHECK_INVENTORY` — so T3 registers it; until then the emitted Blocking severity survives the post-pass untouched). Path-safety + presence + tracked are one check: reject empty/absolute/`..`-containing, reject not-under `completions/artifacts/` (the engine-encoded owned-home root — a structural location the intrinsic gate owns, *not* domain content, since `owned-location` is engine-native), reject symlink-escape (canonicalize → must stay under `<repo>/completions/artifacts/`), reject absent, reject untracked; pass only on a durably-staged-under-home tracked artifact. **Never reads the artifact's bytes** (presence, not content — the determinism boundary). An omitted `owned-location` field is **inert** (the omitting-context guard, proven with a tracked-predicate that panics if consulted). Honest bound (recorded so the completion audit can't charge it): the gate proves **presence-at-owned-path, NOT genuineness** — the orchestrator writes both field and file, so authenticity stays orchestration-level (the M8 analogue). Proven on a **fixture** doctype (engine unit tests over all 6 fire cases + the staged pass + the omitted-inert path + a `validate_task`→`plan_finalize` phase-2 block/land integration; a CLI fixture-pack acceptance over the real binary asserting `finalize` blocks on absent and lands on a `git add`ed artifact under the owned home, both committed together). The real `completion-record` rides this gate in Increment 5. Files: `crates/engine/src/validate.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/owner_artifact_gate.rs`.

## 2026-06-09 — M16 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut the planning-half increment (Deliverable: `jigc start --workflow planning "<milestone>"` mints an off-router task, composes the planning spine with the **Settle checkpoint**, authors a `roadmap` milestone entry + `deferral-ledger` + `decisions-log` entries via idempotent-create + `add-item`/`set-slot`/`set-field`, and `finalize` promotes the three running singletons — proven end-to-end across **two** milestone runs = [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) flow 19) into five ordered, single-concern tasks. *Grounding (verified against base `c3e9205`, not assumed):* this increment is **pure pack data + e2e/honesty tests — zero `crates/*/src` change** — because the substrate the doctypes and workflow need was shipped end-to-end in Increments 1–3 and **spiked against the real binary on a fixture** (`crates/cli/tests/singleton_running_doc.rs`): `singleton: true` fixed-slug create (`engine::schema` flag + `engine::state` mint), idempotent `create` copy-in **gated to singleton** (the non-singleton ADR path stays mint-or-reject), per-item **repeatable-section conformance** (`validate.rs` runs `required-slot-present`/`required-field-present`/`field-value-conformant` per item, `id-from` exempt — so a half-authored entry already blocks), the `owner-artifact.present` knob, `set: on-create` date derivation (proven via `adr`), item-leaf `set-field`/`set-slot` authoring (proven via `arch-doc` `#components/<id>/implemented-by`), `selectable: false` off-router parsing + the catalog filter, multi-type `allows-create` (`Vec<AllowsCreate>`, proven via `sub-task`), and the `checkpoint: {reason: <slug>}` step kind emitting `Checkpoint: <slug>` (M15). So `singleton_running_doc.rs` is the **exact template** flow 19 follows — swap the `runlog` fixture doctype for the three real methodology doctypes and the `keep-runlog` fixture workflow for the real `planning` workflow. The cut mirrors the M12-Inc-1 / M16-Inc-3 pure-pack-data pattern, serial over the shared tree, each one conventional commit. *Why this order:* schemas first (the authoring targets), then the workflow that authors them, then the falsifiable build-honesty/off-router guards over the now-shipped pack bytes, then the e2e that drives all of it through the real binary, then the doc fold-back (the M13/M15 separate-commit discipline).

- **T1** — The three running-doc schemas (pure pack data). Add `packs/methodology/schemas/{roadmap,deferral-ledger,decisions-log}.yaml`, each `singleton: true` with its **own** `location:` subdir (review B-1: `roadmap/`, `ledger/`, `decisions-log/`) and **single-word section ids** (the multi-word reparse defect routed around, as `adr`/`arch-doc`). Shapes per [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The four doctypes: `roadmap` = one repeatable `milestones` section, entry = title (`id-from: title`) + `proves` slot + `decomposition` slot (increments-as-prose, the one-level bound); `deferral-ledger` = one repeatable `entries`, entry = title + `kind` enum (`of: [D, I]`) + `trigger` string + `date` (`type: date, set: on-create`) + `body` slot; `decisions-log` = one repeatable `entries`, entry = title + `date` (`set: on-create`) + `why` slot. **No managed per-entry `ref`** (the pack-composes-alone bound — Codex finding 3); `trigger` is a plain string. *Done:* a CLI test (`crates/cli/tests/methodology_running_doctypes.rs`, mirroring the `methodology_pack_*` fixture-harness) loads the methodology pack through the real binary and asserts each doctype's `describe`/schema projection carries `singleton: true`, its own `location:`, the repeatable section, and the declared leaves (incl. the `kind` enum members + the `date`-`set: on-create` fields) — `cargo test` green; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` n/a (data only, but run). *Files:* `packs/methodology/schemas/roadmap.yaml`, `packs/methodology/schemas/deferral-ledger.yaml`, `packs/methodology/schemas/decisions-log.yaml`, `crates/cli/tests/methodology_running_doctypes.rs`. *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The four doctypes (the singleton/own-location/single-word-id shapes); `crates/cli/pack/schemas/{adr,arch-doc}.yaml` (the section-id + repeatable + `set: on-create` precedents); `crates/cli/tests/singleton_running_doc.rs` (the fixture this generalizes). *Assumption to prove (not a trusted claim):* T1's test must **exercise the exact new shape** — load all three real schemas through the binary and assert the singleton flag + own-location + repeatable-leaf set parse, rather than trusting "mirrors the `runlog` fixture"; the fixture proved the *flag's mechanism*, not these three YAML files. *Notes:* `as`-role names for T2's create-gate are fixed here implicitly by the type ids (`roadmap`/`deferral-ledger`/`decisions-log`).

- **T2** — The `planning` workflow + its phase-walk steps (pure pack data). Add `packs/methodology/workflows/planning.yaml` (`creates-task: true`, `selectable: false`, `allows-create: [{type: roadmap, as: roadmap}, {type: deferral-ledger, as: ledger}, {type: decisions-log, as: log}]`) including ordered steps for the **phase walk** (`scope` / `detect-gaps` / `settle` / `review` / `decompose` as Reason prose) + the **doc-authoring** steps (idempotent-create + `add-item`/`set-slot`/`set-field` over the three doctypes + the commit doc) + the methodology `finalize` step. The **Settle** step is `checkpoint: {reason: settle}` — the M15 primitive, **no new dialect work**. The judgment phases (`detect-gaps`, `settle`, `review`) stay **pure agent-judgment prose** — no gap-count lint, no scored checklist (the `methodology_honesty_artifact` bar, build-finding A-3). *Done:* `jigc start --workflow planning "M99"` over the methodology pack (real binary) composes and **mints a task dir**, the composed stdout emits `Checkpoint: settle` at the Settle step head and the create/add-item/set-slot guidance lines for the three doctypes; asserted in a compose test extending the `methodology_pack_compose` harness. `cargo test`/`clippy`/`fmt` green. *Files:* `packs/methodology/workflows/planning.yaml`, `packs/methodology/steps/{plan-scope,detect-gaps,settle,plan-review,decompose,author-roadmap,author-ledger,author-decisions}.yaml` (or the minimal step set the include-list needs), `packs/methodology/config/commands.yaml` (the `{{cli.X}}` create/add-item/set refs the steps resolve), a compose test in `crates/cli/tests/`. *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The authoring spine (`creates-task: true, selectable: false`, the `sub-task` precedent) + The four doctypes (the drivers); [milestone-planning-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md) → The loop (the five phases + Settle as the human gate); `packs/methodology/workflows/{increment,dev-task}.yaml` + `crates/cli/pack/workflows/sub-task.yaml` (the workflow-shape precedents); `packs/methodology/steps/plan-gate.yaml` (the existing `checkpoint` step form). *Assumption to prove:* the `{{cli.X}}` command-refs the authoring steps emit (`jigc doc create roadmap`, `add-item`, `set-slot`/`set-field` on item-leaf addresses) must be spiked against the **built command grammar** (run the exact emitted lines, or read the clap verb set) — the M8 invocation-command-is-a-claim discipline ([milestone-planning-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md) → Settle traps); the compose test asserting they appear is not the same as proving they run (T4 runs them).

- **T3** — Extend the build-honesty + off-router guards for `planning` (test-only, falsifiable). (a) Extend the `methodology_increment_off_router` pattern: the methodology `default-workflow.of` enum still names exactly `[dev-task]` (now also forbidding `planning`), and bare `jigc start` over the methodology pack lists `dev-task` only — `planning` (`selectable: false`) never leaks into the model-free selection catalog (the M8 catalog-leak class). (b) Extend the `methodology_honesty_artifact` bar to the planning steps: `settle`/`detect-gaps`/`review` stay judgment prose (restate/stop-and-check/surface-the-fork handback present; no `gap-count`/`>=`/`checklist` hollowing) — the `methodology_honesty_artifact` FAIL exemplar, applied to the new phases. *Done:* the extended assertions go **red** if `planning` is added to the enum or surfaces in the catalog, or if a planning judgment step is mechanized into a lint/checklist — and **green** over the shipped T1+T2 bytes. `cargo test` green. *Files:* `crates/cli/tests/methodology_increment_off_router.rs` (extend), `crates/cli/tests/methodology_honesty_artifact.rs` (extend). *Refs:* [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The `planning` workflow (Off-router) + Build-time honesty watch (A-3); [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) → success bar #2 FAIL exemplars; the M8 catalog-leak class. *Notes:* `bare_start...lists_dev_task_only` already asserts `ids == ["dev-task"]`, so adding `planning` (selectable:false) keeps it green by construction — T3 adds an **explicit** `planning`-named negative assertion so the guard is falsifiable for *this* workflow, not merely incidentally satisfied (`documented != delivered`).

- **T4** — Flow 19 two-run e2e acceptance over the real binary (the headline).
