## 2026-06-09 — M16 build halt (inc-4 T4): multi-slot-per-repeatable-item lifted (a deferral, by human choice)

The build ran increments 1–3 + inc-4 T1–T3 clean, then **halted at inc-4 T4** (the flow-19 acceptance) on a **genuine planning miss** — caught not by either review pass but by the executor's M13 cold-start binary spike (the discipline working as designed, one phase later than ideal). **The defect:** the `roadmap` doctype's milestone entry was specified (and T1 shipped) with **two prose slots** (`proves` + `decomposition`), but the engine's repeatable-item storage holds **exactly one slot per item** (`ParsedItem.slot: Option<Span>` / `ItemContent.slot: Option<String>`) — authoring both drops one (last-writer-wins, `render(parse(x)) != x`). The locked docs were internally contradictory: [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) asserted the two-slot shape **and** the deferred multi-slot/multi-level limit simultaneously. Neither the same-model nor the cross-model review caught it (both focused on location/singleton/ref/gate); the executor's spike did — the milestone-build human gate fired correctly (writing T4 over a single-slot collapse would need a masking test).

**Decision (human-chosen): build multi-slot-per-repeatable-item** (option 3 — lift the deferred limit), *not* collapse the roadmap to one slot (option 1) — so the roadmap entry keeps its genuine two-part structure rather than a workaround. This **graduates the "Multi-slot sections + their rendering" deferral** ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)) for the **repeatable-item** case (the Simple-section case stays deferred — no driver). **Settled rendering (the multi-slot sub-label syntax the deferral flagged open):** an item template with **>1 slot** renders each slot under a `#### <Leaf-Title>` sub-heading (single-word leaf ids, title-cased — routing around the multi-word-section-id reparse defect, the same discipline section ids follow); an item with **exactly one slot** keeps the current **bare-prose** form (byte-identical backward-compat with `arch-doc`/`deferral-ledger`/`decisions-log`/`completion-record`). This mirrors the document's heading hierarchy one level deeper (`##` section → `###` item → `####` item-slot-label); within a multi-slot item, `#####`+ stays opaque slot-internal content (only `####` at the leaf-label level delimits). Scoped to repeatable items; the roadmap's two slots become valid, schema + authoring step unchanged. Built as **inserted Increment 1b** (engine substrate, [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16) before T4 resumes.

## 2026-06-09 — M16 milestone-completion: built, audited, 3 findings fixed + re-verified — ✅ shipped

M16 built end-to-end via the [milestone-build harness](implementation/milestone-build-workflow.md) (26 commits, base `c3e9205`): increments 1, **1b**, 2–5 — **1 design halt** (inc-4 T4, the two-slot/one-slot-per-item contradiction → the human lifted the deferred multi-slot limit as inserted Increment 1b, then T4 resumed via a cached-prefix replay) and **0 in-increment fix rounds**. **The self-hosting machinery loop is closed:** jigc composes its own `planning` + `completion` workflows (`creates-task: true, selectable: false`, the `sub-task` precedent) and manages four working-doc doctypes (`roadmap`/`deferral-ledger`/`decisions-log` running singletons + per-milestone `completion-record`) — on **fresh instances** (jigc's own files migrate at v1). Engine deltas: repeatable-section conformance, `singleton: true` + idempotent-create (copy-in → create-or-update + clobber fix), multi-slot-per-repeatable-item (`#### <Leaf-Title>`), the `owner-artifact.present` #5 gate (presence at a safe owned-location durably-staged path, never content; four-list severity sync → 27/18).

**The [milestone-completion audit](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md)** (independent code-review + real-binary e2e, parallel) returned **11/11 e2e scenarios passing** (flows 19 + 20 reproduced in throwaway repos) and **3 code-review findings — every one verified-real (reproduced as a red), auto-fixed, re-verified** (fix-now by default; none too-big or contested):
- **HIGH (`ddd8eb5`)** — multi-slot slot prose containing a `#### ` line-start shadowed the item-slot delimiter → silent round-trip corruption (`render(parse(x)) != x`) of the shipped `roadmap`. Fix: a parse-level `conformance.item-slot-delimiter-shadowed` block (the `Run:`/`Spawn:`/`Checkpoint:` marker-shadow discipline applied one level deeper); single-slot byte-identity held (zero snapshot churn), `conformance.*` codes are inventory-exempt so no severity-sync.
- **LOW (`a8056e4`)** — item-level `date set: on-create` was never materialized (the `add-item` mint left it empty). Fix: a CLI-side `today_iso()` deriver threaded through `add_item`. **Spillover surfaced + tracked, not fixed:** **doc-level** `set: on-create` (e.g. `adr`'s date, M1) is *also* inert — no on-create deriver ever existed; not exercised by M16's flow, so deferred ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md), the triage "pre-existing + not-flow-exercised → track" rule).
- **LOW (`f3f9855`)** — a gitignored owner-artifact wrongly passed the #5 gate (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` drops gitignored files, so a present-but-non-committable file read as tracked). Fix: a `git_untracked_all` predicate (drop `--exclude-standard` for the durable-presence check); the staged-passes / absent-untracked-unsafe-blocks cases held.

Re-verify: full gate green (`fmt` · `clippy -D warnings` · `test` (412 cli + engine + integration, 0 failures) · `build`), the deliverable holds under the re-run flows. **The dialect-extension trigger ledger is now fully resolved** (M15 checkpoint #2/#4-structural; M16 #5 presence-gate; #1 A==A lint + #3 gate-command knob stay deferred with named triggers). **M16 is adoption-arc prereq #2 — M17 (dogfood + measurement) is unblocked.** Completion fold-back: [doctype-map.md](implementation/doctype-map.md) (4 doctypes shipped), [self-hosting.md](design/self-hosting.md) (What M16 built), [validation.md](design/validation.md) (27/18 inventory + the `owner-artifact` row, reconciled by the build).

### 2026-06-09 — M16 inc-5 / T1: `completion-record` shipped; `severity` enum = `[blocking, advisory]`

The `findings.severity` enum members were left unspecified by planning (only `disposition`'s `[fixed, deferred, contested]` was pinned). Chosen **`[blocking, advisory]`** — mirroring the engine's own `finding::Severity` vocabulary (`blocking`/`warning`/`advisory`), so an audit finding's recorded severity reads in the same terms the validation gate emits. Schema shipped at `packs/methodology/schemas/completion-record.yaml`; exercised through the binary (`crates/cli/tests/methodology_completion_record.rs`): describe-loads, exact-shape + `owned-location` bare re-serialization, an authored instance round-trips byte-stable through `finalize`-promotion, and a half-authored `findings` entry (empty `disposition`) blocks at `schema-conformance.required-field-present`.

## 2026-06-12 — M17 planning: Settle — the measurement substrate, the A/B control, the dogfood-record, the pre-fix set

M17 (dogfood + measurement, the adoption-arc terminus) planned per the [milestone-planning workflow](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md): four capability-auditors exercised the built surface, four gap-detectors probed decisions/docs/doctypes/capabilities, and a binary spike exercised the new doctype shape before its design was written. Design home created: [design/measurement.md](design/measurement.md) (fact definitions, capture substrate, A/B protocol, three-case protocol, seeded-failure obligation). The settled forks, each human-chosen:

- **Scope: pilot-first, sequenced inside M17** — one pilot (unlike-jigc) validates the measurement methodology behind a four-condition pilot gate before runs 2+3 proceed; a terminus milestone with open-ended fix-what-hurt needs a bound.
- **Capture = hooks + three soundness increments** (over pure-protocol and over a full event-log/report verb): a versioned PostToolUse hook artifact (Bash → jigc invocations; Write|Edit → the OOB denominator, works on the control arm) + findings emitted on *successful* finalize + **absorb advances the file-state baseline at landed finalize** (fixes the verified re-fire defect — one OOB edit re-fired `reconciliation.absorb` indefinitely because the CLI never persisted the post-sweep state) + a distinct validation-blocked exit code. Smallest sound substrate; the engine never opines on the thesis.
- **build-health = written counting protocol** (transcript + hook log, orchestrator-counted, transcribed as typed ints honestly labeled protocol-counted) — the binary cannot see halts/fix-rounds without a runtime, and the no-runtime invariant holds. This homes the M12-deferred quantitative comparison as *protocol*, not engine surface.
- **Run record = net-new `dogfood-record` doctype** (methodology pack; per-run `id-from: title`; int fact fields + case/arm/binary-sha + verdict enum + judgment slot + owner-artifact), driven by a `record-dogfood` workflow (`creates-task: true, selectable: false` — the completion authoring-spine pattern). **Spiked green end-to-end through the real binary at planning** (author → malformed-int/invalid-enum write-blocks → finalize → promote → OOB round-trip). Design-binding facts from the spike: **`location: dogfood/`, never shared** (the reconcile sweep parses every file in a location dir against every schema declaring it — sharing `completions/` cross-blocks); the owned-artifact home stays the hardcoded `completions/artifacts/`; `int` has no range constraint (counts protocol-honest, not schema-clamped). The **control arm gets no record** — its counts live in the comparison owner-artifact prose (no N/A-int contortion; the optional-field deferral stays unfired). Records are authored through jigc *in the twin*, then exported as plain committed files to `completions/artifacts/M17/<case>/` (jigc's own repo stays unmanaged until v1).
- **Comparator: the A/B control supersedes the hand-run-trend framing** of the M12 deferral — the trend had no runnable home on foreign projects (the deferral's own reason); trend talk is qualitative corroboration only. A/B = twin `/tmp` copies of the pilot target at one baseline (verified: `jigc setup` deltas galey's CLAUDE.md by exactly 4 lines — the twins differ by precisely the adapter), matched real intent, hooks on both arms, rubric'd human judgment (LLM-assist permitted), verdict never computed.
- **Targets:** pilot = `gherrink-galey` (TS, unlike-jigc, doc↔code honestly gated off); case-2 = **`gherrink-lacon`** (Rust, ~208 md, `docs/` — exercises ingest on a real corpus *and* is the one case where doc↔code genuinely adjudicates); case-3 = greenfield, **human-driven** ("testing how it feels" — the strongest-form Half-B, un-hollowable by construction), intent named at the pilot gate.
- **Pre-fix run-breakers only** (six, each verified at this gate by real exercise — "it hurt" already happened; the rest stay genuine dogfood findings): (1) the planning workflow's missing finalize tail (composed prose strands the authored docs); (2) `finalize.base-mismatch` hard-pin (a task minted before other commits land can only discard — the completion workflow's own shape hits it *by design*; pinned direction in [design/finalize.md](design/finalize.md): auto-re-pin iff *(paths changed between recorded base and HEAD)* ∩ *(dirty working-tree paths ∪ promote destinations)* = ∅, conflict-route on overlap); (3) `--task`-less composed write-commands (fail with >1 active task, which the workflows themselves create; pinned: compose-time substitution — the authoring steps' literal commands carry the minted task id via placeholder, deterministic pack+compose surface); (4) the **#5 owner-artifact omission-bypass** (an omitted `owner-artifact:` line yields no finding anywhere — a declared owned-location becomes required like any other field; *conformance owns field-absence, the gate owns the named file* — chosen over a gate-blocks-on-absence shape to keep conformance uniform; baked into [design/methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → engine work item 3); (5) the **artifact false-rename block** (spike-found, pre-existing: a promoted owner-artifact enters the file-state baseline, the per-schema sweep never re-sees `completions/artifacts/**`, and every subsequent finalize in the repo false-blocks on `reconciliation.rename` — hits completion-record's own flow too; pinned direction in [design/reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md): *missing means absent from disk, not absent from the walk* — chosen over excluding the artifact home, which would blind the sweep to a genuinely deleted artifact dangling behind a committed record); (6) **QUICKSTART's stale one-call-mint claim** (it documents the pre-router `jigc start`; it is case-3's verbatim fixture, so the staleness would contaminate the greenfield measurement). Deliberately *not* pre-fixed (dogfood data, tracked in [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)): the Rust-hardcoded `re-verify` gate prose, the dirty-tree sweep, the owner-artifact raw-`git add` friction, the ingest scan breadth, the doc-code non-Rust silent-symbol-pass.
- **Install channel: copy binary + probe sibling** to a PATH dir — the `cargo install` packaging trigger stays consciously unfired (recorded, [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)); the 418MB probe-target-dir embed defect is tracked, not M17-blocking.
- **Binary pinning:** each measured run pins one build (sha in the record); fixes land between runs; a mid-run binary change marks the run contaminated → re-run.
- **Seeded-failure obligation** (the falsifiable edge against the green-by-construction FAIL mode): every measured run plants one OOB edit + one bad-finalize attempt; each must register exactly once or the run fails regardless of its numbers — the M16 fires-and-blocks discipline applied to measurement itself.
- **Terminus:** completing M17 closes the roadmap spine — the product is built, self-hosted, and thesis-tested. Explicitly post-spine (tracked, not scheduled): v1 in-place migration of jigc's own working docs, legacy auto-migration, the public pack-authoring API, store-scope cardinality enforcement.

**Independent design review (2026-06-12, pre-decompose): 3 blocking / 7 important / 4 minor — all 14 accepted + baked before the cut.** The blocking catches: flow 21 sequenced the seeded OOB edit before any committed managed doc existed to edit (reordered — seeds plant mid-run after the first promoting finalize, target class named); the adapter-adherence denominator double-counted a hook-observed edit later absorbed (dedup rule added: one OOB event per path per run, channels corroborate never sum; the managed-doc path set defined incl. `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/`; the seed pinned to the absorb channel); three pre-fix shapes were unscoped forks (pinned in their design homes — see the pre-fix bullet). Important catches baked: expected organic values stated (organic drift-caught ≈ 0 by the validate-first loop — a paired non-headline validate-block count added; pilot adherence ≈ 100% near-tautologically — case 2 is where the core bet is tested); build-health includes **audit-findings** (human-chosen: counted from the run's completion-record findings entries where the completion workflow runs); the A/B matched task pinned to **one `dev-task`** on the jigc arm (human-chosen — like-for-like session shape; the full spine is the surrounding pilot, not the A/B); the roadmap M17 entry + self-hosting.md's superseded comparator sites rewritten with forward pointers; the absorb persistence rule recorded in reconciliation.md (its home), the validation-blocked exit code pinned to **3** (+ the error path honors `--format json` in the same increment); the #5 requiredness reversal baked into methodology-docs.md with the why; QUICKSTART moved into the pre-fix set (= six). Minor: the unblinded-judge bound named in measurement.md, the doctype-map prose covers the net-new row, the apparatus-home placement made conscious.

**Cross-model review (2026-06-12, Codex over the baked design): 2 blocking / 4 important / 2 minor — all 8 accepted + baked.** The blind spots the same-model pass blessed: **seeds validate the instrument, never the thesis** (a planted event is by construction not an agent decision — the record now splits `seeded-*` instrument-check fields from the organic facts the thesis reads, and the pilot gate is explicitly substrate-validation whose verdict must name ≥1 non-seeded observation); **asymmetric adherence units** (raw verb invocations vs. one-absorb-per-path would green the ratio by command granularity — the unit on both sides is now one logical mutation per doc address × finalize window, invocations demoted to telemetry); **halts split** `halts-expected` (scripted checkpoint ceremony) vs. `halts-unplanned` (the health signal); drift-caught headline is organic-only with `seeded-blocks`/`validate-blocks` as separate fields; **a third comparison arm** (human-chosen): **static-methodology CLAUDE.md** — the methodology content hand-frozen into a static file, pilot-only — isolating dynamic composition + the write channel from methodology *content* (without it, A-beats-B can't attribute the win to jigc rather than written-down methodology); **pre-registration** (intent, acceptance checks, allowed interventions, stop condition, rubric — written before any arm runs, the carryover mitigation); the record is per-jigc-run (the dead `arm: control` enum variant dropped); the owner-artifact must carry the **raw hook log + tally output + transcript with content hashes** so transcription is auditable, not procedural. Codex confirmed the determinism boundary holds (verdict stays a judge slot; the CLI never computes "jigc helped").

## 2026-06-12 — M17 planning: decomposition

Cut M17 from the twice-reviewed [measurement.md](design/measurement.md) into **five harness-fittable increments + three protocol phases** ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 17 decomposition) — the structural split is the decomposition's load-bearing decision: the dogfood runs are **not** increments (genuine live sessions recorded as owner-artifacts — the Half-B class a TDD loop would hollow), so the milestone-build harness drives increments 1–5 only, and the runs follow from the main session per protocol. Risk-first order: (1) emission + exit-code soundness (the tally's discrimination substrate — finalize-success findings, exit 3, JSON error path); (2) file-state soundness (absorb baseline-advance at landed finalize + the false-rename disk-presence fix — one edit one absorb, artifacts don't poison); (3) finalize re-pin + owned-location requiredness (the serial-task shape + the omission gate); (4) pack/doc pre-fixes (planning finalize tail, composed `--task` substitution, QUICKSTART); (5) the recording surface (dogfood-record + record-dogfood + the hook apparatus + flows 21/22) — last of the increments because its e2e exercises everything before it. Engine-semantics changes precede the pack/apparatus work that depends on their behavior; every increment names its red obligations in the roadmap cut. Fix-what-hurt increments insert between runs, never mid-run (binary pinning).

## 2026-06-12 — M17 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1 — Emission + exit-code soundness](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-1--emission--exit-code-soundness-the-tallys-discrimination-substrate) into four ordered, single-concern tasks. *Why four, this order:* the success-emission (T1), the exit split (T2), and the JSON error path (T3) are three independent behavioral changes the scope names separately; T4 is the third scope bullet — the joint discrimination matrix the tally counts against, last because it seals the outcome space the first three open. Grounding facts the cut rests on (verified against base `7d0382a` — code read + the real binary exercised, not assumed):

- **The silent-success gap is real and singular.** `TaskArea::finalize` (`crates/cli/src/task.rs:418–472`) computes the preflight `ValidationReport` (`:424`) but renders it only on the planner-block branch (`:452–460`, stderr); the landed path (`execute_finalize_plan`, `task.rs:609–627`) returns `SUCCESS` printing nothing — so the `reconciliation.absorb` advisory (`engine/src/file_state.rs:168`) is swallowed exactly there. The renderer to reuse exists: `render::validation(format, &report)` covers agent/human/json (`render.rs:245–261`).
- **The exit-code space is verified free.** Every block and every operational error today maps to `ExitCode::FAILURE` = 1 (blocked validate `task.rs:160–164`, blocked finalize `task.rs:459`, all `Err` arms); the real binary confirms clap's usage error exits **2** — so **3** (pinned at the M17 settle review) is unclaimed. Fallout is low: blocked-path tests assert `!status.success()`, which exit 3 still satisfies.
- **The JSON gap is verified live.** `jigc task validate nonexistent --format json` prints plain text on stderr and exits 1 (run at planning) — the operational-error funnels (`eprintln!("{err:#}")` in `task.rs`, `cli.rs`, `milestone.rs` dispatch arms) never consult `format`.
- **The exit-3 boundary, pinned:** 3 = a blocking-`ValidationReport` / `plan_finalize`-findings outcome — `task validate` (the `validate-blocks` paired count keys on it), `task finalize`, and the same-class milestone-finalize planner block (`milestone.rs:~508–513`; exit-code-only there — its dispatch carries no `format`, renderer untouched). Setup/ingest/join blocks and git/hook commit rejections are **not** validation outcomes and stay 1; clap usage stays 2. Derived from [measurement.md](design/measurement.md) → drift-caught + the validate-blocks paired count, not a new fork.

- **T1** — Landed `task finalize` emits the findings envelope (stdout, symmetric with `validate`, advisories included; emission only after the commit lands — a git/hook rejection emits no success envelope; `task finalize` only, milestone success out per the deliverable's words). *Done:* new e2e `crates/cli/tests/finalize_outcome_surface.rs::landed_finalize_emits_findings` — task A promotes an adr; a conformant OOB edit hits the committed adr; task B `finalize` lands (exit 0) **and** stdout carries the `reconciliation.absorb` advisory (the absorb-evidence clause proven, not assumed); a clean landed finalize emits the positive no-findings line; both repeated under `--format json` (stdout parses as the report envelope). Red-first: the landed path prints nothing today. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, the new test.
- **T2** — The exit-code split: a named `EXIT_VALIDATION_BLOCKED` (= 3) at the three validation-block sites (`run_validate`, the `task finalize` planner-block branch, the milestone-finalize planner-block branch); everything else untouched per the pinned boundary. *Done:* e2e `validation_blocked_exits_3` — a finalize blocked by a staged violation (e.g. dangling `supersedes` forward-ref) exits **3** with the envelope on stderr; a blocked `task validate` exits **3**; an operational error (`task validate nonexistent`) still exits **1**. Red-first: both blocked paths exit 1 today. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, the test.
- **T3** — The operational-error path honors `--format json`: one shared `render::operational_error(format, err)` — Json: a single-key JSON object `{"error": "<anyhow chain>"}` on stderr, exit stays 1; Agent/Human: today's `{err:#}` byte-unchanged — swapped in at every format-bearing error funnel (`task.rs` dispatch + `run_validate`/`run_finalize`/`execute_finalize_plan` err arms, `cli.rs` `run_*` err arms, `milestone.rs` dispatch arms; verbs that take no `--format` are out by construction). *Done:* e2e `operational_error_honors_json` — `jigc task validate nonexistent --format json` exits 1 and stderr parses as JSON carrying the start-a-task route; the agent-format output is byte-unchanged. Red-first: verified plain-text today on the real binary. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, the test.
- **T4** — The discrimination matrix (the drift-caught counting contract). *Done:* e2e `outcome_space_is_discriminable` — one throwaway repo, every outcome pairwise distinguishable by **exit code + output alone**, in both renderer families (agent + json): landed finalize → 0 + envelope on stdout; validation-blocked finalize → 3 + envelope on stderr; operational error → 1 + the JSON error envelope under `--format json`; usage error → 2 — the code space asserted collision-free. *Files:* `crates/cli/tests/finalize_outcome_surface.rs`.

Every *Grouped scope* bullet maps: bullet 1 (finalize-success emission, symmetric with `validate`) → **T1**; bullet 2 (the exit split + the error path honoring `--format json` — its two clauses) → **T2** + **T3**; bullet 3 (renderer/e2e proof: blocked vs. landed vs. operational-error distinguishable) → **T4** (T1–T3 contribute the per-outcome red tests; T4 seals the joint matrix). No bullet narrowed or punted. **No genuine new fork** — exit 3 and the same-increment JSON error path were pinned at the M17 settle review (above); the one open representation (the error-envelope shape) is pinned in T3 as `{"error": …}`, a rendering detail inside the CLI's existing generic-JSON convention. Cross-references [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M17 Increment 1.

## 2026-06-12 — M17 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 2 — File-state soundness](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-2--file-state-soundness-one-edit-one-absorb-artifacts-dont-poison) into two ordered, single-concern tasks — one per defect, each carrying its own roadmap-named red obligation as the red step (folding the bullet-3 red obligations into the fixing tasks keeps every task genuinely red-first; a separate trailing e2e task would arrive green). *Why this order:* the persistence fix (T1) restructures the CLI finalize path the post-promotion e2e (in T2) drives through, so it lands first; the rename fix (T2) is engine-local and independent. Grounding facts the cut rests on (verified against the current code, increment 1 landed at `e21269f` — read, not assumed):

- **The re-fire defect is real and singular.** `TaskArea::validate` (`crates/cli/src/task.rs:375–397`) loads the file-state record, the sweep absorbs *in memory* (`engine/src/validate.rs:207`, `file_state.rs:212`), and the record is **dropped** — never saved. `finalize` (`task.rs:437`) calls the same `validate()` and equally drops it; phase-7 `advance_file_state` (`task.rs:793–813`) reloads from disk and records only the plan's `hash_updates` (promote destinations) + the landed commit's files (`git_commit_files`, `task.rs:970`) — an OOB-edited committed doc the task never touched is in neither set, so its absorbed baseline never persists and `reconciliation.absorb` re-fires in every later task. The fix site is exactly the landed branch of `task finalize` (`task.rs:486–497`), per the [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) persistence amendment.
- **The staged-key constraint is documented intent, not a fork.** The sweep record also carries task-relative `docs/<type>:<slug>.md` baseline-adopt keys (`validate.rs:183`); the doc-comment at `task.rs:358–364` pins why those must *stay* unpersisted (a fresh task's staged instance baseline-adopts fresh rather than drifting against a stale staged hash). So the landed-finalize persistence covers the **committed-store keys only** (`docs/`-prefixed keys stripped), with the commit re-hash winning on overlap — T1 carries the regression guard.
- **Purity needs no new code, only a guard test.** `start` runs no sweep (`start.rs` has no `FileStateRecord`), CLI doc reads run no sweep (`doc.rs` likewise), and the milestone-finalize boundary runs no sweep either (`milestone.rs` has no `FileStateRecord` — its `try_execute_finalize_plan` call at `:539` carries no post-sweep record to persist, so leaving it untouched is vacuous, not a narrowing). The only sweep caller is `validate_task` via `task validate`/`finalize`.
- **The false-rename defect is real and located.** `reconcile_committed_store` classifies *missing* as recorded-at-entry minus walked (`file_state.rs:313–317`), where the walk is a non-recursive `<location>/*.md` glob but `persisted_committed_path` (`:337–345`) is a *prefix* match — so a promoted owner-artifact like `completions/artifacts/<run>/x.md` (location `completions/` per `packs/methodology/schemas/completion-record.yaml:21`, durably baselined at its finalize by `git_commit_files`) is in the record, never in the walk → a permanent weak-signal blocking `reconciliation.rename` on every later sweep, exactly as the [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) rename amendment records.

- **T1** — Absorb baseline-advance persisted by landed `task finalize` only (the re-fire fix + the pure-reader guard). `TaskArea::validate` returns the post-sweep record alongside the report; `finalize` threads it to the landed branch, where `advance_file_state` starts from the post-sweep record's committed-store keys (`docs/`-prefixed staged baselines stripped) and applies `hash_updates` + the commit re-hash on top; the blocked branch and the standalone `task validate` verb persist nothing; milestone boundary untouched (no sweep there — verified above). *Done:* new e2e `crates/cli/tests/file_state_soundness.rs::absorbed_oob_edit_fires_absorb_exactly_once_across_tasks` — one conformant OOB edit on a committed adr; task A's landed finalize emits `reconciliation.absorb` once in its envelope; task B's `validate` + landed `finalize` emit **zero** absorb for that path (red today: re-fires); plus `validate_does_not_persist_file_state` (running `task validate` alone leaves `.jigc/state/file-state.json` byte-unchanged/absent) and an assertion the persisted record carries no `docs/` keys (the staged fresh-adopt behavior survives). Inc-1's `landed_finalize_emits_findings` keeps passing. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, the new test.
- **T2** — The false-rename fix: *missing means absent from disk, not absent from the walk* — filter `recorded_missing` in `reconcile_committed_store` by genuine disk absence before routing to `detect_rename`; present-on-disk-but-outside-the-walk yields no finding and its baseline stays as-is ([reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → the rename amendment). *Done:* engine unit test `file_state.rs::baselined_path_outside_walk_is_not_missing` — a recorded `completions/artifacts/<run>/x.md` present on disk under the location prefix but never walked → zero `reconciliation.rename`, hash untouched (red today: weak-signal block); delete it → the weak-signal blocking rename fires. Plus the roadmap's post-promotion red e2e in `file_state_soundness.rs::promoted_owner_artifact_does_not_poison_later_finalizes` — through the real binary with the methodology pack: a finalize promoting a completion-record + its owner-artifact lands, the **next** task's finalize lands clean (red before this fix: permanent `reconciliation.rename` block), and `rm`-ing the artifact makes the following finalize block again (genuinely deleted still blocks). Existing strong/weak rename tests keep passing. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/file_state.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/file_state_soundness.rs`.

Every *Grouped scope* bullet maps: bullet 1 (absorb baseline-advance persisted by landed finalize only) → **T1**; bullet 2 (the disk-presence rename fix) → **T2**; bullet 3 (the two red obligations) → the re-fire case is **T1**'s red e2e, the post-promotion finalize + deleted-artifact-still-blocks case is **T2**'s red e2e — each named in the task that delivers it, nothing punted to "later". **No genuine new fork** — both fixes were pinned as design amendments in [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) at the M17 settle, and the one implementation subtlety (which sweep keys persist) is resolved by the existing documented staged-fresh-adopt intent (`task.rs:358–364`), guarded by a T1 test rather than re-decided. Cross-references [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M17 Increment 2.

## 2026-06-12 — M17 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 3 — Finalize re-pin + owned-location requiredness](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-3--finalize-re-pin--owned-location-requiredness-the-serial-task--omission-gates) into four ordered, single-concern tasks. *Why four, this order:* the re-pin splits along the established engine-pure/CLI-git-facts seam (the decision rule first as a pure engine function, then its CLI wiring + the two history-shape e2e reds), the requiredness flip is one independent engine site, and the completion-shaped seal comes last because it needs both halves. Grounding facts the cut rests on (verified against the current code on top of inc 1–2, `847558f` — code read + fixtures traced, not assumed):

- **`base` is read by the planner only at the phase-1 equality.** `plan_finalize` consults the pin solely at `finalize.rs:173–174` (the milestone sibling at `:250–251`); no later phase reads it — so a re-pin is a pure substitution of the *effective* pin, with zero downstream-phase change. The validate sweep is base-independent (`TaskArea::validate` feeds `head`, never `base` — `task.rs:395–404`); the only other CLI consumer is `has_diff` (`task.rs:455`, `git_diff(&base.sha)`), which **must** be recomputed against the effective base on a re-pin, else a no-work task reads the moved history as its own diff and slips the empty-commit guard.
- **The stage step is base-independent.** Finalize stages via `git add --all` (`task.rs:648`); commits already landed between the recorded base and HEAD are clean in the working tree, so a re-pinned finalize commits only the task's own work — no stage change needed.
- **No re-pin persistence is needed.** A landed finalize removes the working area at post-commit; a blocked one must not mutate it (the inc-2 landed-only discipline). So the re-pin is per-invocation **in-memory** — `base.json` is never rewritten; a blocked-then-retried finalize re-derives the same decision deterministically.
- **Two existing tests flip under the amendment — both fixtures are disjoint.** `finalize_to_git.rs::finalize_aborts_with_no_commit_when_head_moved` (`:576`) and `e2e_audit.rs::scenario_5b_finalize_aborts_on_base_mismatch` (`:639`) both dirty `limiter.rs` while the human commit touches only `other.txt` — under the pinned overlap rule they re-pin and land, so T2 rewrites them as the disjoint-lands red and adds the overlap fixture that keeps the block.
- **The requiredness flip is one engine site, and the pack needs no schema change.** `is_author_required`'s `FieldType::OwnedLocation` early-return (`validate.rs:733–735`) is the only absence exemption; the value check is already permissive (`check_value`'s shared String arm, `write.rs:3440`), so requiredness adds no value constraint — the #5 gate keeps owning the named file (`validate.rs:357–420`, untouched). `owner-artifact` carries no `default:`/`set:` (`packs/methodology/schemas/completion-record.yaml:31`), so the flip alone makes it author-required; every existing completion-record test sets the field (flow20 + `owner_artifact_gate.rs` traced), so only the M16 exemption unit test (`validate.rs:961`) inverts.

- **T1** — Engine: the pure base-divergence re-pin decision. A new `engine::finalize` pure function (e.g. `decide_base_repin(task_dir, base, head_sha, changed_paths, dirty_paths, schemas)`) returning *no-divergence* (base == head) / *re-pin* (*(paths changed base→HEAD)* ∩ *(dirty working-tree paths ∪ promote destinations — derived via the existing `plan_promotions` sweep)* = ∅) / the blocking findings (overlap → an upgraded `finalize.base-mismatch` finding **naming the overlapping paths** + the conflict route: resolve the overlap or `jigc task discard`). The CLI supplies the two git path-sets (the `tracked_predicate`/`has_diff` precedent — the engine stays shell-free); `plan_finalize`'s phase-1 equality stays as defense; the **milestone sibling is consciously unchanged** (the [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) amendment targets the serial-task phase 1; M7's join boundary has no serial-task shape). *Done:* engine unit tests (`cargo test -p engine repin`) — disjoint history re-pins; a dirty-path overlap blocks naming the path; a promote-destination overlap blocks; an unmoved base is no-divergence. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/finalize.rs`.

## 2026-06-12 — M17 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 4 — Pack + doc pre-fixes](implementation/roadmap.md#increment-4--pack--doc-pre-fixes-the-composed-surface-tells-the-truth) into four ordered, single-concern tasks. *Why four, this order:* the planning tail is one pack-only include (independent, first); the task-disambiguation bullet splits along the engine/pack seam — the inline-substitution *mechanism* (T2, the one genuine engine change) before its pack-wide *adoption + proof* (T3, which consumes it); the QUICKSTART rewrite is doc-only and closes last. Grounding facts the cut rests on (verified against the current code on top of inc 1–3, `41bb471` — code read **and** the real release binary exercised, not assumed):

- **The stranded-docs gap is one missing include.** `packs/methodology/workflows/planning.yaml` ends at `{{ include: step:author-decisions }}` — no finalize; `completion.yaml` and `dev-task.yaml` both end with `{{ include: step:finalize }}`, and `steps/finalize.yaml` **already carries the commit-doc authoring guidance** (the four `set-commit-*` command-refs + `finalize-task`) — so the roadmap's "(+ commit-doc authoring guidance)" clause ships inside the same include; no new step.
- **The >1-active-task wall is real for *every* composed doc-verb line.** Reproduced live: with two active tasks, `jigc doc set-slot commit:<id>#summary --from-file -` (the composed form — note the address already carries the task id) *and* `jigc doc create adr --title …` both exit 1 with ``more than one active task — name one with `--task <id>` ``; all four doc verbs already accept `--task` (`doc.rs` — explicit wins, else single-active, else reject), so the fix is purely on the composed-command surface.
- **"Extend the same mechanism" is two verified precedents — and the literal-line half genuinely needs engine work.** Catalog `{ from: "task.id" }` args resolve at compose (the dev-task compose emits `` Run: `jigc task finalize third-task` `` — verified live) and already pass both `workflow_refs` gate sites (dev-task/completion gate clean today); inline token recognition exists for `{{fill:}}` (`next_fill_token`, `compose.rs:1616`, with the skip-non-matching discipline). But inline **bare data-values do not resolve**: `emit_line` (`compose.rs:504–566`) recognizes only lone-line placeholders (`parse_lone_placeholder` requires the whole trimmed line), so a literal `--task {{task.id}}` would emit verbatim — T2 is a real change, not a reuse claim.
- **The substitution is additive-safe.** No pack step body carries a mid-line `{{` (the sole occurrence is `over: "{{ milestone.tasks }}"` — fan-out front-matter, never an emitted body line), and `methodology_pack_compose.rs`'s existing *no-`{{`-survives* assertion then guards the literal-line substitution for free.
- **QUICKSTART's staleness verified live.** The dev pack pins `default-workflow: router` (`crates/cli/pack/config/defaults.yaml:2`); on a fresh repo `jigc start "<intent>"` emits the router menu + the `jigc start --workflow <chosen> "<intent>"` re-run line and **mints nothing** — QUICKSTART §2 claims it mints and composes `single-task`. The probe sibling: `build.rs` places `doc-code` next to `jigc` (present in `target/release/` after the release build; `invoke.rs` resolves `<jigc-bin-dir>/doc-code`), so QUICKSTART's `cp target/release/jigc /usr/local/bin/` installs a binary whose anchor-carrying finalizes hit the floored `pack-probe-integrity` failure (the decisions-pending M17-audit note).
- **The full `--task`-less surface, enumerated** (grep-verified): methodology catalog — `set-commit-type`/`-scope`/`-summary`/`-body`, `create-roadmap`/`-ledger`/`-log`, `create-completion-record`; dev catalog — `set-commit-summary`, `create-adr`/`-spec`/`-prd`/`-arch-doc`; literal authoring lines — methodology `author-roadmap` (3), `author-ledger` (4), `author-decisions` (2), `author-completion-record` (7) + dev `author-arch-doc` (4). Already task-carrying (untouched): `validate-task`, `finalize-task`, `bind-spec`, `recompose-task`; not task-scoped: `milestone-finalize`, `run-ingest`. The dev pack is **in** scope: the settle pre-fix #3 names "`--task`-less composed write-commands" without pack restriction, and the dogfoods run the dev pack's workflows under concurrent active tasks.

- **T1** — `planning.yaml` gains the finalize tail. Append `{{ include: step:finalize }}` after `author-decisions` — the identical include `completion.yaml`/`dev-task.yaml` carry, bringing the commit-doc authoring guidance with it. *Done:* new e2e `methodology_pack_compose.rs::planning_composes_the_commit_fill_and_finalize_tail` — composed `planning` (real binary, `JIGC_PACK_DIR`) emits the four `set-commit-*` Run lines + `` Run: `jigc task finalize <minted-id>` `` **after** the decompose/author steps (red today: composed planning contains no finalize line); the existing planning compose assertions (ordering, no-`{{`-survives) and flow19 stay green. *Files:* `packs/methodology/workflows/planning.yaml`, `crates/cli/tests/methodology_pack_compose.rs`.
- **T2** — Engine: inline data-value substitution in emitted prose lines. Every *Grouped scope* bullet maps: bullet 1 (the planning finalize tail + commit-doc authoring guidance) → **T1** (the guidance rides the included step — verified, not a new surface); bullet 2 (composed write-command task-disambiguation via compose-time substitution, proven against >1 active task) → **T2** + **T3** (mechanism then adoption — the staging is named in both; the >1-active-task proof is T3's e2e); bullet 3 (QUICKSTART router reality + the probe sibling) → **T4**. The increment's *Proves* (composed prose followed verbatim lands the planning loop, never hitting the wall) is T1+T3's combined e2e surface. **No genuine new fork** — the substitution direction was pinned at the M17 settle (pre-fix #3: "compose-time substitution … deterministic pack+compose surface"); T2's inline-recognition rule is a rendering detail fixed inside the dialect's existing lone-line semantics and the `{{fill:}}` token-scan discipline, both verified above, not re-decided. ### 2026-06-12 — M17 inc-5 / T4: the hook-log schema pinned (v1 JSONL); `python3` as the stock-interpreter latitude

The assigned elaboration lands: the **v1 append-only JSONL schema** (two event kinds — `jigc` with `cmd`/`exit`/`findings[{code,path}]`, `file_op` with `tool`/`path`; `v: 1` on every line) is pinned at [`implementation/dogfood/README.md`](implementation/dogfood/README.md), with [measurement.md](design/measurement.md)'s open-question line flipped to a forward pointer. Latitude calls made within the planner bounds: **script language = `python3`** (the hook input is nested JSON whose `command` strings carry arbitrary quoting/newlines — sh/awk extraction would corrupt; `python3` is the stock interpreter on a dev machine, and `cargo test` executes both scripts for real in `crates/cli/tests/dogfood_apparatus.rs`, a committed v1 fixture pinning backward-readability); **window semantics** — a landed `finalize` (exit 0) *closes* the window it belongs to, so its own absorb findings land in the window being closed; **path attribution rides the findings field** (`location.address` from the JSON envelope, the first backticked token from agent text) — the absorb-channel dedup needs the path, codes alone can't dedup per (path × window). The hook always exits 0 and is off with `JIGC_DOGFOOD_LOG` unset — observation never perturbs the run.

## 2026-06-13 — M17 pilot: single-task comparison run, the grain finding, and the increment-workflow gap

The pilot's three-arm comparison ran live on `gherrink-galey` (matched intent: heading `maxLevel` consistency), with the arm environments corrected mid-setup: **GSD is arm B's *content*, not contamination** — galey is a GSD project, jigc positions as *replacing* GSD, so **B = the GSD run** (`~/.claude`, GSD agents/skills active, mem off); **A = jigc** and **C = static-methodology** run in a clean home with GSD scaffolding stripped from `CLAUDE.md` (project facts kept). claude-mem off on every arm + the personal `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (`@PRINCIPLES`) moved aside (those *are* contamination). Pre-registration amended pre-run twice (recorded): the GSD correction, and **bare intent issued identically to all arms** — jigc routing is the adapter's job, not an instruction (a first arm-A run was discarded for spoon-feeding `jigc start`).

**Result — all three landed a correct fix (<5 min each); A ≈ C.** jigc (A) and static-methodology (C) both produced test-first + quality commits; GSD's *fast skill* (B) was quickest but **skipped the test**. jigc's adapter **routed the agent unprompted** (the adherence bet held) and the **capture apparatus validated end-to-end** on real sessions (jrun logged every verb with real exits — the no-exit-code harness contingency works; hardened post-run so a closed pipe / `| head` can't drop an event, and `argv[0]` hides the wrapper).

**The structural finding (why A≈C):** `dev-task` has **no `allows-create`** — a lone code task produces only a transient `commit` and touches **none** of jigc's differentiators (managed `decisions-log`/`roadmap`/`completion-record`, validation, drift, supersession). Decision-recording is **milestone-grained** — `author-decisions` lives only in the heavy `planning`/`completion` loops. So the single-task comparison validates the **adapter + methodology layer + apparatus**, but **cannot** test the differentiators; *any* code task ties for the same reason. Retained as that validation; **superseded as the thesis test** by a milestone-grained run (the next direction). **Owed (→ [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)):** a lightweight **increment-level workflow** that can record a decision / manage a doc for sub-milestone work — the grain gap the dogfood surfaced.

## 2026-06-13 — M18 planning (Settle): the store-wide `jigc validate`, four forks, baseline-verified

Planned via the milestone-planning workflow. The capability-auditor recon (4 subagents, exercised at HEAD `6382dbc`) plus a live gap-detector **spike** (drove the real `doc-code` binary over a committed 3-ADR store using only public engine surface — one finding for the dangling anchor, none for the valid one, address-sorted) **proved the store-sweep shape end-to-end before any build** — the probe/snapshot/ingest spine is genuinely task-decoupled. Design home: [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Store-scope re-validation. Four forks settled (all to the recommended option):

- **Command shape → top-level `jigc validate`.** The realization of VISION's named-but-unbuilt `jigc validate [target]` loop, scoped in M18 to **doc↔code over the committed store**; the four-target breadth stays a named envelope (as `single-task` realized one VISION workflow). *Why:* the sweep is **task-less by construction**, so hanging it off `task validate --store` (which requires a task id) is the awkward shape; `jigc validate` claims the right surface for future growth.
- **Severity → report-only, exit 0 with findings** (the `jigc ingest` precedent, not the exit-3 gate). *Why:* the done-picture is detect-and-report; a read command with no transaction to block leaves the "integrity at the finalize boundary, not every write" invariant untouched **by construction**. This also inverts the M10 masking-trap guard *intentionally* — task scope excludes unrelated committed docs, store scope surfaces exactly that pre-existing drift (its whole purpose); the inversion is stated so it isn't "fixed" back.
- **Multi-valued `code-anchor` → honest bound + non-silent guard**, not list-element enumeration. *Why:* no shipped `code-anchor` is list-valued (generality for a non-existent case), but the enumerator's current **silent drop** of a list value would be a false "all clear" at store scope — so M18 replaces the drop with a loud guard finding.
- **Probe distribution → scope M18 to build-tree/local-release** (where `doc-code` sits beside `jigc`); the `cargo install` embed-extract fix stays on its existing trigger ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)), unfired. *Why:* the over-time thesis test installs probe+jigc together; widening the install channel is unrelated scope.

Build constraints recorded for decomposition (not forks — implementation guardrails the recon surfaced): the sweep is a **new read-only committed-store walk** (deterministic, address-sorted) that **must not route through `reconcile_committed_store`** (it mutates record+index via *absorb* and would re-baseline genuine drift when run task-less); it **lifts** the private `collect_from_source` projection rather than reusing the task-scoped `enumerate_target_surface` (whose masking-trap guard excludes the very docs the sweep must see). Sweep covers **all three** code-anchor doctypes — `adr.cites-code`, `arch-doc.components/implemented-by`, **`spec.criteria/maps-to-test`** (the third was missed in the M18 handover; recon caught it). **Doctypes: none owed** — pure read-path over already-shipped, actively-created types. **Honest bounds carried into the test:** `symbol-exists` = structural anchor drift only (never behavioral prose drift); non-`.rs` `#symbol` silently passes (file-existence only). **Test half = pre-registered post-build experiment** (plain markdown under `completions/artifacts/M18/`, Codex judge — the M17 native-grain-test template), **not** a build increment and **not** a managed doctype. Forward harness review **skipped** — M18 rides the proven validation/probe substrate (spike-confirmed), not off-substrate.

**Independent design review (design-reviewer, baked back before decompose):** one BLOCKING + two SHOULD-FIX, all accepted; the reuse spine, masking-guard inversion, determinism, and scope-honesty were verified sound.
- **B1 (blocking) — "exit 0 always" swallowed the intrinsic `pack-probe-integrity.*` meta-findings.** A `doc-code` crash mid-sweep would have exited 0 over an unverified store (the cited `jigc ingest` precedent never invokes a probe, so it never had to distinguish a routed *content* finding from a probe that *failed to run*). Fixed to a **two-class exit rule**: stale-anchor content findings → listed, exit 0; any probe-integrity meta-finding → **non-zero exit** (the sweep can't claim a trustworthy result). Still not a transaction gate — the command honestly reports it couldn't complete ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → Severity).
- **S2 — probe-absence behavior unspecified** (the common `cargo install` misconfiguration). Fixed: **pre-flight probe-presence check** → one operational error, not N per-anchor crash meta-findings.
- **S1 — the test-half catch-rate framing is tautological** (the static arm rots 100% by construction, so catch-count is decided before the run). The pre-registration must make catch-count *not* the headline and design a **refutable net-value** measure (true catches **−** false-positive friction on legitimate refactors **−** repair-loop cost); frame to prove-or-refute like the native-grain test.

## 2026-06-13 — M18 test half: maintenance/drift comparison ran — H0 (tie), over-time advantage undemonstrated-not-refuted

The build half shipped + audited clean (top-level `jigc validate`, 3 increments, 2 LOW audit findings fixed). The **test half** then ran the founding thesis's best remaining shot ([completions/artifacts/M18/maintenance-test/](completions/artifacts/M18/maintenance-test/), pre-registration frozen first, binary re-pinned `00e67f0f`).

- **Design (anti-tautology):** both arms *maintain* a toy Rust project over an identical 5-step code-evolution sequence (rename/delete/move/test-rename/control), both told to keep doc citations honest (standing `CLAUDE.md` rule, code-work primary), differing ONLY in mechanism — arm J has `jigc validate`, arm S manual diligence. Metric = stale-citation count of each arm's final state + the per-step caught-vs-shipped timeline. Diligence-vs-machine, genuinely refutable — not catch-rate-vs-silent-rot.
- **Result: H0 — flat tie.** 4 blind subagents (2/arm) → **0 stale citations in all four**, every break repaired in-step (incl. step 3's one-symbol-two-docs break), no over-editing on the control step. Confirmed mechanically + by 2 independent blind review agents over de-identified bundles (both returned 0/arm).
- **Honest reading:** H0 under the **pre-registered session-compression bound** — one focused session with a telegraphing task list is the static arm's *best* case; `jigc validate` never fired because diligence never failed (every J-arm repair was *proactive*; validate only *confirmed* clean — the detector never caught drift the agent missed). So the tie **cannot refute** the over-time claim, and a win would have been strong. Restates the native-grain lesson at maintenance grain (machine-guaranteed integrity ties capable diligence at moderate scale).
- **Behavioral blind spot, observed in the wild:** both judges independently flagged that both jigc arms let a component's *prose* degrade (dropped a clause the code still performs) while its symbol stayed valid — `validate` green over behaviorally-drifted prose. Structural-anchor honesty ≠ documentation honesty. Stated as observed-here (n=2), not a general tendency.
- **Verdict Codex-passed** (the M17 lesson): removed phrases implying the detector detected/drove repair, narrowed "capability is real" to the structural sweep, bounded the prose finding. Owed regime for a real over-time test: genuine cross-session separation, where diligence actually fails. Propagated to [VISION.md](VISION.md) → "What is proven (M17–M18)" and [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M18 Outcome.

## 2026-06-13 — M19 planning (Settle): the auto-firing backstop — warn-only git pre-commit hook + finalize relay

Planned via the milestone-planning workflow (3 capability-auditors + 4 gap-detectors, all exercising HEAD `80b501d`). M19 builds the mechanism that makes the M18 detector *fire* (M18's tie was because `jigc validate` never fired), then tests it under genuine cross-session forgetting. Five forks settled (four to the human, one constraint-forced), plus one spike-driven build addition:

- **Mechanism → an assistant-neutral git `pre-commit` hook**, installed by `jigc setup`, running `jigc validate`. SessionStart-validate is **out**: Claude Code session hooks don't fire for Agent-tool subagents (so the cold-subagent test can't exercise it) and a hook dumping a drift report violates `assistant-adapter.md`'s locked "routing, not content" discipline. **Git-hook only** (no SessionStart route) — keep M19 focused; SessionStart-validate is a future need-driven add.
- **Severity → warn-only** (the hook always exits 0, surfacing findings, never blocking). Constraint-forced: `jigc validate` exits 0 on content findings; a *blocking* store-sweep re-introduces the masking-trap (rejects commits for unrelated pre-existing drift — what M18 avoided) **and** self-gates `jigc finalize` (which commits without `--no-verify`). Recorded as decided, not an open fork. (A `--strict`/CI-gate opt-in stays a future need-driven decision, not M19.)
- **Install home → `jigc setup`'s assistant-neutral install path**, distinct from the per-assistant adapter profile (a git hook is a VCS-event install, identical for every assistant). Precedent: setup already does the neutral project-layer init. `assistant-adapter.md` elaborated with a "neutral install responsibilities" section (the model accommodates it — elaborate, not revise).
- **Loop-closure (spike-driven) → finalize relays hook output on success.** Spiking the seam (`task.rs:git_commit` uses `.output()` and surfaces stdout/stderr **only on failure**) revealed finalize *swallows* a warn-only pre-commit hook's warning on a successful commit — so the jigc-arm agent (which commits via finalize) would never see the drift. Fix: `git_commit` relays captured output to the agent on success too (~small change + test). This **resolves the standing `finalize.md` "commit-msg hook output capture" open question** — a genuine latent-UX fix, not just test scaffolding. Without it the chosen pre-commit mechanism doesn't close the loop.
- **Test refutability → no-cue induced slips.** Cold agents fix their *own* step's break by diligence (M18), so drift only accumulates when a break slips *with no cue*: each step's code change breaks a citation in a doc the step's task list does **not** mention, so a diligent cold agent has no reason to touch it, and the warn-only backstop catches it at a later commit (vs the static arm's silence). Strategy settled now (it constrains the build); exact symbols in the pre-registration.

**Doctypes: none** (pure integration + experiment; the test half is plain markdown under `completions/artifacts/M19/`, the M18 pattern — not a managed doctype, not `dogfood-record`). **Forward harness review skipped** — M19 rides the proven setup/adapter/validate substrate; the one novel seam (hook-fires-inside-finalize) was spiked and is handled (warn-only → no abort; success-relay → visible). **Honest bounds carried into the test:** structural drift only (`symbol-exists`), never behavioral prose drift (M18 observed jigc-green-over-drifted-prose); the cargo-install probe-distribution gap stays on its trigger (M19 targets build-tree/local, like M18). **Open build hazards flagged for the increments:** the hook must resolve the real hooks dir (`core.hooksPath` + git-worktree `.git`-is-a-file), be idempotent + non-destructive (preserve a pre-existing `pre-commit`), and the PATH-vs-absolute-`jigc` choice (a hook calling bare `jigc` runs whatever is on PATH — stale-binary risk).

**Independent design review (design-reviewer, baked back before decompose):** 2 BLOCKING + 3 SHOULD-FIX + 2 NICE-TO-HAVE, all accepted; the spike claim + the exit-code-conflation catch were verified sound.
- **B1 — fan-out finalize fires the sweep N+1× and the relay was specified only for the aggregate commit.** Fixed (finalize.md): relay on the aggregate `git_commit` only; per-sub-task `commit_empty_message` commits (tree-empty) don't relay; the N+1 fires are accepted (warn-only, harmless), a skip-on-empty-diff optimization named out-of-scope.
- **B2 — the warn-only/never-noise contract was prose, not spec; and `jigc validate` exits non-zero + prints errors in no-fault cases (not-a-project/probe-missing).** Fixed (assistant-adapter.md): the hook **keys on content findings, not the exit code** — runs `jigc validate --format json`, warns only on `doc-code.*` findings, else prints nothing and exits 0 (clean / not-a-project / probe-missing / probe-integrity all silent).
- **S1 — relay-on-success is general (one combined git stream, can't single out jigc's hook) and could pollute structured output.** Fixed (finalize.md): relayed output goes in a delimited section after the success result, never in the routing footer/JSON envelope; the (general) behavior change is documented.
- **S2 — the "Proves" line over-claimed that firing is sufficient.** Fixed (roadmap): build *contract* (surfaces, warn-only, does not force repair) separated from test *hypothesis* (does surfacing change repair behavior); a tie stays a possible honest outcome.
- **S3 — no-cue slips risk rigging static-arm-loses + jigc wins only if the warning is acted on.** Folded into the roadmap pre-reg obligations: justify no-cue slips as the realistic over-time case, score the repair (not just the catch), keep tie/static-win reachable.
- **N1/N2** — hook regenerates on every `setup` + no-ops if `jigc` is gone (folds into B2's guard); the hook is an **install artifact** (peer to `.claude/settings.json`), outside the managed-doc store / file-state / reconciliation — no determinism-boundary tension.

## 2026-06-13 — M19 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code at base `4079e95`. Increment 1 = **the auto-firing git `pre-commit` hook (install + output discipline)** — a new assistant-neutral install step in `setup::install` that writes a sentinel-marked, idempotent, non-destructive `pre-commit` running `jigc validate --format json`, warn-only (always exit 0), surfacing a warning **only on `doc-code.*` content findings**. Three tasks, risk-first within the increment: the load-bearing **output-discipline contract** first (the B2 exit-code-conflation landmine — the script's runtime logic, proven by *executing the rendered script* against staged `jigc validate` JSON), then the **real-hooks-dir resolution + idempotent/non-destructive write** (the `core.hooksPath` / worktree / preserve-existing hazards), then **wire into `setup` + the end-to-end binary acceptance** (real `jigc setup` + real `git commit`s). Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M19 Increment 1; design homes [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md) → neutral install responsibilities + [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Auto-firing the sweep. *Why:* the script's output discipline is the one place a naive build ships a defect (the exit code is wrong-way-round — `jigc validate` exits 0 on *found drift*, non-zero on no-fault cases), so it is built + proven as executable bytes before it is wired in.

**Grounded facts verified against the real binary/git before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**
- `git -C <repo_root> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks` resolves **all three** hazards in one call — verified live (git 2.53): it returns `core.hooksPath` directly when set, returns the **common** hooks dir from inside a linked worktree (the `.git`-is-a-file case), and `--path-format=absolute` (git ≥ 2.31) guarantees an absolute path regardless of cwd. So the hooks-dir resolution is a single `git` subprocess, **not** the naive `<repo_root>/.git/hooks` join every other module (`locate.rs`, `pack.rs`, etc.) uses.
- The **PATH-vs-absolute-`jigc` choice is decided: embed the absolute path of the installing binary** (`std::env::current_exe()`) into the hook script. Verified to compose with probe resolution — `invoke::doc_code_default` resolves the `doc-code` probe as a sibling of `current_exe()` (`<bin-dir>/doc-code`), so a hook that invokes the *absolute* installing `jigc` keeps that sibling-probe resolution consistent (a bare-`jigc`-on-PATH hook could run a different binary whose sibling probe differs/absent). This is a doc-elaboration pin within the design's flagged hazard ("the PATH-vs-absolute choice is a real hazard"), made + logged here per the doc-elaboration-pin rule, not a new fork.
- `jigc validate --format json` emits a `ValidationReport` whose `findings[]` each carry serde fields `probe` + `check` (`engine::finding::Finding`); a `doc-code` content finding has `"probe": "doc-code"`, a probe-failure meta-finding has `"probe": "pack-probe-integrity"` — verified by reading the struct + `run_validate_store`'s two-class exit. So the hook keys on `"probe": "doc-code"` presence in the JSON, never the exit code.
- `jigc finalize` commits **without `--no-verify`** (`finalize.md` → 6. Commit; `task.rs::git_commit`), so the hook genuinely fires on a finalize commit — the increment-2 relay closes that loop.

Ordered tasks:
- **T1 — the hook-script body generator + its output-discipline contract (the load-bearing B2 piece).** A new pure function in `crate::setup` (CLI-side, engine stays filesystem-/shell-free) — `precommit_hook_body(jigc_path: &Path) -> String` — that renders the POSIX-`sh` hook script: a sentinel-marked block running the **absolute** installing-`jigc` path's `validate --format json`, parsing the output, and warning **only when a `"probe": "doc-code"` content finding is present**, otherwise printing nothing; the script **always `exit 0`** and **keys on findings, not the exit code**, no-op'ing cleanly when the embedded `jigc` is absent/non-executable. *Done:* a unit test golden-locks the rendered script bytes for a fixed `jigc_path` (the sentinel marker present, `exit 0` present, the absolute path embedded, `--format json` present); and a behavioral test **executes the rendered script** (`sh -c`) with the embedded `jigc` pointed (via a stub on `PATH`/an absolute test double) at canned `jigc validate` outputs across all five cases — (clean → silent, exit 0), (a `doc-code.*` content finding → a human-readable warning on stdout/stderr, exit 0), (not-a-jigc-project non-zero+stderr → silent, exit 0), (a `pack-probe-integrity.*` meta-finding → silent, exit 0), (`jigc` absent/unexecutable → silent, exit 0) — asserting *warns iff a `doc-code` content finding*, never on the exit code, always exit 0. `cargo test` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` clean. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/setup.rs` (+ a `crates/cli/tests/` integration test if the script-execution proof reads cleaner as an integration test). *Design:* [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md) → neutral install (the B2 output-discipline contract); [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Auto-firing the sweep. *Note:* covers grouped-scope bullet 2 (the output discipline + the PATH-vs-absolute choice). The hook's *placement on disk* + idempotency land in T2; the *end-to-end fire at real `git commit`* lands in T3.

The install artifact lives in git's control dir, **outside** the managed-doc store / `file-state` / reconciliation (grouped-scope bullet 3) — satisfied by *where* this writes (the resolved hooks dir, never a managed `location:`); no task routes it through `file-state` (it is never opened as a `FileStateRecord`).

Every bullet maps to a task in this increment; nothing is punted.

## 2026-06-13 — M19 test half: cross-session drift comparison ran — H0 (tie), but the backstop fired + drove repair (on jigc's own drift)

The build half shipped + audited clean (the warn-only `pre-commit` backstop + the finalize success-relay; binary re-pinned `5d64adc`). The **test half** ran the M18-owed regime ([completions/artifacts/M19/cross-session-test/](completions/artifacts/M19/cross-session-test/), pre-reg + appendix frozen first).

- **Design:** genuine cross-session forgetting — a fresh **cold blind subagent per step** (no memory, blind to prior steps touching docs) — over a longer/denser **no-cue** sequence (extended `ratelimit` seed, 16 citations / 4 docs, 8 steps). jigc arm has the warn-only backstop installed; static arm none. n=3 chains/arm (48 cold-subagent runs). Arm-J repair = agent discretion under CLAUDE.md.
- **Result: H0 — tie. All 6 chains ended at 0 stale citations.** Scored mechanically (per-commit citation resolution) + independently re-verified + Codex-passed.
- **The timeline is the finding, and it cuts against the naïve H1:** the **static arm was CLEAN at every commit** (right-first-try diligence — every cold agent fixed its own citation in-step, even cold + no-cue); the **jigc arm was the only one that drifted** — transient stale citations persisting up to 4-commit windows — and recovered via later **detector-prompted** cleanup (J repair commits credit `jigc validate` / "the store-scope doc-code gate" by name). So **unlike M18 (detector never fired), M19's backstop demonstrably fired in anger and drove repair** — a real loop-closure capability gain — **but on drift that arose in jigc's own arm**, and it was **neither a comparative end-state nor timeline win** (static dominated per-commit cleanliness).
- **Honest mechanism (independently challenged, corrected):** *net-dependent cleanup latency*, **not** moral hazard — jigc agents also attempted per-step honesty (a slip was missing a *second* citation site, not negligence). jigc = drift→detect→repair; static = right-first-try; both land clean, but only jigc ever exposed stale citations.
- **Load-bearing bound:** the backstop is **warn-only / advisory** — the loop closed because agents *heeded* the relayed warning, not as a mechanism guarantee (the ergonomic-not-enforced boundary). And static's clean record is N=3 first-try on a small, well-telegraphed citation set — not proven robustness. **The regime where jigc would strictly win** (first-try diligence leaving *residual* final drift the detector catches and the control ships) **was not reached — static didn't fail.** Owed for a real comparative result: denser/larger citation graphs, or truly separated human sessions, where diligence predictably leaves residual drift. Propagated to [VISION.md](VISION.md) → "What is proven (M17–M19)" and [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M19 Outcome.

## 2026-06-14 — Direction: accept scope-bound (option B); reframe the value claim as salience-independence

After the thrice-H0 arc, settled on the handover's **option B** — stop chasing a comparative-superiority benchmark; ship/harden what's built and reframe the value claim to what the evidence + mechanism support. Maurice's observation sharpened it: the three ties all held **instruction salience** fixed — the static arm got a *clean, on-point* "keep citations honest" rule, the best case for static conventions, and **symmetry required that idealization** (a fair test can only give both arms the same clean instruction).

- **The reframe (mechanism, not measurement):** static conventions are **salience-dependent** (work only as well as the agent attends to the relevant line, which decays as the rules file grows); jigc's backstop is **salience-independent** (the `pre-commit` sweep fires identically at 5 or 5,000 lines — a mechanism, not an instruction, so it never competes for attention). Predicts jigc's advantage appears precisely in the regime the tests *excluded* (large, noisy rules surface).
- **Why it stays unmeasured:** reproducing that regime means handing the static arm a realistically bloated rules file — which breaks symmetry and confounds the result (conventions degrade at scale, or *that* file was bad?). Stated as **predicted-by-mechanism, not measured, not cheaply measurable** — the honest scope boundary, not a backdoor superiority claim. Landed in [VISION.md](VISION.md) → "What is proven (M17–M19)".

## 2026-06-14 — M20 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code at base `96b22c7`. Increment 1 = **probe rides in the binary: `cargo install` becomes a supported channel** — a `cargo install`-shape (non-build-tree) `jigc` produces a ~MBs binary whose `jigc setup` extracts the `doc-code` probe beside it, so `jigc validate` / code-anchor finalize work on a fresh machine **with no `JIGC_DOC_CODE_PROBE` override**. Five tasks, **risk-first**: the build-system surgery first (the de-bloat, then the embed+extract — the highest-uncertainty change and the (I)-pick), then the task-scope absence fix (independent), then the no-override install acceptance (the *Deliverable* + *Proves*, which composes the prior three), then the QUICKSTART doc. Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M20 Increment 1; design home [module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md) → Probe distribution. *Why:* the bloat and the missing-extract are *separate* sites (the design-review B2 correction — don't conflate them), so each is its own task; the no-override resolution is the *proven* path (the M10 invocation-path-masking lesson — testing only the override masks a probe that doesn't ship), so it is exercised through the real binary with the override unset.

**Grounded facts verified against the real code/tree before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**
- **Bloat measured at the real site.** `crates/cli/pack/` is **401M**, of which the probe's gitignored `target/` (`crates/cli/pack/probes/doc-code/target`, `git check-ignore`-confirmed ignored) is **401M**; the real pack content (schemas/workflows/steps/config, `pack/` minus `probes/`) is **~176K**. `pack.rs:50` `static PACK: Dir = include_dir!("$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/pack")` embeds the *whole* tree (`include_dir` honors no `.gitignore`, has no exclude filter), so the probe `target/` is embedded dead weight. Verified by `du` + reading `pack.rs`.
- **The probe is NOT embedded today — it is a build-script-copied sibling.** `build.rs` runs a detached `cargo build --manifest-path pack/probes/doc-code/Cargo.toml` and `std::fs::copy`s the produced binary three-parents-up from `OUT_DIR` to sit beside `jigc` (`<target>/<profile>/doc-code`). `pack.rs`'s `EmbeddedPack` only embeds the pack-resource tree, never the probe binary. So the `include_bytes!` extract path (T2) is **net-new**, not a swap of T1. Verified by reading `build.rs` + `pack.rs`.
- **Store-scope pre-flight already exists; task-scope does not.** `cli.rs:515` `require_doc_code_probe()` resolves `invoke::doc_code_program()` and `bail!`s **one** operational error if the probe file is absent — wired into `validate_store_in_repo` (`cli.rs:494`), real-binary-tested in `tests/validate_command.rs` (the "exactly one `doc-code probe not found`" assertion). The **task** path (`task.rs::TaskArea::validate` line 382 → `validate_task(…, &doc_code_invoker, …)`, and `finalize`) has **no** such pre-flight: on a spawn failure `doc_code_invoker` (`task.rs:278`) maps to `ProbeRunStatus::Exited { code: None }`, which the engine floors as a **per-anchor** `pack-probe-integrity.crash`. So T3 ports the existing pre-flight, it does not invent it. Verified by reading both paths.
- **`jigc setup` is an ordered numbered install spine.** `setup::install` (`setup.rs:322`) runs steps 0–5, each mapping an IO failure to a `Finding::block("setup.<step>", msg, route)`; step 5 (the M19 `pre-commit` hook) already resolves `std::env::current_exe()` and writes beside it. The probe-extract step appends as a new numbered step in the same idiom, writing to `current_exe().parent()`. Verified by reading `setup.rs`.
- **The real-binary test idiom.** Integration tests drive `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc")` over a throwaway `git init` repo; the probe is selected for *positive* tests via `JIGC_DOC_CODE_PROBE` pointed at a freshly-built probe (`tests/validate_command.rs`, `tests/flow13_acceptance.rs`). The **no-override** install proof (T4) must therefore *unset* `JIGC_DOC_CODE_PROBE` and stand the probe up only via the setup-extract, into a bin dir with **no** build-tree sibling. Verified by reading the test harness.
- **The `decisions-pending.md` cargo-install trigger (line 69) is already marked GRADUATED at M20 planning** — no edit owed to it this increment. Verified by reading the entry.

Maps to no *new* grouped-scope bullet — it is the cross-cutting proof the *Deliverable* names; its size assertion is the load-bearing red step for T1's de-bloat.
- **T5 — Update QUICKSTART.md.** Replace the manual `cp target/release/{jigc,doc-code}` two-binary copy (`QUICKSTART.md:16–24`) with the single-binary install + `jigc setup` extract: `cargo install`-style installs only `jigc`; `jigc setup` places the `doc-code` probe beside it (no manual probe copy).
