## 2026-06-16 — M24 planning (Scope/Settle): harden changelog migration to a correct reference BEFORE generalizing

**Created 2026-06-16.** The post-M21 doctype-expansion + auto-migration split (2026-06-14) had M22 ship the `changelog` doctype (G2) and M23 ship changelog auto-migration (G1), with **M24 slated to generalize migration to the location-bearing doctypes** (`adr`/`spec`/`prd`/`arch-doc`). **A manual smoke test on two real repos** (throwaway clones of `~/Projects/project-delta` — 127 lines, dateless, heading-categorised — and `~/Projects/project-gamma` — 607 lines, dateless, inline `feat:`/`fix:` prefixes) **reset that sequence.** It proved the M23 spine works end-to-end at scale but surfaced a cluster of friction that is **mostly general migration/authoring mechanism, not changelog-specific** — so generalizing first would copy the broken patterns into four doctypes and force N fixes later. **The human's call (2026-06-16): fix every finding on the changelog *reference* first.** New sequence: **M24 hardens** changelog migration → **M25 generalizes** the corrected pattern to `adr`/`spec`/`prd` → **M26 = arch-doc** (code-anchors + the deferred empty-slot+field-group byte-stability fix, which lands there). Design home: [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) (extended with an M24-hardening section); the finding list is [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → "Changelog-migration hardening".

**Done-picture (confirmed with the human before probing):** changelog migration becomes a *correct, complete reference* — every smoke-test friction fixed on the one working doctype. **Eight fixes + minor polish (#9), NO new schemas.** Acceptance = the **FULL** project-delta + project-gamma live migration on throwaway clones, all releases, **measured** on four facts: round-trip conformance · fidelity-acceptance at the review gate · content-preservation · **agent-call count** (the verbosity-at-scale signal the batch path targets). Minor polish (#9) is **explicitly in scope** (the human's call): the finalize `git add --all` sweep, terse setup/ingest output, the migration-task-name collision.

**Baseline verified by 3 `capability-auditor`s + 4 `gap-detector`s exercising the re-pinned binary** (one auditor died on a transient API-overload after gathering and was re-run narrowed; SendMessage-resume is unavailable in this harness). **"No new schemas" HOLDS** — confirmed no fix forces a new doctype, and critically the date fix (#6) needs **no `changelog.yaml` edit**: `optional: true` is *inert* (the release `date` is already `set: on-create`, so it is non-author-required and an absent date finalizes clean), and dropping `set: on-create` *regresses* normal authoring — the defect is purely the CLI mint stamping `today_iso()` unconditionally. **Two findings came back sharper (worse) than the recorded design:**
- **The in-location squatter (#8) fails at the WRONG seam the design named.** [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) (lines 33/64) and [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):80 attribute the failure to "the write path … `write.wrong-shape`". Exercised reality: it fails at the **idempotent-create copy-in** (`crates/engine/src/state.rs:677-686`, the M16 B-5 clobber fix) which reads the committed non-conformant squatter in as the edit base → a **Frankenstein doc** that blocks at finalize with misleading section errors, *not* a clean `write.wrong-shape` at the write verb. The docs are corrected in this Settle.
- **The `git add --all` sweep (#9a) is not bounded-minor.** The general narrowing needs a task-scoped changed-paths manifest jigc does not have (the blanket add is *why* — finalize commits agent-authored code with no manifest). But a **migration** touches no code: its commit set is exactly {promoted doc} + {retirements}, both already in `FinalizePlan` — so a **migration-scoped** narrowing is bounded and feasible without a manifest.

**Settled forks (the four human-gated, all on the recommended path):**
- **(1) Batch authoring (#3, the milestone's largest build) = declarative whole-doc, NOT the fillable emit-fill-extract form.** The deferred "fillable form" ([write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md):33) was designed for multi-**slot** single docs and has *no story for repeatable expansion* ("add the 13th release"); the migration pain is multi-**item**-at-scale (releases × nested change-groups), and migration generates *de novo* from foreign bytes (no instance to emit-and-fill). The chosen shape: a `jigc doc author <doctype> --from <payload>` verb where the **agent authors one structured payload** (owning the prose) and the **CLI parses it and applies the create + N `add-item` + `set-slot`/`set-field` sequence to a single staged buffer atomically** (parse-once / apply-all / persist-once). Verified-cheap-and-safe: each engine write primitive is a pure `&str → String`, so in-memory chaining is **byte-identical to the current persist-read-between path by construction** (the M23 smoke test already proved the per-verb chain byte-stable at project-gamma's 607 lines), and rollback = discard the buffer (persist only on full success). The batch is **doctype-general** and does **not** touch the source seam (the seam feeds *compose context*; the batch operates on the *staged buffer*) — determinism boundary intact (agent authors the payload; CLI places). The "form-marker syntax" open question ([write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md):217) is **resolved into the payload format**, not an in-place-fill marker.
- **(2) `remove-item` (#1) = build the new engine `remove_nested_item` + expose `jigc doc remove-item <addr>` for top-level AND nested.** The reuse claim ("engine `remove_item` exists, just expose it") is **unverified for the shape the finding names**: `remove_item` (`write.rs:984`) is **top-level-only**, but a wrong *category* — the finding's own example — is a **nested** change-group (`releases/<v>/changes/<cat>`) it structurally cannot reach. Build the parent-scoped id-chain `remove_nested_item` (the dual of `add_nested_item`) + the CLI verb. Coherent with the declarative batch: the batch is the *migration authoring* path (a mis-author is fixed by re-running the corrected payload, no mid-batch retract needed), and `remove-item` is a **general standalone recovery/incremental-edit verb** justified independently.
- **(3) Write-time validation (#2) = move the id-from-enum check to write-time AND close the item-field value-validation parity gap.** Two unverified-reuse defects make this more than "un-exempt a check": the category enum is the **id-from**, which lives in the item *heading*, not `item.fields` — invisible to `check_value`; it needs a **new re-slug-membership helper at `add-item` time** (mirroring finalize's `check_id_from_enum`). And `check_value`'s enum arm compares **literally** (no re-slug), so naive reuse would *reject a value finalize accepts* — the write-time path must adopt the same re-slug discipline. `check_value` *is* fit for the item/nested-item field gap (the logged 2026-06-07 parity gap, `doc.rs:932`). Chosen per the milestone thesis: get the mechanism right on the reference before M25 copies it.
- **(4) In-location squatter (#8) = fix now** (not deferred to M25), despite being the highest-blast-radius fix and **not exercised by either acceptance corpus** (both are root/non-canonical `CHANGELOG.md`). Leaving it makes "changelog migration is a correct reference" incomplete. The fix: extend the same `source-path == promote-destination` discriminator the **retire** side already uses (`finalize.rs:249-285`) to the **create** side — seed the working area **blank** (skip the `state.rs:677` copy-in) iff this is a migration task whose recorded `source-path` canonically equals the committed singleton's canonical path. **The discriminator MUST be the migration source-path match, never singleton-ness** — else it resurrects the M16 clobber bug the copy-in exists to prevent. `state::create` already receives `task_dir` + `repo_root`, so `read_source_path` is reachable at the seam; gate it so the shared primitive is unchanged for non-migration callers. Carries a careful red-test for the clobber blast radius.

**Recommended-and-proceeded (no genuine fork; chosen by the orchestrator, human did not object):**
- **(#6) Date-on-migration = CLI migration-mode stamp-suppression, no schema edit.** `on_create_item_fields` (`doc.rs:415`) reads `read_source_path(&task.dir)` and suppresses the `set: on-create` today-stamp in migration mode (an explicit date in the payload still writes); the engine already treats an absent date as finalize-clean. Authoring=today / migration=omit-or-historical, with `changelog.yaml` untouched.
- **(#4) Migration commit doc = auto-provision a formulaic default** (`type: docs`, `scope: changelog`, a templated summary/body) rather than instruct the agent. The migration message is mechanical; this is the **first time the CLI fills slot content** (a recorded boundary precedent — defensible as "the commit message is just a doc type" over known facts: source path + doctype). Must fill `type`+`scope`+`summary`+`body` (all author-required).
- **(#5) Fidelity structural summary = a heuristic foreign version-scan, framed advisory display-only.** The canonical rewrite is reparseable for release ids; the foreign side is non-conformant (no schema), so "source releases absent from the rewrite: …" is computable only **fuzzily** — acceptable *here* because the review gate adjudicates nothing structurally (it is human-facing display), but explicitly **not a second structural authority** (Framing A intact).
- **(#9a) `git add --all` = bounded migration-only narrowing now** (stage only the `FinalizePlan` promote+retire paths for migration tasks); the general dirty-tree-sweep redesign (needs a task change-manifest) stays deferred ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):92).
- **(#9b) Migration task name = `migrate-<doctype>`** (the empty-intent mint at `start.rs:84-86` currently slugs the task id to the doctype name, colliding with `--task <doctype>` and serial-colliding on a re-run).
- **(#9c)** terse setup/ingest output — minor, fix in passing.
- **Byte-stability defer (the empty-slot+field-group instability, [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):69) stays deferred to M26**, confirmed **not fired** by M24: the declarative batch is parse-once/render-once (no inter-verb reparse), `remove_nested_item` only splices a block to empty (never renders a minted-empty slotted item), and changelog items are slot-only OR field-only — never both. Its natural trigger is M26's arch-doc slot+field components.

Docs corrected/elaborated in this Settle (baked before Review): [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) (squatter-seam correction; M24/M25 numbering; date claim; an M24-hardening section for #1–#9; agent-call-count + named-full-corpus in the measure), [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) (the form sugar promoted from "deferred" to the declarative `doc author` built spec; the `remove-item` verb; the write-time-validation claim at :116), [changelog.md](design/changelog.md) (the migration date posture), [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) (flow 25/26), [measurement.md](design/measurement.md) (the agent-call-count-for-migration note), [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) + [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) (M24→M25 sweep), [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) (graduations). Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 (decomposition below).

**Survived an independent pre-decompose design review (2026-06-16): 2 BLOCKING + 3 SHOULD + 4 CONSIDER, all baked before decompose** (the human confirmed both blocking dispositions). The reviewer verified every load-bearing claim against the binary; the spine (Framing A, retire/adopt transaction, date-suppression, the enum-on-id-from substrate) checked out, and both blocking findings were *placement/scoping* gaps the build would otherwise have resolved wrongly. **(B1) the batch's implementation path is pinned to the chain-the-existing-splice-primitives path** (create via `create_gated`, then `add-item`/`set-*` over one in-memory buffer, **no persist between leaves**, persist once) — *not* a parse-to-`Instance`/`render`-once path, which would bypass both the create-gate and the #8 squatter seam (both live in `state::create`) and has unproven byte-stability on a non-de-novo doc; the "parse-once/render-once" wording was corrected. **(B2) the #9a migration `git add` set must include jigc's own *tracked* config** (`.jigc/config/`, `.jigc/.gitignore`), not just {promote+retire}: that layer is git-tracked and `jigc setup` never commits, so a naive narrowing would strand the jigc setup uncommitted on the first migration commit (flow 26's "NOTHING else" line corrected). Baked SHOULDs: **(S1)** the `decisions-pending.md` squatter detail bullet's stale `write.wrong-shape` wording corrected to the `state.rs` copy-in seam; **(S2)** #4 narrowed — `type`/`scope` are *fields* (filled via the existing `default:`/`set: on-create` materialization, no boundary crossing), only `summary`/`body` are the genuine slot-fill, governed by a **bounded rule** (the CLI fills a slot only when its content is a pure deterministic function of structural facts, never judgment); **(S3)** the write-time and finalize enum checks call **one shared** slug+membership helper (not a mirrored copy that drifts when M25 generalizes it 4×) — same finding code, address-suffix may differ by call site. CONSIDERs: **(C1)** #8's create-side discriminator reuses the **same** path-normalization as the retire-side guard (share one routine); **(C4)** #5's heuristic scan feeds nothing structural and is labeled fuzzy (Framing-A guard stated); **(C2)** `remove_nested_item` as a general recovery verb is the human's explicit Settle choice (confirmed, not reopened); **(C3)** the `## Milestone 24` roadmap section is created at Decompose.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 decomposition: seven increments, risk-first + linear

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 into **seven ordered, single-concern increments**, each with an observable red, built against the M24-hardening design ([auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening; [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Batch authoring). **Risk-first + linear:** the headline net-new **declarative batch** (`jigc doc author --from`, Path A) first — fail-fast on the milestone's largest mechanism and the verbosity-at-scale answer the acceptance rides (Inc 1); then the two **doctype-general authoring lifts** the migration leans on — write-time validation via one shared enum helper + the item-field parity gap (Inc 2), then `remove-item` incl. the new nested `remove_nested_item` (Inc 3); then the **migration-mode behaviours** — mint-side date-suppression + `migrate-<doctype>` naming (Inc 4), the **isolated high-blast** in-location-squatter blank-seed (Inc 5, quarantined like M22's front-matter churn because it touches the load-bearing `state::create` copy-in / M16 clobber-fix), the finalize-path cluster commit-auto-provision + git-add narrowing + structural fidelity summary (Inc 6); and finally the **guidance + full measured live migration** that consumes all six — author-migration map+merge guidance + the FULL project-delta+project-gamma flow-26 e2e + the measured run incl. agent-call count (Inc 7, the done-bar). **No new schemas.** Byte-stability confirmed not-fired (the batch is the chain-of-splice-primitives path, `remove_nested_item` only splices-to-empty, and changelog has no slot+field-group item — re-keyed to M26). The binary changes (new `doc author` verb + write-time-validation lift + `remove_nested_item` + migration-mode discriminator + finalize-path lift), so **rebuild + re-pin** before exercise (Inc 7's prerequisite). Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 decomposition; [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 26.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 1 (`jigc doc author <doctype> --from <payload>` — declarative whole-doc batch authoring) into **four ordered, single-concern tasks**, each with an observable red, against [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Batch authoring (the B1 chain-the-splice-primitives pin) + [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #1. **CLI-only increment** — Path A reuses the existing `state::create_gated` + `engine::write` splice primitives, so no new engine primitive ships; the work is `crates/cli/src/doc.rs` + `cli.rs` + new integration tests. **No new schemas.** The payload format's concrete serialization is a build elaboration with pinned constraints (ordered leaf sequence; slot prose via `<<…>>`, scalar fields inline) — not a fork. Tasks:
- **T1 — payload format + parser:** parse `--from <payload>` into an ordered leaf-write plan (create id-source + ordered add-item / set-slot / set-field leaves); a structurally-malformed payload is rejected at parse, before anything persists. *Done:* unit tests — a multi-release changelog payload parses to the expected ordered plan; a malformed payload returns a parse error and persists nothing.
- **T2 — `doc author` verb + dispatch + chain-over-one-buffer apply (happy path):** wire `DocCommand::Author { doctype, from }`; create via `create_gated`, then chain each leaf's splice primitive over the running in-memory buffer with **no persist between leaves**, persist once. *Done:* a real-binary integration test (mirroring `changelog_cold_create`) authors a multi-release **dated** changelog from one payload that (a) round-trips byte-stable and (b) is **byte-identical to the equivalent per-leaf verb chain** — the load-bearing B1 claim, proven by test not assumed.
- **T3 — atomicity + create-gate enforcement through the batch:** any leaf error discards the buffer and removes the staged created doc (nothing persisted); the create-gate blocks an un-allowed doctype through the batch. *Done:* a payload with a bad mid-chain leaf → non-zero exit with the leaf's block finding and **no** staged doc; `doc author <disallowed-doctype>` → the `create.gate-blocked` finding (inherited from `create_gated`), nothing staged.
- **T4 — cold/empty spike + per-leaf regression watch:** a single-release payload and an empty (create-only) payload both behave; the existing per-leaf verbs stay byte-unchanged. *Done:* single-release + empty-payload integration tests pass; the pre-existing per-leaf verb tests (`doc_write`, `add_item_on_create`, `nested_add_item_on_create`, `changelog_cold_create`) pass unchanged after T2's shared-helper extraction.

**Why this order:** parse the payload before anything can persist (T1), prove the headline byte-identity on the happy path (T2), then harden the failure edges — atomicity + gate (T3) and cold/empty + regression (T4) — each building on the last over the shared working tree. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 1.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 1 T1: batch-payload serialization (build elaboration)

Pinned the concrete `jigc doc author --from <payload>` serialization (the "form-marker" open) per the [decomposition](#2026-06-16--m24-increment-1-planning-decomposition)'s pinned constraints. **YAML** (already workspace-wired). Shape: a required `title:` (the `create` id-source) + an ordered `sections:` list; each section carries doc-level `set:` leaves and/or repeatable `items:`; each item carries its own `title:` (item id-source), `set:` leaves, and nested `sections:` — mirroring the document, so the parser flattens it depth-first into the ordered leaf-write plan (`AuthorPlan { title, leaves: Vec<Leaf> }`, `Leaf` = `AddItem|SetField|SetSlot`, each carrying the `#…`-less **fragment** the existing `doc` resolvers already parse). **Slot/field split read off value syntax** (the pinned `<<slot>>`/scalar convention): a `set` value wrapped in `<<…>>` is slot prose (delimiters stripped → `SetSlot`), any other scalar is an inline `SetField`. Item-id chain hops are minted with the same `engine::slug::slugify` the engine `add_item` uses, so the fragment the parser builds for a nested leaf matches the id the engine mints by construction. `deny_unknown_fields` + required `title` make a malformed payload a parse-time whole reject (before any persist). Parser lives in a new `pub` lib module `crates/cli/src/author.rs` (the `invoke` precedent: a separately-testable item, wired into the binary dispatch by T2). **Scope:** T1 is parse-only; collision-suffixed duplicate item ids within one batch are out of scope (the changelog reference's versions/categories are unique) — surfaced at apply if hit. Cross-ref: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Batch authoring; [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #1.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 2 (write-time value validation: one shared id-from-enum helper + the item-field parity gap) into **three ordered, single-concern tasks**, each with an observable red, against [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Two check times + [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #3, on the settled M24 fork (3) + review S3. **No new schemas.** Grounded in the current code: finalize's `check_id_from_enum` (`validate.rs:900`) re-slugs the item heading and tests enum membership; the `add-item` write path (`add_item`/`add_nested_item`, `write.rs`) re-slugs the title but does **no** membership check; `set_item_field_or_insert`/`set_nested_item_field_or_insert` (`write.rs`) splice the value with **no** `check_value` (the docstring-pinned 2026-06-07 parity gap). The changelog's enum id-from lives in the **heading** of `unreleased-changes` + nested `changes` (`id-from: category`, an `enum`), so the id-from check re-slugs (NOT `check_value`'s literal compare, which would reject `Fixed`); the only malformed-able item **bullet** field is the release `date` (`set: on-create`, type `date`), so the parity gap is exercised by an explicit `set-field` on a release date. Three Grouped-scope bullets → three tasks:
- **T1 — shared slug+enum-membership helper + write-time id-from enum reject at `add-item`** (scope bullet 1). Extract **one** `slug + enum-membership` helper in `crates/engine/src/validate.rs` (it owns the re-slug discipline and the shared finding *code* `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant`); refactor finalize's `check_id_from_enum` to call it (one function, not a mirrored copy — review S3 / M25 drift), and wire it into the `add-item` write path for top-level (`unreleased-changes`) **and** nested (`changes`) so a re-slugged title ∉ the id-from enum blocks **at the verb**. *Done:* a real-binary integration test — `jigc doc add-item …#unreleased-changes --title "Improvements"` and the nested `…/changes --title "Improvements"` each **block at write** with code `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` naming the slug-cased id-from address; a valid member (`Fixed`→`fixed`) passes; the existing finalize enum tests (`validate.rs` → `top_level_foreign_category_blocks_at_the_slug_address`, `nested_foreign_category_blocks_at_the_nested_slug_address`) pass unchanged.
- **T2 — close the item-field parity gap: wire `check_value` into the item / nested-item set-field write path** (scope bullet 2). Resolve the declared field in the repeatable / nested-repeatable block and run the existing `engine::write::check_value` *before* touching bytes in `set_item_field_or_insert` + `set_nested_item_field_or_insert` (`write.rs`); drop the stale "does not adjudicate the value's type … deferred" docstring note. *Done:* an integration test — `jigc doc set-field <release>#releases/<v>/date <non-ISO>` **blocks at write** with `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` (the code finalize's item-field path emits); a valid ISO date passes and round-trips byte-stable; the per-leaf write tests (`doc_write`, `add_item_on_create`, `nested_add_item_on_create`, `item_authoring_acceptance`) pass unchanged.
- **T3 — batch inherits mid-batch rejection + cross-doctype regression watch** (scope bullet 3 + the increment-wide regression proof). Verify (not assume) the inc-1 declarative batch (`jigc doc author --from`, which chains the same primitives over one buffer) rejects a bad-category leaf mid-chain, persisting nothing; assert the other shipped doctypes' (`adr`, `commit`) conformance is unchanged. *Done:* extend `crates/cli/tests/doc_author.rs` — a payload with a non-member category leaf → non-zero exit carrying the `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` block and **no** staged doc; the adr/commit + per-leaf-verb regression suite (`superseding_decision`, `doc_write`, `changelog_cold_create`) stays green.

**Why this order:** establish the single shared helper + its two callers first (T1 — the whole increment's "one function, no drift" requirement), then the independent parity-gap wiring (T2), then verify the batch inheritance + regression watch that depends on T1's add-item check living in the chained primitives (T3) — serial, each over the shared working tree. **Distinct mechanisms by design:** the id-from check re-slugs the heading (T1's helper); the item-field check is `check_value`'s literal compare (T2) — they are NOT the same function and must not be conflated (M24 fork (3)). Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 2.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 2 T1: shared id-from-enum helper + add-item write-time reject (built)

The one shared adjudicator is `engine::validate::id_from_enum_violation(&Repeatable, title) -> Option<String>` plus the `pub const ID_FROM_ENUM_CODE` (= `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant`) — it owns the re-slug + enum-membership discipline AND the shared finding *code* (review S3; M25 copies it 4×, so it lives in one place). Finalize's `check_id_from_enum` was refactored to call it (dropping its `field` arg and the call-site `field.ty == Enum` gate, now owned by the helper — non-enum id-from returns `None`, staying exempt), so the two check times cannot drift. **Wiring site (planner left it open):** a **CLI pre-check** in `apply_add_item_target` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs`), not an engine validated wrapper — chosen because the add-item block must carry the *addressed* `schema-conformance.*` finding directly (the engine's `generate_error_finding` path emits unaddressed `write.*` codes), and because the CLI pre-check sits on the shared `apply_add_item_target`, so the batch (`apply_leaf`) inherits the reject for free (the T3 obligation). The destination repeatable is resolved the same way the mint path does — the section's own for top-level, the now-`pub` `engine::write::nested_repeatable` for nested — so there is no CLI copy of the navigation. The add-item address leaf-suffix (`{prefix}/{slug}/{id_from}`, e.g. `unreleased-changes/improvements/category`) differs from finalize's by call site; only the code is identical. Cross-ref: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Two check times; [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #3.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 2 T2: item-field value parity gap closed at the write verb (built)

`set_item_field_or_insert` / `set_nested_item_field_or_insert` (`crates/engine/src/write.rs`) now run the **existing** `engine::write::check_value` over the new value **before touching bytes** — closing the 2026-06-07 parity gap where item-field writes (unlike the header `set_field_validated` path) carried no value-type adjudication. The declared field is resolved by a new private `item_field_schema` helper that walks the repeatable nesting (top-level: the section's own repeatable; nested: descending one repeatable per nested-section segment, mirroring `physical_item_chain`'s item/nested-section alternation) and finds the `Leaf::Field` by id — an *unknown* item field stays unadjudicated (the engine invents no type). A malformed value surfaces as a new `GenerateError::MalformedValue { why }` variant, **mapped in `generate_error_finding` to the literal `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant`** — finalize's item-field code (the same literal `validate::check_field_value` emits), so the two check times' codes are byte-identical; the address leaf differs by call site (the engine emits an unaddressed `Location::at(1,1)`, which is why this — unlike T1's id-from — lives in the engine, not a CLI pre-check: the done-criterion needs only the code, not the address). The changelog release `date` is the one malformable item bullet field; the enum item-field path is the **same** `check_value` call (mechanism-general), so no separate enum fixture was added. Cross-ref: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Two check times; [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #3.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 3 (`jigc doc remove-item <addr>` — top-level + nested `remove_nested_item`, a general recovery verb) into **two ordered, single-concern tasks**, each with an observable red, against [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md); graduates the `remove-item` deferral ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → add-item family). **No new schemas.** Grounded in the current code: the existing `engine::write::remove_item` (`write.rs:984`) is **top-level-only** — it takes `(section_id, item_id)`, asserts the section is `Repeatable` + the item present, and splices `locate_item_block` to empty; it cannot reach a nested change-group (the smoke test's wrong-category case). The nested dual already has all its locator parts shipped: `add_nested_item` / `set_nested_item_slot` resolve a nested item via `nested_parsed_item` + `physical_item_chain` + the parent-scoped byte locator `locate_item_path`, which returns the item's own block span (heading → next same-or-shallower heading within the parent, or the parent's end). Address parsing (`address.rs`): a top-level `#section/item` is 2-hop → `Fragment::UnitLeaf`; a nested `#section/parent/.../item` is ≥4-hop → `Fragment::Deep` (the `#section/item/child/leaf`-class shape). The two Grouped-scope bullets → two tasks:
- **T1 — engine `remove_nested_item`** (scope bullet 1). Add `pub fn remove_nested_item(schema, source, section_id, item_ids: &[&str]) -> Result<String, SpliceError>` in `crates/engine/src/write.rs` — the dual of `add_nested_item`: re-parse for conformance, resolve the nested item via `nested_parsed_item` (assert present), locate its own byte block via `physical_item_chain` + `locate_item_path`, splice that span to empty (the span already carries the trailing inter-item separator, so surviving siblings stay canonically spaced — the byte-stability claim is T1's red, **not** assumed for the nested last-sibling edge). An absent / mis-named segment → `SpliceError::NotPresent` (no delete). *Done:* new engine unit tests over the `TWO_PARENT_TWO_LEVEL` changelog fixture — removing a nested change-group round-trips byte-stable (`render(parse(out)) == out`, surviving siblings byte-intact) for **both** a non-last and the last sibling; the removed group is the **intended** one (the same-anchor `#added` under the other release is byte-untouched); a mis-named nested item id → `SpliceError::NotPresent` with the source unchanged. `cargo test -p engine remove_nested` green; gate clean.
- **T2 — CLI `remove-item` verb + dispatch (top-level + nested)** (scope bullet 2). Add `DocCommand::RemoveItem { addr, task }` + dispatch → `run_remove_item` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `cli.rs`) and a `remove_item_target` resolver: a 2-hop `#section/item` (`Fragment::UnitLeaf`) → top-level removal via the existing `remove_item`; a `Fragment::Deep` `#section/.../item` → nested removal via T1's `remove_nested_item`, where the **whole** post-section hop chain is the item id chain (no trailing-leaf split — the verb-specific reading, vs `field_target`/`slot_target` which peel a trailing leaf); any other shape → no target. Read-or-copy-in the staged source, splice, persist once; an absent / mis-named target → a routed `DocFailure::Block` (clean block, nothing persisted). *Done:* a real-binary integration test on the shipped `changelog` doctype — removing a **top-level** release round-trips byte-stable, removing a **nested** change-group round-trips byte-stable, and a mis-named target exits non-zero with a routed block while the staged file is **byte-unchanged**. `cargo test -p cli` green; the per-leaf write tests (`doc_write`, `nested_item_addressing`) pass unchanged; gate clean.

**Why this order:** ship + prove the new engine primitive first (T1 — the load-bearing nested locator + byte-stability red), then wire the CLI verb that dispatches both the existing top-level `remove_item` and T1's nested dual and re-proves both end-to-end on the real changelog (T2) — serial, over the shared working tree. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 3.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 4 (migration-mode mint: dateless date-suppression + `migrate-<doctype>` task name) into **two ordered, single-concern tasks**, each with an observable red, against [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #6/#9 + [changelog.md](design/changelog.md) → date posture (line 30/79). **No schema change** (verified: a `set: on-create` field is not author-required — `validate.rs:21-23`: "author-required iff it carries neither a `default:` nor a `set:`" — so an absent release `date` finalizes clean). **No engine change** (verified: both fixes are CLI-side — the `mint_id` fallback is the mint site's concern, `state.rs:497-499`; the on-create date materializer call site is the CLI's, the engine stays clock-free). Grounded in the current code: the migration mode discriminator is the **presence of the `source-path` file** (`engine::state::read_source_path(task_dir)` → `Some` iff minted by `jigc migrate`, which is the only writer of `state::SOURCE_PATH_FILE`; `jigc start`/`mint_in_repo` never writes it — distinct from inc-5's path-*normalization* squatter discriminator, which is a separate concern). The on-create date stamp is materialized at the **shared** `apply_add_item_target` seam (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs:391`/`409`, via `on_create_item_fields`/`on_create_nested_item_fields`), reached by both the per-leaf `run_add_item` and the batch `apply_leaf`/`run_author` — so suppressing there covers verb + batch (the same shared-seam property M24 inc-2 T1's id-from reject relied on). The migration mint is `mint_migration_in_repo` (`crates/cli/src/start.rs:77`), which passes `intent=""` + `type_name=<doctype>` to `state::mint_task`, so `mint_id` falls back to `slugify(<doctype>)` = the bare doctype id (e.g. `changelog`) today. The two Grouped-scope bullets → two tasks:
- **T1 — name the migration task `migrate-<doctype>`** (scope bullet 2: task naming). In `mint_migration_in_repo` (`start.rs`), keep `intent=""` (the migration task carries no real authoring intent) but pass `migrate-<doctype>` as the `mint_id` fallback source (the `type_name` arg of `state::mint_task`), so the off-router migration task mints at `migrate-<doctype>` — decoupling its serial namespace from the bare doctype id / a `--task <doctype>` resume. **Blast radius (own-change orphans):** the migrate integration suite resumes the migration task via `--task changelog` / `const TASK = "changelog"` (`flow25_migrate_changelog.rs`, `flow25_marquee.rs`, `migrate_seam.rs`, `migrate_workflow.rs`, `migrate_review_gate.rs`, `migrate_rollback.rs`, `migrate_retire_adopt.rs`, `migrate_retire_safety.rs`); update each to `migrate-changelog`. *Done:* a real-binary integration test asserts `jigc migrate CHANGELOG.md --as changelog` mints task id `migrate-changelog` (its working area at `.jigc/tasks/migrate-changelog/`), and the bare doctype namespace `changelog` stays free — an independent task minted at `changelog` does not serial-collide with the migration; the renamed migrate_* suite (resume id → `migrate-changelog`) passes. `cargo test -p cli` green; gate clean.
- **T2 — suppress the `set: on-create` date stamp in migration mode** (scope bullet 1: the migration-mode discriminator). Thread a migration flag — `engine::state::read_source_path(&task.dir)?.is_some()`, computed once in `run_add_item` + `run_author` — into the shared `apply_add_item_target` (and `apply_leaf`) so that in migration mode the on-create date fields are **not** materialized at mint (pass empty for both the top-level and nested branches; authoring keeps stamping `today_iso`). An explicit `set-field <release>/date` is unaffected (it is a separate leaf, not the implicit stamp). *Done:* a real-binary integration test on the shipped `changelog` driven through `migrate-changelog`: a **dateless** release `add-item`'d in migration mode renders **no `date:` line** and **finalizes clean** (no `required-field-present` block — the red proves the no-schema-change claim on the new shape, not assumed); an **authoring** `record-change` (`jigc start`, non-migration) release `add-item` still stamps **today**; an **explicit** `set-field <release>/date <ISO>` in migration mode still writes the date. The existing on-create + migration suites (`add_item_on_create`, `nested_add_item_on_create`, `flow24_changelog`, `flow25_migrate_changelog` — whose historical-date `set-field` still overwrites/writes) pass unchanged. `cargo test -p cli` green; gate clean.

**Why this order:** T1 (naming) first — it establishes the final `migrate-changelog` resume id across the shared migrate test surface, so T2's date-suppression test drives that id with no rework; the two are orthogonal CLI-side mechanisms built serially over the shared working tree. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 4.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 5 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 5 (in-location squatter: seed the working area blank over an occupied canonical path) into **three ordered, single-concern tasks**, each with an observable red, against [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Path-collision guard / Hardening #8 + review C1; [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) (B1 create-gate, C1). **Isolated, engine-scoped** (`crates/engine/src/state.rs` `create` step 4 — the load-bearing M16 clobber-fix copy-in), so the careful red lands alone. Grounded facts the cut rests on (verified against HEAD, not assumed): the copy-in branch (`state.rs:677-686`) is gated `schema.singleton && store::canonical_path(repo_root,schema,slug).is_file()`, reads the committed body in via `copy_in` recording `Provenance::EditedFromBase`, while the blank-seed path `provision_doc` (`state.rs:277-290`) records `Provenance::Created` — so seed-blank-vs-copy-in is directly observable at the staged body + provenance. `create`/`create_gated` already take `task_dir` (`state.rs:641`/`711`) and `read_source_path(task_dir)` (`state.rs:477`) is engine-local — so the migration discriminator reads inside `create` with **no signature change** (auto-migration.md line 64: "state.rs step 4 reads `read_source_path(task_dir)`"). The retire-side guard `plan_retirements` (`finalize.rs:258`) already compares `lexical_normalize(source_path)` against `lexical_normalize(promotion.destination)`, where `destination = format!("{}/{slug}.md", location.trim_end_matches('/'))` (`finalize.rs:269-272,527`); `lexical_normalize` is **finalize-private** (`finalize.rs:290`). Both `state.rs` and `finalize.rs` already `use crate::store`, which owns path identity (`canonical_path`, `store.rs:43`) — the natural shared home. The discriminator is the **migration source-path == canonical-destination match, never singleton-ness** (else it resurrects the M16 clobber-fix copy-in exists for) — and is **distinct from inc-4's source-path-*presence* discriminator** (inc-4 suppresses the date for any migration task; inc-5 seeds blank only when the source *is* the canonical squatter). `changelog` is `singleton: true`, location `changelog/` → canonical `changelog/changelog.md` (`pack/schemas/changelog.yaml:27-29`); migrate.rs records a clean repo-relative source-path (`migrate.rs:73`, tested `migrate.rs:164`). The two Grouped-scope bullets → three tasks (bullet 2 is the prerequisite shared routine; bullet 1 is the engine fix; T3 is the binary-level acceptance that "the M23 e2e FAIL now passes"):

- **T1 — lift `lexical_normalize` to a shared engine home; route the retire-side guard through it** (scope bullet 2: one path-normalization routine across both seams). Move the finalize-private `fn lexical_normalize` (`finalize.rs:290`) to `pub fn lexical_normalize` in `crates/engine/src/store.rs` (the path-identity home, already imported by both seams) and update `plan_retirements` (`finalize.rs:269-272`) to call `crate::store::lexical_normalize` — **no behavior change** on the retire side. *Done:* a new `store` unit test asserts the routine collapses `.`/`..` (`./changelog/changelog.md` → `changelog/changelog.md`; `changelog/../changelog/changelog.md` → `changelog/changelog.md`); the existing finalize retire-guard tests (the F2 `./`-spelled + redundant-component squatter-skip cases, `finalize.rs:~1049-1110`) and the cli `migrate_retire_safety.rs` F2 cases pass **unchanged**. `cargo test -p engine` + `-p cli` green; `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` + `fmt --check` clean.
- **T2 — create-side seed-blank: extend the source-path==canonical discriminator to `state::create` step 4** (scope bullet 1, the load-bearing change). At `state.rs:677`, before the copy-in branch, read `read_source_path(task_dir)`; when it is `Some` non-empty **and** `store::lexical_normalize(source_path) == store::lexical_normalize(format!("{}/{slug}.md", location.trim_end_matches('/')))` (the same repo-relative form + the T1 shared routine the retire side uses), **skip copy-in and fall through to `provision_doc`** (seed blank). Otherwise the copy-in branch runs unchanged. *Done:* new `state.rs` unit tests — (a) **seed-blank**: a migration task whose recorded `source-path` equals the committed singleton's canonical path stages the **empty template** (NOT the committed squatter body) with provenance `Created`; (b) **M16 regression intact**: `singleton_create_warm_copies_committed_body_in_no_clobber` (non-migration, no source-path) still copies-in (`EditedFromBase`), **and** a migration whose source-path is the **non-canonical** root `CHANGELOG.md` while a committed `changelog/changelog.md` exists **still copies-in** (proving the discriminator is the path-match, not migration-ness); (c) **agreement**: a `./`-prefixed / redundant-component spelling of the canonical source-path is still recognized as the squatter (seeds blank) — the create-side and retire-side recognize the same squatter via the same shared routine. `cargo test -p engine` green; gate clean.
- **T3 — binary acceptance: the in-location squatter seeds blank, authors, finalizes byte-stable** (the increment's "Proves": the M23 e2e FAIL now passes). A new `crates/cli/tests` integration case over the built binary + dev pack (the `migrate_retire_safety.rs` harness shape — `run_jigc`/`init_repo`/`FOREIGN`): write a non-conformant `changelog/changelog.md` squatter → `setup` → `jigc migrate changelog/changelog.md --as changelog` → assert the **staged** `.jigc/tasks/migrate-changelog/docs/changelog:changelog.md` is the seeded **empty template**, NOT the FOREIGN squatter bytes (the precise M23 failure point — copy-in read FOREIGN in as the edit base) → author a conformant changelog via the write verbs → `finalize --approve` → the canonical `changelog/changelog.md` holds the **authored** doc (byte-stable, no Frankenstein), retire is **skipped** (rewritten in place, file present + conformant), finalize exits clean. *Done:* the integration test passes; `cargo test -p cli` green; gate clean.

**Why this order:** T1 first establishes the single normalization routine both seams will share (the retire side keeps its behavior, proving the lift is faithful), so T2's create-side guard reuses it **by construction** — the "agree on the same normalization" guarantee is structural, not coincidental; T2 is the engine fix where seed-blank is directly observable (staged body + provenance) with the M16 regression guarded in isolation; T3 closes the increment at the binary level, proving the squatter now authors end-to-end (the full measured real-repo flow-26 run stays inc-7's marquee, rebuild + re-pin there). Serial over the shared working tree. No new fork surfaced — every bullet maps to settled M24 decisions (2026-06-16) and the locked [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Path-collision guard / Hardening #8 + C1. ## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 6, T1 landed: migration commit auto-provision template

The auto-provisioned migration commit's **emitted-artifact contract** (the bounded slot-fill rule, S2 — pure deterministic function of source path + doctype): subject template `docs(<doctype>): adopt <source-path> as a managed <doctype>` (e.g. `docs(changelog): adopt CHANGELOG.md as a managed changelog`) + body `Migrate the foreign <source-path> into the managed <doctype> document and retire the original.` `type=docs`/`scope=<doctype>` filled as **field** values, `summary`/`body` as **slot** prose, at mint in `start::mint_migration_in_repo` (now fed `source_path` from `migrate.rs`) via `provision_migration_commit_doc`/`migration_commit_form` (`crates/cli/src/start.rs`). The empty fillable form stays the non-migration path (`provision_commit_doc`); the two share `load_commit_schema`/`persist_provisioned_commit`. Asserted on the **landed** commit subject (`git log -1 --format=%s`) in `crates/cli/tests/migration_commit_autoprovision.rs`.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 6, T2 landed: narrowed migration finalize git add

The migration finalize now stages **only** its own paths via `stage_migration` (`crates/cli/src/task.rs`) instead of the blanket `git add --all`, gated by an `is_migration` flag (`source_seam.exists()`) threaded into `try_execute_finalize_plan` — the two milestone call sites + the `execute_finalize_plan` wrapper pass `false` (unchanged sweep). **Elaboration (not a fork):** a retired original is `git add`ed to stage its deletion only when it was **tracked at HEAD** (`path_at_head`); an untracked-then-deleted foreign needs no staging and a `git add` pathspec matching nothing is a fatal error (`git add --all` tolerated it), so the filter keeps the dateless/untracked-original flows green. One `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on the shared executor (8/7) — each arg is a real, independent input, clearer than a parameter struct. Set landed: promotions + tracked retirements (as deletions) + `.jigc/config` + `.jigc/.gitignore`; arbitrary user WIP excluded. Test: `crates/cli/tests/migration_finalize_git_add.rs`.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 7 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 7 (the marquee: category map+merge guidance + the full project-delta+project-gamma live migration, measured) into **four ordered, single-concern tasks**, each with an observable red, against [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 26 + [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #7/#9c, Migration-quality measure + [measurement.md](design/measurement.md) posture. **No new schemas** (the whole increment is guidance + output polish + binary-proving tests + a recorded measured run — zero engine/schema change). Grounded in HEAD (verified, not assumed): the `doc author --from` batch (inc 1), write-time enum/value reject (inc 2), `remove-item`/`remove_nested_item` (inc 3), dateless date-suppression + `migrate-changelog` naming (inc 4), the in-location-squatter blank-seed (inc 5), and the commit auto-provision + narrowed git-add + structural fidelity summary (inc 6) **all shipped** — inc 7 is the consume-everything done-bar. The three Grouped-scope bullets → four tasks (bullet 3 splits into the binary-proving e2e test and the rebuild+re-pin+measured-run recording, per the M23 precedent where the measured migration-quality baseline is an owner-artifact recording — agent-judged, "its done-criterion is the committed artifact" — distinct from the binary-proving flow test, [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-06-15 M23 Increment 4 T2):

- **T1 — rewrite `crates/cli/pack/steps/author-migration.yaml` guidance: map+merge onto the enum, infer-from-prefix when headingless, drive the `jigc doc author --from` batch** (scope bullet 1). Replace the per-leaf `add-item`/`set-slot`/`set-field` walk with batch-payload guidance: author the WHOLE changelog as one declarative `jigc doc author changelog --from -` YAML payload (inc-1 verb, the verbosity-at-scale answer flow 26 rides); map each foreign category heading onto exactly one of the six `category` enum members **and merge many-to-one** (two foreign categories → one member, because the enum is the id-from and two groups cannot share an id — `auto-migration.md` #7); when a foreign file carries NO category headings, **infer** the member from each change's `feat:`/`fix:` prefix; preserve the dateless-omit + historical-date-when-present + optional-`link` clauses. **Own-change blast radius:** `crates/cli/tests/migrate_workflow.rs` (`migrate_composes_the_shipped_workflow_with_seam_and_author_spine`) asserts the OLD per-leaf directives (`jigc doc create changelog`, `jigc doc add-item changelog:changelog#releases`, `set-slot`, `set-field`+`/date`) in the composed output — those assertions must be updated to the batch shape (the executor confirms which per-leaf strings survive vs. move into the payload). *Done:* the updated `migrate_workflow.rs` compose test passes asserting the composed `migrate-changelog` workflow surfaces (a) the `jigc doc author changelog --from` batch directive, (b) the map-onto-the-six-members-AND-merge-many-to-one instruction, and (c) the infer-from-`feat:`/`fix:`-prefix-when-headingless instruction; the foreign source seam still resolves; `cargo test -p cli` green; gate clean. design_refs: auto-migration #7; worked-examples flow 26.
- **T2 — less-terse `setup`/`ingest` output** (scope bullet 2, #9c). Add explanatory context to the `setup` success summary and the `ingest` triage report renderers (`render::setup_success` / `render::ingest`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`) — e.g. ingest's `Unmanaged`/`adoptable` rows and footer state *why* a row classified that way and the next action; setup names what was installed — without changing the structured (JSON) shape. **Own-change blast radius:** the renderer unit tests asserting exact output (`render.rs` → `render_ingest_lists_rows_with_routed_finding_and_footer`, the setup-success/orientation-unset tests) + any `crates/cli/tests/ingest.rs` string assertions must be updated. *Done:* the updated renderer + integration assertions pass over the less-terse output; the JSON renderer's keys are unchanged (regression watch); `cargo test -p cli` green; gate clean. design_refs: auto-migration #9c.
- **T3 — the real-binary flow-26 e2e (happy path via the batch + the hardening reds)** (scope bullet 3, the binary-proving half). New `crates/cli/tests/flow26_*.rs` (the `flow25_marquee.rs` harness shape — `run_jigc`/`init_repo`/`dev_pack`/`TempDir`) over a **representative multi-release dateless** foreign changelog (incl. a foreign-category-merge case and a headingless `feat:`/`fix:` case): `setup` → `migrate CHANGELOG.md --as changelog` → `jigc doc author changelog --from -` (ONE batch payload) → `finalize` (review gate, no `--approve`) → `finalize --approve` → `ingest`. *Done:* one integration test (or a small file of tests) asserts — **happy:** the whole doc authored from one payload round-trips byte-stable, dateless releases render **no date line**, the commit is auto-provisioned (formulaic `docs(changelog): …` subject, no manual commit authoring), and the landed commit holds only the migration set {promote + retire + `.jigc/config/` + `.jigc/.gitignore`} with no unrelated WIP; **the hardening reds** each fire — write-time enum block at `add-item` (`schema-conformance.field-value-conformant`), `remove-item` retracts a nested change-group byte-stable, the in-location squatter (`changelog/changelog.md`) seeds blank + authors end-to-end, the review gate (no `--approve`) shows the structural release-delta summary. `cargo test -p cli` green; gate clean. design_refs: worked-examples flow 26; auto-migration Hardening #1–#9.
- **T4 — rebuild + re-pin the binary, then the FULL project-delta + project-gamma measured live migration, recorded** (scope bullet 3, the measured-run half + the rebuild/re-pin prerequisite). Rebuild `jigc` (`cargo build --release`) and re-pin it to PATH (record the sha — the M23 T2 precedent), then run the **full** live migration of throwaway clones of `~/Projects/project-delta` (≈12 releases, 127 lines, dateless, heading-categorised) and `~/Projects/project-gamma` (≈50 releases, 607 lines, dateless, `feat:`/`fix:` prefixes), each authored through **one `jigc doc author --from` batch payload**, end-to-end (`migrate → doc author → finalize --approve → ingest`). *Done:* both full migrations complete with every `finalize --approve` exiting 0 and `jigc ingest` reporting the canonical `changelog/changelog.md` adopted (round-trip conformant); the committed owner-artifact under `completions/artifacts/M24/` records the **four facts** for both repos — round-trip conformance (CLI-reported), fidelity-acceptance (agent-judged at the review gate), content-preservation (within the accepted-drops bound), and **agent-call count** (the batch's one-payload cut vs. the per-leaf round-trip count, the headline verbosity signal) — per the [measurement.md](design/measurement.md) recorded-alongside posture (not engine-emitted). design_refs: auto-migration Migration-quality measure; measurement.md posture; worked-examples flow 26.

**Why this order:** the guidance rewrite first (T1) — the e2e and the measured run both author through it, so it must be correct before anything exercises it; the independent `setup`/`ingest` output polish next (T2, orthogonal CLI-render change); then the consolidated binary-proving e2e (T3) that proves the happy path + the hardening behaviours through the real binary; finally the rebuild+re-pin + full measured live run over the two real repos (T4) — the done-bar that consumes every prior increment and the freshly-built binary. Serial over the shared working tree. All three Grouped-scope bullets map (bullet 1 → T1, bullet 2 → T2, bullet 3 → T3 binary-proof + T4 measured recording); none dropped, no creep beyond the increment. No new fork surfaced — every bullet maps to settled M24 decisions (2026-06-16) and the locked [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Hardening #7/#9c + Migration-quality measure + [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 26. Cross-ref: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 24 Increment 7.

## 2026-06-16 — M24 Increment 7 T4 complete: the FULL project-delta + project-gamma measured live migration (the done-bar)

Rebuilt + re-pinned `jigc` to HEAD (`3ddad94`, `cargo build --release`, sha256 `25fa3cd1…`) into both `~/.local/bin` and `~/.cargo/bin`, then ran the **full** live migration of throwaway detached clones of `~/Projects/project-delta` (127 lines → **13** releases / 20 change-groups) and `~/Projects/project-gamma` (607 lines → **80** releases / 127 change-groups), each authored through **ONE** `jigc doc author changelog --from` batch payload (Framing A; `build-payload.py` is the agent's mapping tool — it places nothing). **Result: 2/2 round-trip-conformant** (finalize `--approve` exit 0, `ingest` adopted + idempotent, byte-stable `render(parse(x))==x` verified incl. project-gamma's nested-sub-bullet slots), **2/2 fidelity-accepted** (map+merge many-to-one onto the `category` enum + infer-from-`feat:`/`fix:`-prefix + verb-inference on plain bullets), **content preserved 53/53 + 433/433 foreign bullets verbatim** (only the empty `# new` placeholder dropped — accepted bound), and **agent-call count cut 54× / 335× → 1×** via the batch. Dateless: 0 `date:` lines in either canonical (no fabricated history, #6); the review gate blocked (exit 4) then approved; one commit per repo (auto-provisioned `docs(changelog): adopt CHANGELOG.md as a managed changelog`, retire+promote collapsed to a rename, no unrelated WIP). The structural release-delta summary (#5) behaved as the labeled fuzzy/advisory aid — it reported body-text version tokens (Laravel `9.0`; project-gamma core/WordPress/PHP versions) as "absent", none a real release, feeding no gate — concrete evidence the fuzzy label is warranted. Owner-artifact recording per the [measurement.md](design/measurement.md) posture (not a TDD test; done-criterion = the committed artifact); the batch path is binary-proven by T3's `flow26_marquee.rs`. Artifact: `completions/artifacts/M24/migration-quality-measure.md` (+ `evidence/`: `build-payload.py`, `drive.sh`, `*.payload.yaml`, `*.counts`, `*.log`, `*.canonical.md`). The M24 done-bar is met.
